elements.stimulus: Apply nReset low and release it, keep ena high, set clk_cnt=0, hold scl_i and sda_i high, then drive cmd=START (4'b0001) while idle and continue clocking until command completion.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: the module acts as the bit-level I2C controller by executing the START sequence: it releases SCL and SDA, pulls SDA low while SCL is high, then pulls SCL low and produces a one-clock cmd_ack pulse.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate monitor to sample scl_oen, sda_oen, cmd_ack, and idle after each posedge; compare the observed output-enable sequence and one-cycle acknowledgement against the START transaction reference model.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset low and release it, keep ena high, set clk_cnt=0, hold scl_i and sda_i high, remain idle, then drive an unsupported cmd value such as 4'b0011 for multiple enabled clocks.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: without a recognized bit-level controller command, no I2C transaction is initiated; the module remains idle, both SCL and SDA remain released, and cmd_ack stays low.
elements.check_method: Monitor idle, scl_oen, sda_oen, and cmd_ack on every posedge for the entire stimulus window; assert that no command-sequence state or output-enable transition occurs and that no acknowledgement pulse is observed.

elements.stimulus: After reset, hold ena=1, clk_cnt=16'h0000, and both external bus lines released high. Present cmd=4'b0001 (START) through an enabled timing tick, then keep cmd stable until completion.
elements.expected_response: Holding case for scl_oen and sda_oen: the controller accepts START, initially releases SCL and SDA, drives SDA low while SCL remains released high, then drives SCL low; the command terminates with a one-clock cmd_ack pulse.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model to compare the sampled scl_oen and sda_oen waveform and phase ordering from command acceptance through cmd_ack, allowing the registered one-cycle output latency.

elements.stimulus: Generate a completed START first, then with ena=1 and clk_cnt=16'h0000 present cmd=4'b0010 (STOP) on an enabled timing tick while the bus is otherwise released high.
elements.expected_response: Holding case for scl_oen and sda_oen: the controller drives SDA low, releases SCL and waits for filtered SCL high, then releases SDA while SCL is high to form STOP; the command terminates with a one-clock cmd_ack pulse.
elements.check_method: Compare registered scl_oen and sda_oen samples against a STOP-sequence reference model, checking that SDA release occurs only after SCL is released/high and before cmd_ack.

elements.stimulus: After reset, hold ena=1 and clk_cnt=16'h0000, keep SCL high, and issue cmd=4'b1000 (READ) on an enabled timing tick. Provide stable external SDA values of 0 and then repeat the test with SDA=1; allow each command to complete.
elements.expected_response: Holding case for scl_oen and sda_oen: the controller releases SDA for the slave, releases SCL for the read window, then drives SCL low again and completes with cmd_ack; SDA remains released throughout the read-bit data phase.
elements.check_method: Compare the output-enable waveform to the READ reference model and verify the SDA output enable is released before SCL release, remains released during the sample window, and the sequence ends only after the low phase and cmd_ack.

elements.stimulus: After reset, hold ena=1 and clk_cnt=16'h0000 and issue cmd=4'b0100 (WRITE) on an enabled timing tick. Run once with din=0 and once with din=1, with the external bus released and no arbitration loss.
elements.expected_response: Holding case for scl_oen and sda_oen: the controller drives SDA low for din=0 or releases SDA for din=1, releases SCL for the high phase, then drives SCL low and completes with cmd_ack.
elements.check_method: Use separate reference-model waveforms for din=0 and din=1; compare registered scl_oen and sda_oen at every clock, checking SDA polarity and the required SCL release/high then driven-low phase ordering.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep ena=1, clk_cnt=16'h0000, and the filtered bus idle/released high. While the FSM is idle, present cmd=4'b0000 (NOP) and each unsupported encoding 4'b0011, 4'b0101, 4'b0110, 4'b0111, 4'b1001, 4'b1010, 4'b1011, 4'b1100, 4'b1101, 4'b1110, and 4'b1111 for an enabled timing tick.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case for scl_oen and sda_oen: because no supported command-specific sequence is requested, scl_oen and sda_oen remain at their idle released levels; no command phase occurs and cmd_ack remains low.
elements.check_method: For every unsupported command, assert that the output-enable traces contain no START, STOP, READ, or WRITE phase transitions and compare against the idle reference model; separately check cmd_ack is never asserted.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt to a small nonzero value, present cmd=START, and hold scl_i and sda_i released high so the command is accepted on a clk_en tick.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: scl_oen and sda_oen produce a START waveform by releasing both lines, pulling SDA low while SCL is high, then pulling SCL low; cmd_ack pulses for exactly one clock at completion.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate scoreboard to compare the registered output-enable sequence and one-cycle cmd_ack pulse against the START reference waveform.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and repeatedly apply cmd=0000 and each unsupported 4-bit command value other than 0001, 0010, 0100, and 1000, with the bus released high.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: no supported command behavior occurs; scl_oen and sda_oen remain in the idle released state and cmd_ack remains low.
elements.check_method: Assert that no command waveform is observed and that cmd_ack is never high during or after each unsupported-command trial.

elements.stimulus: With ena=1 and a normal released-high bus, issue cmd=STOP after first making the bus busy through a filtered START condition.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: the controller drives SDA low, releases SCL and waits for filtered SCL high, releases SDA while SCL is high, and produces one cmd_ack pulse at the terminal phase.
elements.check_method: Compare scl_oen and sda_oen at every enabled timing tick with the STOP reference model and verify exactly one completion pulse.

elements.stimulus: With ena=1 and the bus released high, apply cmd=WRITE with din=0, then repeat with din=1; allow the external bus to match the driven or released SDA value.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: each command produces a single-bit WRITE waveform, drives SDA low for din=0 or releases SDA for din=1, releases SCL for the high phase, pulls SCL low, and emits one cmd_ack without asserting al.
elements.check_method: Use an open-drain bus model and scoreboard the SDA/SCL enable phases, command acknowledgement count, and arbitration status.

elements.stimulus: With ena=1 and the bus released high, apply cmd=READ; during the released SCL-high sample window drive sda_i first low and then high in separate trials.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: sda_oen remains released for the read bit, scl_oen releases SCL for the sample window and then drives it low, dout reports the synchronized filtered input bit at the filtered SCL rising edge, and cmd_ack pulses once.
elements.check_method: Drive the external open-drain bus, predict filtered SCL/SDA edges with a reference model, and compare dout capture timing, value, output enables, and cmd_ack.

elements.stimulus: Apply cmd=READ with ena=1, but hold the command incomplete by preventing a valid filtered SCL rising sample edge and then abort the attempt with reset before the terminal phase.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: no completed READ-cycle result is reported; dout does not update from a read sample and cmd_ack remains low for the aborted cycle.
elements.check_method: Monitor filtered SCL rising-edge events, dout changes, and cmd_ack; assert that no read result or completion pulse occurs before reset.

elements.stimulus: After a filtered START has made the bus busy, apply a stable filtered STOP transition by driving SDA from low to high while filtered SCL is high.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: busy clears after the synchronized and filtered STOP detection.
elements.check_method: Model the synchronizer, filter majority, and delayed filtered values, then compare busy with the model on the detected STOP event.

elements.stimulus: While busy is asserted, inject SDA and SCL raw glitches shorter than the synchronization and filter sampling interval, without producing a majority-filtered START or STOP transition.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: busy does not change because the unsynchronized, glitch-filtered-out transitions are not treated as bus START or STOP conditions.
elements.check_method: Check that the reference filtered signals and sta_condition/sto_condition remain inactive and that busy retains its prior value.

elements.stimulus: Issue cmd=WRITE with din=1, ena=1, and during the released SCL-high arbitration-check phase force the external SDA line low.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: al asserts, the active WRITE aborts without cmd_ack, and both scl_oen and sda_oen are released.
elements.check_method: Use the open-drain bus model to force SDA low, then assert sticky al, absence of cmd_ack, return to idle, and released output enables.

elements.stimulus: Issue cmd=WRITE with din=0 and hold SDA low during the released SCL-high phase; separately complete a normal WRITE with din=1 while external SDA remains high.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: a condition that does not constitute arbitration loss does not assert al; the din=0 WRITE completes despite SDA low, and the normal din=1 WRITE completes without al.
elements.check_method: Check al before and after each trial, verify cmd_ack only for the completed writes, and compare arbitration decisions with the din-dependent reference model.

elements.stimulus: Issue a START, STOP, WRITE, and READ with ena=1 while externally holding filtered SCL low after the DUT releases SCL high; then release SCL high and allow each command to continue.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: slave clock stretching delays the high-phase FSM transition and command completion; no command phase advances or cmd_ack occurs until filtered SCL becomes high, after which the proper waveform completes.
elements.check_method: Monitor slave_wait, clk_en, output-enable phases, and cmd_ack against a variable-latency timing model that pauses the counter during stretching.

elements.stimulus: During a command with SCL released high, externally create a filtered SCL falling edge before the controller's expected high-period timing completes, representing another master controlling the shared clock.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: multi-master synchronization is applied; the timing counter reloads and local low-period timing restarts, preventing the FSM from using an unsynchronized local phase and preserving correct subsequent command ordering.
elements.check_method: Compare scl_sync, counter reload/expiration, clk_en timing, and subsequent scl_oen transitions with a reference synchronization model.

elements.stimulus: Toggle raw scl_i and sda_i asynchronously around clk edges, then apply stable levels for enough enabled clocks to pass through the two-stage synchronizers and three-sample filters.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: bus behavior and READ sampling use the synchronized and glitch-filtered values rather than raw inputs; stable transitions eventually affect filtered signals and filtered SCL rising edges only after the modeled synchronization/filter latency.
elements.check_method: Compare cscl/csda, filter sampling events, majority-filter outputs, filtered edge events, and dout against a cycle-accurate synchronizer/filter reference model.

elements.stimulus: During an active START, STOP, WRITE, or READ command, force a short raw-line transition that does not persist through synchronization and majority filtering, and do not otherwise create arbitration loss.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: the filtered bus remains unchanged, no false START/STOP or arbitration-loss status is generated, the command waveform is not aborted, and the command may complete with its normal cmd_ack.
elements.check_method: Assert no sta_condition, sto_condition, or arbitration-loss event is produced by the glitch, while the command scoreboard observes the normal completion behavior.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep ena high and model external pull-ups on SCL and SDA. Issue a START command with cmd=0001, then allow the sequence to advance through the phase that pulls SDA low and the subsequent phase that pulls SCL low.
elements.expected_response: Holding case for the observed behavior: scl_o and sda_o remain 0 throughout. During the SDA-drive phase sda_oen is 0 and the resolved SDA line is low; during the SCL-drive phase scl_oen is 0 and the resolved SCL line is low. The output enables therefore use active-low drive control.
elements.check_method: At every settled posedge during the START sequence, assert scl_o==0 and sda_o==0. In the drive phases, compare scl_oen and sda_oen against the reference FSM phase and verify that each corresponding externally pulled-up line resolves low only when its enable is 0.

elements.stimulus: Complete a START, then issue a STOP command with cmd=0010 while ena is high. Provide external pull-ups and allow the STOP sequence to enter its SCL-release phase followed by its SDA-release phase.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting release case for the observed behavior: scl_o and sda_o remain 0, while scl_oen is 1 when SCL is released and sda_oen is 1 when SDA is released. With no external low drive, the corresponding resolved lines are high, demonstrating the distinction between enable=0 drive-low and enable=1 release.
elements.check_method: Use phase-qualified assertions on the registered outputs after each posedge: require scl_o==0 and sda_o==0 unconditionally, require scl_oen==1 in the STOP SCL-release phase, and require sda_oen==1 in the final SDA-release phase; verify both resolved bus lines rise through the modeled pull-ups.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low between clock edges, deassert it, then keep rst low, ena high, clk_cnt=0, cmd=NOP, and an externally released-high SCL/SDA bus for at least four rising edges.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of shows: scl_o and sda_o remain constant 0 on every sampled clock. In the reset/idle released-line state, scl_oen=1 and sda_oen=1; each 1 acts as an active-low output-enable release, so the corresponding open-drain line remains externally high.
elements.check_method: At each rising edge after asynchronous reset settles, compare scl_o and sda_o against 0 and compare scl_oen/sda_oen against 1; additionally sample the resolved SCL and SDA lines and verify both are high when no external device drives them low.

elements.stimulus: With nReset deasserted, ena high, clk_cnt=0, and both external bus lines released high, issue cmd=START for one enabled clock and then return cmd=NOP; run until the START sequence reaches its SDA-low-while-SCL-high phase and then its SCL-low phase.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting control case of shows: scl_o and sda_o remain constant 0 throughout the START sequence. During the START low-drive phase, sda_oen=0 enables low SDA drive while scl_oen=1 releases SCL; in the following SCL-low phase, scl_oen=0 enables low SCL drive. A 0 therefore drives the corresponding open-drain line low, while a 1 releases it.
elements.check_method: Use a clock-by-clock scoreboard for the START sequence: assert scl_o==0 and sda_o==0 in every cycle, check the registered enable values in each phase, and compare the resolved bus levels to the open-drain model (line low iff the corresponding enable is 0 or the external participant drives low).

elements.stimulus: Apply reset, deassert reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, issue a START command, and observe the phase in which the START sequence pulls SDA low while SCL remains released high.
elements.expected_response: Holding case for SDA: sda_oen is 0 and the resolved SDA bus line is low; scl_oen remains 1 and the resolved SCL line is high through the external pull-up.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after registered outputs settle, compare sda_oen and scl_oen with the resolved open-drain bus model: line = 0 when the corresponding enable is 0, otherwise line = external pull-up high. Confirm the SDA low phase occurs while SCL is high.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset, deassert reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, issue a START command, and observe the following phase after the START condition when the sequence pulls SCL low.
elements.expected_response: Holding case for SCL: scl_oen is 0 and the resolved SCL bus line is low. The SCL low is produced by the low output-enable, independent of the external pull-up.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after registered outputs settle, check that scl_oen=0 and sample the resolved SCL line with the open-drain bus model; require the line to be low while this enable is asserted.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset, deassert reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, issue a START command, and observe the initial START-sequence phase before SDA is pulled low, when both SCL and SDA are released.
elements.expected_response: Holding case for released SCL: scl_oen is 1 and the resolved SCL bus line is high because the external pull-up is allowed to act; no DUT low drive is present on SCL.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after registered outputs settle, verify scl_oen=1 and resolve the SCL line with an external pull-up model; require the observed line to be high.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset, deassert reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, complete a START command, then issue a STOP command and observe the terminal STOP phase after SCL is released high, when SDA is released.
elements.expected_response: Holding case for released SDA: sda_oen is 1 and the resolved SDA bus line is high while SCL is high, allowing the external pull-up to raise SDA and form the STOP condition.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after registered outputs settle, verify sda_oen=1 during the terminal STOP phase and resolve SDA using an external pull-up model; require SDA to be high while SCL is high.

elements.stimulus: Compile and elaborate a top-level I2C master architecture that instantiates the DUT using the exact module name `i2c_master_bit_ctrl` and its specified ports.
elements.expected_response: Elaboration succeeds with `i2c_master_bit_ctrl` present as the Bit Command Controller module; no unresolved module, port, or width errors occur.
elements.check_method: Use the simulator/compiler elaboration result and inspect the elaborated hierarchy for an instance whose module type is exactly `i2c_master_bit_ctrl`.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset=0 then release it, keep rst=0 and ena=1, present cmd=START (4'b0001) while the bus inputs are released high, and clock until cmd_ack pulses.
elements.expected_response: Holding case for REQ-0007: the presented START command directly determines the SCL/SDA control sequence. scl_o and sda_o remain constant 0; scl_oen and sda_oen initially remain released (1,1), then sda_oen changes to 0 while scl_oen remains 1 to create START, and subsequently scl_oen changes to 0 while SDA remains driven low. The sequence completes with a one-clock cmd_ack pulse.
elements.check_method: At every posedge after registered outputs settle, compare scl_o and sda_o against constant 0 and compare the observed scl_oen/sda_oen trace against the reference START sequence, checking ordering and completion at cmd_ack.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset=0 then release it, keep rst=0, leave the bus released high, set ena=0, present cmd=START (4'b0001), and clock for longer than the normal START sequence; then also drive cmd=NOP (4'b0000) with ena=1 while idle.
elements.expected_response: Otherwise/non-holding case for REQ-0007: no command-specific SCL/SDA control sequence is produced when the enabled command-controller acceptance condition is absent. scl_o and sda_o remain constant 0, scl_oen and sda_oen remain at the released pair (1,1), and no cmd_ack is generated for either the disabled START or the NOP command.
elements.check_method: Monitor the complete output trace over the stimulus interval and assert that no output-enable departure from (1,1) occurs and cmd_ack remains low; independently compare scl_o and sda_o to constant 0.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, hold scl_i=1 and sda_i=1, issue cmd=START, and provide clocks until cmd_ack asserts or the command aborts.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: from command acceptance through cmd_ack, scl_oen and sda_oen show the START bit-level waveform: both lines are initially released, SDA is driven low while SCL remains released high, and SCL is then driven low before completion.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge, compare the observed scl_oen and sda_oen sequence against a reference START waveform model; require the expected phase ordering and termination at the one-clock cmd_ack pulse.

elements.stimulus: After a completed START or while the bus is busy, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, hold scl_i=1 and sda_i=1, issue cmd=STOP, and provide clocks until cmd_ack asserts or the command aborts.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: from command acceptance through cmd_ack, scl_oen and sda_oen show the STOP bit-level waveform: SDA is driven low, SCL is released high, and SDA is then released while SCL remains high before completion.
elements.check_method: Compare the sampled output-enable trace with a reference STOP waveform model and check the required ordering, completion pulse, and absence of an abort.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, hold scl_i=1 and sda_i=1, issue cmd=READ, drive sda_i with a stable read value of 0, and provide clocks through the read bit cycle until cmd_ack asserts or the command aborts.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: from command acceptance through cmd_ack, sda_oen remains released for the slave-driven read bit, while scl_oen releases SCL for the read sampling window and subsequently drives SCL low to finish the bit cycle.
elements.check_method: Compare scl_oen and sda_oen at every command phase with a reference READ waveform model; require the release/sample/low ordering and completion at cmd_ack.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, hold scl_i=1 and sda_i=1, issue cmd=WRITE with din=0, and provide clocks through the write bit cycle until cmd_ack asserts or the command aborts.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: from command acceptance through cmd_ack, sda_oen drives SDA low for din=0, scl_oen releases SCL for the write high phase, and scl_oen then drives SCL low to complete the bit cycle without abort.
elements.check_method: Compare the output-enable trace with a reference WRITE(din=0) waveform model, including SDA polarity, SCL release/drive ordering, and completion at cmd_ack.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, hold scl_i=1 and sda_i=1, issue cmd=WRITE with din=1, keep the external SDA line high during the released write phase, and provide clocks until cmd_ack asserts or the command aborts.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: from command acceptance through cmd_ack, sda_oen releases SDA for din=1, scl_oen releases SCL for the write high phase, and scl_oen then drives SCL low; the command completes without arbitration abort because the observed SDA remains high.
elements.check_method: Compare scl_oen and sda_oen against a reference WRITE(din=1) waveform and check that the expected release/low phases occur before the one-clock cmd_ack.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, hold scl_i=1 and sda_i=1, first drive cmd=NOP=0000 and then an unsupported cmd=0011 for complete enabled clock intervals, without issuing START, STOP, READ, or WRITE.
elements.expected_response: Non-holding case: scl_oen and sda_oen do not exhibit any command-specific START, STOP, READ, or WRITE bit-level waveform; they remain in the idle released-line behavior and no command sequence is started.
elements.check_method: Monitor the output enables over the complete stimulus windows and compare against the idle reference trace; fail if any command-specific phase transition or bit waveform appears.

elements.stimulus: Compile and elaborate i2c_master_bit_ctrl with a test harness that connects clk, rst, nReset, and ena as driven one-bit signals; drive clk with a clock, toggle rst and nReset, and drive ena through both 0 and 1.
elements.expected_response: When REQ-0009 holds, the module elaborates successfully and accepts clk, rst, nReset, and ena as input connections; subsequent driving of those signals is legal. The harness can compile without undeclared-port, direction, or width errors.
elements.check_method: Run RTL compilation and elaboration with strict port checking, then use interface reflection or the elaborated netlist to confirm that clk, rst, nReset, and ena each exist as one-bit inputs. Record a passing bin for successful connection and legal driving of all four ports.

elements.stimulus: Create interface-negative variants of the harness or DUT, separately omitting clk, rst, nReset, or ena and reversing one of their directions to output, then compile and elaborate each variant using the same four-input harness connections.
elements.expected_response: When REQ-0009 does not hold, compilation or elaboration fails for each variant with a required-port-missing, invalid-port-connection, direction, or equivalent interface mismatch error; no variant is accepted as a conforming i2c_master_bit_ctrl interface.
elements.check_method: Run strict compile/elaboration checks on each negative variant and assert that the tool rejects every variant. Record distinct failure bins for omission and direction reversal of each required port.

elements.stimulus: Instantiate the DUT and inspect its top-level interface. Confirm that a port named clk_cnt exists, is an input, and is driven with legal boundary values 16'h0000 and 16'hFFFF.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: the module elaborates successfully with clk_cnt declared as a 16-bit input, and both zero and all-ones 16-bit values are accepted without width mismatch.
elements.check_method: Use an elaboration/interface-schema check to match the exact port name, direction, and $bits(clk_cnt)==16; compile and run boundary-value connections with warnings treated as errors.

elements.stimulus: Run the interface checker against contrasting DUT interface declarations in which clk_cnt is absent, renamed, declared with 15 bits, or declared with 17 bits.
elements.expected_response: Non-holding case: the interface check fails for every contrasting declaration and reports that the required input port named clk_cnt is not exactly 16 bits.
elements.check_method: Use a compile-time port-schema assertion or lint check that rejects missing, renamed, 15-bit, and 17-bit clk_cnt declarations; treat any successful elaboration as a test failure.

elements.stimulus: Compile and elaborate the DUT with cmd declared as input logic [3:0] and cmd_ack, busy, and al each declared as output logic with width 1.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: elaboration succeeds, and port introspection reports cmd as a 4-bit input and cmd_ack, busy, and al as present 1-bit output ports.
elements.check_method: Use the simulator's elaboration result and an interface compile-time assertion or VPI/Verilog port query to compare each port's direction and exact width against the required declaration.

elements.stimulus: Compile and elaborate a mutation of the DUT in which cmd is declared with a width other than 4 bits, such as input logic [2:0] cmd, while the three status ports retain their required declarations.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: the interface check fails because cmd is not a 4-bit input port; the required interface is not accepted.
elements.check_method: Run elaboration and an interface-width assertion; require a reported width mismatch or failed compile-time check for cmd.

elements.stimulus: Compile and elaborate a mutation of the DUT in which cmd_ack is absent, declared with width 2, or declared as an input instead of a 1-bit output.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: the interface check fails because cmd_ack does not show the required 1-bit output status port; this is the specified otherwise condition.
elements.check_method: Use elaboration plus a port-direction and width assertion or VPI port query, and require failure for the cmd_ack declaration.

elements.stimulus: Compile and elaborate a mutation of the DUT in which busy is absent, declared with width 2, or declared as an input instead of a 1-bit output.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: the interface check fails because busy does not show the required 1-bit output status port; this is the specified otherwise condition.
elements.check_method: Use elaboration plus a port-direction and width assertion or VPI port query, and require failure for the busy declaration.

elements.stimulus: Compile and elaborate a mutation of the DUT in which al is absent, declared with width 2, or declared as an input instead of a 1-bit output.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: the interface check fails because al does not show the required 1-bit output status port; this is the specified otherwise condition.
elements.check_method: Use elaboration plus a port-direction and width assertion or VPI port query, and require failure for the al declaration.

elements.stimulus: Compile and elaborate the DUT using the declared module interface, then inspect the dout port metadata.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of shows: dout exists as a one-bit output data port and is connectable to a one-bit observation signal.
elements.check_method: Use compiler/elaborator diagnostics and simulator or netlist interface reflection to verify that dout is present, has width 1, and has output direction.

elements.stimulus: Run the interface conformance check against a DUT variant in which dout is absent, declared as an input, or declared with a width other than one bit.
elements.expected_response: Non-holding side of shows: the interface is rejected because dout is absent or is not declared as a one-bit output data-bit port.
elements.check_method: Require compilation, elaboration, or interface-schema validation to fail with a diagnostic identifying the missing, incorrectly directed, or incorrectly sized dout port.

elements.stimulus: Elaborate the i2c_master_bit_ctrl DUT and inspect its declared ports; connect scl_i and sda_i as driven inputs and connect scl_o, scl_oen, sda_o, and sda_oen as observed outputs.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of shows: scl_i and sda_i are input ports, scl_o and sda_o are output ports, and scl_oen and sda_oen are output ports documented and implemented as active-low output enables.
elements.check_method: Use compile/elaboration reflection or simulator VPI/HDL interface inspection to compare each port direction and name against the required declaration; inspect the implementation or interface metadata for active-low enable polarity.

elements.stimulus: Build an interface-mutated DUT variant in which at least one required declaration is removed or changed, such as declaring scl_oen or sda_oen as an input, omitting scl_o or sda_o, or changing an output-enable description/implementation to active-high.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case of shows: interface inspection or elaboration must report the port as absent, incorrectly directed, or not serving as an active-low output enable; the mutated DUT must not pass the REQ-0013 interface check.
elements.check_method: Run the same automated port-direction and polarity checker used for the holding case and require a deterministic failure identifying the malformed port declaration or polarity.

elements.stimulus: Apply an active-high synchronous reset, release reset, keep ena high and the bus released-high, issue a START command, and run clk through the complete START sequence while sampling cmd_ack immediately after each rising edge and between rising edges.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of the shows statement: at START completion, cmd_ack asserts only on a rising edge of clk, remains asserted for exactly the following clock interval, and does not change between rising edges.
elements.check_method: Use a clocking-block or post-NBA monitor keyed to posedges of clk; record cmd_ack transitions and assert that the rising transition occurs only at a clk posedge and that cmd_ack is high for exactly one inter-posedge interval.

elements.stimulus: Apply an active-high synchronous reset, release reset, keep ena high, issue a READ command with the external bus providing a valid released-high SCL and SDA value, and run clk through completion while observing cmd_ack for at least two rising edges after the completion indication.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case of the shows statement: cmd_ack must not change between rising edges and must be deasserted on the rising edge immediately following its one-clock assertion; it must not remain asserted across multiple clk intervals or pulse asynchronously between edges.
elements.check_method: Monitor cmd_ack continuously between sampled rising edges and compare successive post-edge values; flag any mid-interval transition or any assertion lasting through the second rising edge after command completion.

elements.stimulus: Hold ena high, provide a released-high bus, issue a valid START command, and run clk through completion. Sample cmd_ack immediately after every rising edge and continuously between each adjacent pair of rising edges.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: cmd_ack asserts only immediately after the rising edge that completes the START command, remains asserted for exactly that clock interval, and deasserts only immediately after the next rising edge. It remains stable between rising edges.
elements.check_method: Use a clocking-block or settled post-posedge monitor for edge samples and an independent between-edge sampler. Assert that every cmd_ack transition timestamp coincides with a posedge of clk and that the asserted interval spans exactly one clock period.

elements.stimulus: Run a valid WRITE command with ena high while changing cmd and din at falling edges and at additional non-rising-edge times during the command, including around the terminal phase; continue sampling cmd_ack between rising edges and after each rising edge until completion.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: cmd_ack must not assert, deassert, or otherwise change at any non-rising-edge time in response to these input changes. Any command-completion update to cmd_ack occurs only on a rising edge of clk; between edges it remains stable. A cmd_ack transition between rising edges is a failure of the requirement.
elements.check_method: Timestamp all cmd_ack value changes with a high-resolution event monitor and compare each timestamp against the clk rising-edge event stream. Also compare post-edge samples against all inter-edge samples to detect any transient or mid-cycle pulse.

elements.stimulus: Initialize the DUT, issue a START command with ena high, and allow the command sequence to become active with bus status or output-enable state differing from reset defaults. Assert rst=1 before a rising edge of clk and keep it high through that edge.
elements.expected_response: At the synchronous reset edge, the reset-holding side of the observation applies: cmd_ack=0, busy=0, al=0, scl_oen=1, and sda_oen=1. The command FSM, counters, filtered-input state, and bus-status state are reset.
elements.check_method: At the first posedge of clk with rst high, sample registered outputs after nonblocking updates settle and compare against the exact reset vector {cmd_ack,busy,al,scl_oen,sda_oen}=00011; verify the active command no longer progresses.

elements.stimulus: Initialize the DUT, issue a START command with ena high, and wait until the START sequence is active and has produced a non-reset output state. Keep rst=0 at a rising edge of clk while leaving the command and bus conditions otherwise unchanged.
elements.expected_response: At this non-reset edge, the contrasting side of the observation applies: the reset-default vector is not imposed. cmd_ack, busy, and al retain or follow ordinary command behavior, and scl_oen and sda_oen remain phase-dependent rather than being forced high; in particular, the active START phase must not be synchronously reset merely because a clock edge occurs with rst low.
elements.check_method: At the selected posedge with rst low, compare outputs with the immediately preceding active-command state and verify they are not forced to {cmd_ack,busy,al,scl_oen,sda_oen}=00011; use the command-phase reference model to check the ordinary active-phase values.

elements.stimulus: Deassert nReset high, issue a valid START command with ena high, and advance until the active sequence drives scl_oen low. Then assert nReset low at a time between two rising edges of clk and keep clk unchanged until after observing scl_oen.
elements.expected_response: The nReset-low holding case applies: scl_oen changes asynchronously to high, releasing SCL, immediately after nReset falls and before the next rising edge of clk.
elements.check_method: At a simulation sample taken after nReset falls but before the next clk posedge, compare scl_oen against the reset reference value 1; record a pass only if it is high without waiting for a clock edge.

elements.stimulus: Deassert nReset high, issue a valid START command with ena high, and advance until the active sequence drives scl_oen low. While nReset remains high and no reset is asserted, hold all inputs stable and observe scl_oen during an interval between consecutive rising edges of clk.
elements.expected_response: The nReset-high/no-reset contrasting case applies: scl_oen remains governed by the active command state and does not change asynchronously before a clock edge; it remains low throughout the inter-clock interval.
elements.check_method: Sample scl_oen immediately before and after a mid-cycle observation point, with no clk edge or reset assertion between samples, and compare both values with the command-state reference model; require no asynchronous transition.

elements.stimulus: Deassert both resets, keep the bus released/high, set clk_cnt to a small nonzero value, drive ena=1, present a supported START command, and hold the command until completion.
elements.expected_response: This is the ena=1 side of the requirement: the supported command is accepted, timing progression occurs, and cmd_ack pulses high for exactly one clock when the command finishes.
elements.check_method: At every posedge from command presentation through completion, compare cmd_ack against a reference command-FSM model; require one and only one high cycle, with no extra or missing pulse.

elements.stimulus: Deassert both resets, keep the bus released/high, set clk_cnt to a small nonzero value, drive a supported START command, set ena=0 for multiple enabled-clock intervals spanning the expected command-completion window, then set ena=1 while keeping the command presented.
elements.expected_response: This is the ena=0 side of the requirement: while ena=0, command acceptance and timing progression are disabled, so cmd_ack does not pulse during that observation window. After ena returns high, the command may progress and must eventually produce the normal one-clock cmd_ack completion pulse.
elements.check_method: Window-check cmd_ack on each posedge while ena=0 and require it remains low; then compare post-release behavior with a reference timing/FSM model and require exactly one completion pulse after enable resumes.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset low, release it, set clk_cnt=8, hold ena=0, keep scl_i and sda_i stable high, and run at least 32 rising edges of clk.
elements.expected_response: This is the ena-low side of the contrast: normal timing and filter operation is gated. clk_en remains deasserted and filter_cnt_expired never asserts; the timing counter and filter progression do not advance while ena remains low.
elements.check_method: At every posedge after reset release, sample clk_en and filter_cnt_expired after registered updates settle; assert both remain 0 for the entire ena-low interval and compare against a reference divider/filter model with enable gating.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset low, release it, set clk_cnt=8, hold ena=1, keep scl_i and sda_i stable high, and run for enough rising edges of clk to span multiple divider and filter intervals.
elements.expected_response: This is the ena-high side of the contrast: normal timing and filter operation proceeds. clk_en asserts at the reference-model divider expiration points and filter_cnt_expired asserts at the expected filter sampling intervals, allowing filter progression.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after reset release, compare clk_en and filter_cnt_expired pulses and their cycle spacing with a reference divider/filter model configured for clk_cnt=8 and ena=1; require at least two observed timing-enable ticks and filter-expiration events.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, set clk_cnt to 1, drive ena high, issue a supported WRITE command with din=1, and wait until the WRITE sequence is active and scl_oen has a timed phase value. Then drive ena low and hold it low for multiple rising edges of clk while applying a stable bus-line transition that would otherwise produce a filtered START or STOP.
elements.expected_response: This is the ena-low holding case: scl_oen holds its current timed command-phase value and does not advance to the next SCL phase; busy holds its prior value and does not respond to the attempted filtered START or STOP while the input filter is reset and disabled. No normal bit-timing progression occurs.
elements.check_method: At each posedge clk after ena goes low, compare scl_oen and busy with their values from the first ena-low cycle; require no change throughout the hold interval. Correlate with the timing reference model to require divider reload, filter-counter reset, and no clk_en/FSM progression while ena is low.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, set clk_cnt to 1, keep ena high, issue a supported WRITE command with din=1 on a released-high bus, and allow the command to run for multiple rising edges of clk. Separately drive a stable filtered SDA transition while filtered SCL is high to create a qualifying START or STOP condition.
elements.expected_response: This is the ena-high contrasting case: with timing enabled, scl_oen advances through the WRITE command's timed SCL phases rather than holding its current value, and busy processes a qualifying filtered START or STOP by setting or clearing accordingly.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate divider/filter/FSM reference model to predict clk_en and phase changes; compare sampled scl_oen after each posedge against the predicted phase sequence and compare busy against the predicted filtered START/STOP status update.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low and release it. Set ena=1, clk_cnt=16'd3, cmd=4'b0001 (START), and hold scl_i and sda_i high. Issue the START command and continue clocking until the command sequence completes.
elements.expected_response: Holding case for REQ-0021: the internal counter reloads from clk_cnt, reaches cnt_zero according to the divider reference model, and produces clk_en ticks. The START FSM advances only on those clk_en ticks, eventually pulling SDA low, pulling SCL low, and asserting cmd_ack for one clock.
elements.check_method: At every posedge, compare cnt_zero and clk_en against a cycle-accurate reference divider loaded with 16'd3 while ena=1. Confirm that each observed START phase transition and cmd_ack occurs only after the corresponding predicted clk_en tick.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low and release it. Set ena=1 and clk_cnt=16'd0. Issue a START command with scl_i and sda_i held high, then clock through multiple enabled cycles.
elements.expected_response: Holding-case boundary for REQ-0021: the zero reload value does not stall the divider; clk_en is generated on every enabled clock, and the START FSM advances on successive enabled clocks through its sequence.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model with the specified zero-prescaler behavior and compare clk_en on every posedge. Check that FSM probe transitions and cmd_ack occur on the predicted enabled-clock sequence and that no prolonged interval without clk_en occurs.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low and release it. Set clk_cnt=16'd3, ena=0, and issue a START command while scl_i and sda_i remain high. Hold ena low for several clocks, then raise ena=1 without changing clk_cnt and continue clocking.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting non-holding case for REQ-0021: while ena=0, divider progression and clk_en generation are disabled, the command is not accepted, and the FSM does not advance. After ena becomes 1, the divider resumes using clk_cnt=16'd3 and clk_en ticks permit command acceptance and progression.
elements.check_method: Check that the reference model predicts no clk_en, cnt progression, or FSM advancement during the ena=0 interval, then predicts reload/expiration and clk_en timing after ena=1. Confirm no cmd_ack is produced during the disabled interval and that subsequent START progress follows clk_en.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=8. Hold scl_i and sda_i stable, and run successive rising edges of clk while observing filter_cnt and filter_cnt_expired.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: filter_cnt derives the SDA/SCL filter sampling interval from clk_cnt; with clk_cnt=8, the sampling interval is floor(8/4)=2 enabled clocks. filter_cnt counts/reloads consistently with that interval and filter_cnt_expired occurs at the modeled sampling points.
elements.check_method: Compare filter_cnt and filter_cnt_expired on every enabled clock against a reference model implementing the specified floor(clk_cnt/4) interval and reload/decrement behavior.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0. Hold scl_i and sda_i stable, and run multiple rising edges of clk while observing filter_cnt and filter_cnt_expired.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting boundary case: unlike the clk_cnt=8 case, the zero value must not produce a stuck filter counter; the derived interval is treated as the minimum one enabled clock, so filter_cnt_expired occurs on every enabled clock and new filter samples are permitted each enabled clock.
elements.check_method: Compare the observed filter_cnt and filter_cnt_expired sequence with a reference model that clamps the zero-derived interval to one enabled clock; assert that expiration occurs on every enabled clock and that behavior differs from the two-clock interval in TP-0000.

elements.stimulus: After reset, model a byte controller supplying cmd=4'b0001 (START) on a clock boundary, with ena=1, clk_cnt=16'h0000, and released-high external SCL/SDA lines. Hold cmd until the command is accepted, then allow the START sequence to complete.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of the requirement: the 4-bit cmd value supplied by the byte-controller model is accepted as the bit-level START command. The observable command trace follows the normal START behavior: SDA is pulled low while SCL is high, SCL is subsequently pulled low, and cmd_ack pulses for exactly one clock.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after reset, compare cmd acceptance and the scl_oen/sda_oen/cmd_ack trace against a reference command-decode model; record that the driven value is exactly 4 bits and that the resulting trace matches the START-command expected sequence.

elements.stimulus: Repeat the same reset, bus, ena, clk_cnt, and cmd=4'b0001 sequence, but drive cmd directly from the verification environment rather than from the byte-controller model. Hold cmd until acceptance and allow the START sequence to complete.
elements.expected_response: Non-holding side of the requirement: because the interface exposes only the 4-bit cmd value and no source identity, the DUT must produce the same observable behavior as in TP-0000 for the identical cmd value. No source-dependent difference is permitted in START sequencing, output enables, or the one-clock cmd_ack pulse.
elements.check_method: Run a paired trace comparison between this scenario and TP-0000, matching cmd, scl_oen, sda_oen, and cmd_ack on every clock; require bit-for-bit identical outputs and no source-dependent status or timing difference.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low between clock edges, release it, set rst=0, ena=1, clk_cnt=16'h0000, and hold scl_i=1 and sda_i=1. After reset initialization confirms idle=1, drive cmd=4'b0001 (I2C_CMD_START) and hold it through an enabled clock tick.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: while the FSM is idle and cmd is I2C_CMD_START, cmd is decoded as START, idle becomes 0, and start_sequence becomes active. The START sequence releases SCL and SDA before pulling SDA low while SCL is high.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after reset, sample idle, start_sequence, scl_oen, and sda_oen after nonblocking assignments settle. Assert that start_sequence is entered only after the enabled tick with cmd=0001 and that the observed output-enable phase matches the START reference-model sequence.

elements.stimulus: Repeat reset and initialization with ena=1 and clk_cnt=16'h0000, keep scl_i=1 and sda_i=1, confirm idle=1, then drive cmd=4'b0000 (I2C_CMD_NOP) and hold it through multiple enabled clock ticks.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: when the FSM is idle but cmd is not I2C_CMD_START, the START command is not selected; start_sequence remains inactive and the FSM remains idle without producing a START output-enable sequence.
elements.check_method: Sample idle, start_sequence, cmd_ack, scl_oen, and sda_oen after every enabled posedge. Assert start_sequence=0 and idle=1 throughout the observation window, with no command acknowledgement and no transition into the START reference-model phases.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, leave the filtered bus released high, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, then while idle drive cmd=4'b0010 (I2C_CMD_STOP) for an enabled clock and continue supplying clocks until command completion.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: the STOP command is recognized from idle; SDA is driven low, SCL is released and allowed to become high, SDA is then released while SCL is high, and cmd_ack pulses high for exactly one clock after the STOP sequence completes.
elements.check_method: Use a transaction scoreboard to detect command acceptance and compare scl_oen/sda_oen against the required STOP phase ordering, requiring SDA low before SCL release and SDA release only while filtered SCL is high. Assert that cmd_ack has one rising-clock-wide pulse and no additional pulse for the transaction.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, leave the filtered bus released high, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, then while idle drive unsupported cmd=4'b0011 for multiple enabled clocks while monitoring the bus and command completion.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting non-holding case: no STOP waveform is produced—neither SDA is driven low as a STOP phase nor is a STOP release sequence initiated—and cmd_ack remains low for the entire interval.
elements.check_method: Compare the observed output-enable traces with an idle reference model and assert that no STOP phase transition occurs and cmd_ack never asserts while the unsupported command is applied.

elements.stimulus: After reset, hold ena=1 and drive cmd=4 (I2C_CMD_WRITE) while the FSM is idle; provide din=0 and keep the externally resolved SCL and SDA lines high unless driven low by the DUT. Continue clocking until the WRITE sequence reaches its terminal phase.
elements.expected_response: The command is recognized as WRITE, executes the WRITE bit sequence, and cmd_ack asserts for exactly one clock cycle at completion. This is the holding case of the observed behavior: cmd_ack indicates that the WRITE command was recognized and completed.
elements.check_method: At every posedge clk, compare cmd_ack against a reference WRITE-command FSM model and assert that exactly one pulse occurs after acceptance and that the pulse width is one clock; record the WRITE recognition and completion coverage bin.

elements.stimulus: With the FSM idle and ena=1, apply cmd=0 (NOP) for a complete command-acceptance opportunity, then repeat with unsupported encodings 3, 5, 6, 7, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, and 15; keep the bus inputs high and do not issue a supported command.
elements.expected_response: No WRITE sequence is entered and cmd_ack never pulses for any NOP or unsupported encoding. This is the contrasting case of the observed behavior: without a recognized WRITE command, cmd_ack does not assert.
elements.check_method: Monitor cmd_ack over each acceptance opportunity and the following clocks, compare against a reference decoder, and assert zero pulses for all listed encodings; record separate NOP and unsupported-command coverage bins.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low, release it, keep rst low, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0 with scl_i=1 and sda_i=1, then wait for reset state to settle. While idle, drive cmd=4'b0000 (NOP) for at least two enabled clock edges.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of shows: the command FSM remains in idle; no READ sequence starts, no command output-enable sequence occurs, and cmd_ack remains low.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after reset release, sample the idle probe, read_sequence probe, scl_oen, sda_oen, and cmd_ack after nonblocking assignments settle. Assert idle=1 and read_sequence=0 throughout the NOP stimulus, with no cmd_ack pulse; compare against a reference FSM model.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low, release it, keep rst low, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0 with scl_i=1 and sda_i=1, then wait for reset state to settle. While idle, drive cmd=4'b0011 (unsupported) for at least two enabled clock edges, then drive cmd=4'b1000 (I2C_CMD_READ) and hold it until the command is accepted.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of shows: cmd=0011 leaves the FSM idle with no cmd_ack or READ activity. Contrasting case of shows: after cmd=1000 is accepted on an enabled timing tick, the FSM leaves idle and enters the READ sequence, releasing SDA for the slave and releasing SCL for the read window.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference FSM and assertions sampled after each posedge. During cmd=0011 require idle=1, read_sequence=0, and cmd_ack=0. Following cmd=1000 acceptance require idle=0 and read_sequence=1, with sda_oen=1 and the READ-phase SCL release observed; allow subsequent completion latency to vary with the modeled timing.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=1, present cmd=0100 (WRITE) with din=0, and provide a released-high SCL/SDA bus. Hold these inputs until the command is accepted and the WRITE data-bit transmission phase is reached.
elements.expected_response: During the WRITE data-bit transmission phase, before and throughout the released SCL high phase, sda_oen is 0, meaning the DUT drives SDA low. This is the din=0 side of the specified behavior.
elements.check_method: At each clock while the WRITE data-bit phase is active and before cmd_ack, compare the registered sda_oen output against the reference value 0; record a coverage bin for din=0 and fail on any mismatch.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=1, present cmd=0100 (WRITE) with din=1, and provide a released-high SCL/SDA bus so arbitration is not lost. Hold these inputs until the command is accepted and the WRITE data-bit transmission phase is reached.
elements.expected_response: During the WRITE data-bit transmission phase, before and throughout the released SCL high phase, sda_oen is 1, meaning the DUT releases SDA. This is the din=1 side of the specified behavior.
elements.check_method: At each clock while the WRITE data-bit phase is active and before cmd_ack, compare the registered sda_oen output against the reference value 1; record a coverage bin for din=1 and fail on any mismatch.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, cmd=0000, and let the FSM remain idle. Set din=0 and issue cmd=0100 (WRITE) for one enabled clock. Keep the external bus released, with scl_i and sda_i high, and continue clocking until write_sequence is active and its data-drive phase occurs.
elements.expected_response: For the din=0 WRITE data-bit drive phase, sda_oen is 0 before and while SCL is released for the high phase; with the open-drain bus model this drives SDA low. This is the din=0 side of the requirement's stated behavior.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after registered outputs settle, detect write_sequence and the data-drive phase, then compare sda_oen against 0 and verify the resolved SDA line is low while SCL is released. End the check at cmd_ack or reset.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, cmd=0000, and let the FSM remain idle. Set din=1 and issue cmd=0100 (WRITE) for one enabled clock. Keep the external bus released, with scl_i and sda_i high, and continue clocking until write_sequence is active and its data-drive phase occurs.
elements.expected_response: For the din=1 WRITE data-bit drive phase, sda_oen is 1 before and while SCL is released for the high phase; with the open-drain bus model this releases SDA high. This is the din=1 side of the requirement's stated behavior.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after registered outputs settle, detect write_sequence and the data-drive phase, then compare sda_oen against 1 and verify the resolved SDA line remains high while SCL is released. End the check at cmd_ack or reset.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue a valid READ command. Once the controller releases SCL for the read sample window, externally hold scl_i low for multiple enabled timing intervals.
elements.expected_response: This is the 'external SCL held low' side of REQ-0030's shows statement: cmd_ack remains deasserted, the READ operation does not complete, and no filtered SCL rising edge is observed while scl_i remains low.
elements.check_method: At every posedge clk after registered outputs settle, compare cmd_ack and the filtered-SCL-rise observation against a reference model; assert that cmd_ack stays 0 for the entire interval in which the released external SCL input is held low.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue a valid READ command. Once the controller releases SCL for the read sample window, drive scl_i high and hold it high long enough for synchronization, filtering, and a filtered SCL rising edge; drive a defined SDA value during the sample window.
elements.expected_response: This is the 'external SCL allowed to rise' side of REQ-0030's shows statement: the filtered SCL rising edge occurs, the READ sample is taken, and cmd_ack asserts as the registered one-clock completion pulse after the operation's low phase.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model for SCL synchronization and filtering, then check that the observed filtered SCL rising edge precedes the READ completion and that cmd_ack is asserted for exactly one clock at the predicted variable-latency completion point.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, set ena=1 and a small nonzero clk_cnt, issue a supported START command, release SCL through scl_oen, and externally hold scl_i low while the DUT has released SCL high. Keep the external SCL low through synchronization and filtering, then release it high and allow the filtered high qualification to complete the command.
elements.expected_response: HOLDING CASE: cmd_ack remains withheld while the synchronized and filtered SCL is low, and is produced only after filtered SCL becomes high and the START terminal phase completes; the command does not advance through the high phase during clock stretching.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model for the two-stage SCL synchronizer, filter sampling, filtered SCL value, slave_wait, and FSM timing. Assert that cmd_ack is absent during the filtered-low interval and occurs only after filtered SCL is qualified high.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, set ena=1 and the same clk_cnt, issue the same START command, release SCL, and keep the external scl_i high continuously so no clock stretching occurs.
elements.expected_response: CONTRASTING CASE: with no externally held filtered-low SCL, cmd_ack follows the normal START terminal timing and is not postponed by a slave-wait interval.
elements.check_method: Compare the observed cmd_ack cycle against the reference model's unstretched command timing and verify no slave_wait interval precedes completion.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, start an enabled supported command that has released SCL high, and drive an external filtered SCL falling transition while scl_oen indicates that the DUT is releasing SCL. Hold the external SCL low long enough to pass synchronization and filtering, then return it high after the synchronized low-period timing.
elements.expected_response: HOLDING CASE: the synchronized and filtered external SCL falling edge is detected as clock synchronization; command timing is reloaded or re-timed to the externally driven low period, and cmd_ack is postponed or shifted relative to the no-falling-edge case.
elements.check_method: Monitor the synchronized/filter probes and command-completion trace, compare against a reference divider/FSM model, and verify the completion cycle reflects the external filtered SCL falling edge and timing reload.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, start the same enabled command with SCL released high, and keep scl_i high for the entire active command so no external filtered SCL falling edge occurs.
elements.expected_response: CONTRASTING CASE: without an externally caused filtered SCL falling edge, cmd_ack follows the command's normal terminal timing and is not re-timed by clock synchronization.
elements.check_method: Compare cmd_ack timing with the reference model and with TP-0002, confirming no synchronization reload or completion postponement occurs.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, set ena=1, establish filtered SCL high and filtered SDA high, then drive SDA low and keep both raw scl_i and sda_i stable long enough for synchronization and the three-sample filter to qualify the START transition. After busy sets, drive SDA high while SCL remains stably high for a similarly qualified STOP transition.
elements.expected_response: HOLDING CASE: busy sets only after the qualified filtered START and clears only after the qualified filtered STOP; raw input timing before filter qualification does not cause the status transitions.
elements.check_method: Use the filter/synchronizer reference model to predict sta_condition and sto_condition, then check registered busy transitions against those qualified events and their expected latency.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT with ena=1, establish stable filtered SCL and SDA high, and inject scl_i low pulses shorter than the synchronizer/filter qualification interval while toggling SDA around the pulses without allowing a stable filtered START or STOP condition.
elements.expected_response: CONTRASTING CASE: the raw or short SCL transitions do not become qualified filtered SCL high or low events; busy does not set or clear due to these glitches, and no false START/STOP-driven status transition occurs.
elements.check_method: Confirm with the reference filter model that no sta_condition or sto_condition is generated, then assert that busy remains at its pre-injection value and that no spurious command/status event is observed.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, set ena=1, issue a supported READ command, let the controller release SDA and SCL for the read window, and drive sda_i to a stable value before holding scl_i low and then transitioning scl_i high long enough for a synchronized and filtered SCL rising edge.
elements.expected_response: HOLDING CASE: dout captures the filtered SDA value on the qualified filtered SCL rising edge, not at the raw SCL transition; command completion and cmd_ack follow the subsequent low phase.
elements.check_method: Model synchronizer and filter latency, predict filtered_scl_rise and filtered SDA, and compare dout and cmd_ack cycle-by-cycle at the registered outputs.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, issue a supported READ command, and during its read window inject an scl_i rising pulse shorter than the synchronization/filter qualification interval while changing sda_i during or around that pulse; do not provide a stable filtered SCL rising edge.
elements.expected_response: CONTRASTING CASE: dout does not update because the raw SCL pulse does not become a qualified filtered SCL rising edge; the read sampler does not treat the glitch as a valid sample event.
elements.check_method: Use the filter reference model to verify filtered_scl_rise remains false, then assert dout remains unchanged through the injected pulse and changes only on a later qualified filtered SCL rising edge.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1 and hold the external bus released with filtered SCL high. Issue a START command, then drive sda_i from high to low and hold it stable long enough to pass the two-stage synchronizer and three-sample filter.
elements.expected_response: Holding case for busy: busy changes from 0 to 1 only after the SDA falling transition has propagated through synchronization and filtering and forms a filtered START condition; it does not change at the raw input transition or before the filtered transition.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model of the two-stage SDA synchronizer, filter sampling, three-sample majority, and START detector. Compare the modeled filtered transition and busy update cycle with the DUT busy output.

elements.stimulus: With ena=1, filtered SCL high, and busy=0, apply an SDA high-to-low pulse shorter than the synchronization/filter acceptance interval, then restore sda_i high without issuing a command.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case for busy: busy does not change in response to the SDA glitch because the transition does not survive synchronization and filtering; no filtered START or STOP indication is produced.
elements.check_method: Drive the pulse with a duration below the modeled filter acceptance requirement and compare busy against the reference model's filtered SDA majority and START/STOP detections. Assert that busy remains 0 throughout.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1, issue a WRITE command with din=1, and during the command's released-high SDA arbitration-check phase drive the external bus SDA low and hold sda_i low long enough to pass synchronization and filtering.
elements.expected_response: Holding case for al: al asserts when the synchronized and filtered SDA is low during the released-high WRITE arbitration-check phase, and the active command aborts without cmd_ack.
elements.check_method: Use the reference model to identify the released-high arbitration-check phase and the cycle at which filtered SDA becomes low. Compare that cycle and the subsequent sticky al assertion and command abort with the DUT outputs.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1, issue a WRITE command with din=1, and during the released-high SDA arbitration-check phase apply an external SDA-low pulse shorter than the synchronization/filter acceptance interval, then release SDA high.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case for al: al does not newly assert because the low pulse does not become a filtered SDA-low value during the arbitration-check phase; the WRITE continues to its normal completion and produces cmd_ack.
elements.check_method: Model synchronization and majority filtering, confirm the filtered SDA remains high throughout the arbitration-check sampling point, and compare al and cmd_ack against the DUT. Check that al remains 0 and the command acknowledges normally.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1, issue a READ command, keep SDA released, drive sda_i to a stable 0 before the read sampling window, and provide a stable SCL rising transition that propagates through synchronization and filtering to produce a filtered SCL rising edge.
elements.expected_response: Holding case for dout: on the filtered SCL rising edge in the READ sampling window, dout updates to the synchronized and filtered SDA value, 0, rather than to an earlier raw SDA value.
elements.check_method: Run the synchronizer/filter reference model for SDA and SCL, identify the filtered SCL rising-edge cycle, and compare dout with the modeled filtered SDA value on that cycle and after the registered output update.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1, issue a READ command, and apply a short SDA glitch during the read window that does not survive synchronization/filtering. Do not provide a filtered SCL rising edge during the glitch; retain the prior dout value.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case for dout: dout retains its prior value because no filtered SCL rising edge occurs with a new filtered SDA sample; the raw or unsynchronized SDA glitch does not update dout.
elements.check_method: Use the reference model to confirm that the SDA glitch is rejected and that filtered_scl_rise remains false. Compare dout before, during, and after the glitch and assert that it remains unchanged until a valid filtered SCL rising edge.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue cmd=START with SCL and SDA externally released high; allow the START sequence to complete through its terminal SCL-low phase.
elements.expected_response: At the registered command-completion edge, cmd_ack asserts high for exactly one clk cycle, then returns low and remains low until another command completes.
elements.check_method: Use a clocked reference model to identify the terminal START phase; compare cmd_ack after each posedge and assert a single high sample at completion with low samples on the immediately preceding and following cycles.

elements.stimulus: With ena=1 and the bus in a valid busy transaction state, issue cmd=STOP; provide released-high SCL after the controller drives SDA low and allow the STOP sequence to finish.
elements.expected_response: At the registered command-completion edge after SDA is released high while SCL is high, cmd_ack asserts for exactly one clk cycle and is low on all other cycles.
elements.check_method: Correlate the observed output-enable phase sequence with a reference STOP model, then compare cmd_ack at successive posedges for one and only one high cycle at the terminal phase.

elements.stimulus: With ena=1, issue cmd=READ; release SDA for the external device, drive a valid read bit, allow the filtered SCL rising edge to capture it, and allow the subsequent SCL-low terminal phase to complete.
elements.expected_response: After the READ bit cycle finishes, cmd_ack asserts high for exactly one clk cycle and then deasserts; no ack pulse occurs before the terminal phase.
elements.check_method: Use the filtered SCL edge and READ phase reference model to determine completion, sample cmd_ack after each posedge, and verify exactly one high cycle coincident with completion.

elements.stimulus: With ena=1, issue cmd=WRITE with din=0 and a released bus; allow the controller to drive SDA low, complete the released-SCL high phase without arbitration loss, and return SCL low.
elements.expected_response: When the WRITE bit-level sequence finishes, cmd_ack asserts for exactly one clk cycle and is low before and after that completion pulse.
elements.check_method: Track the WRITE terminal phase with a cycle-accurate reference model and compare registered cmd_ack at every posedge, requiring one high cycle only at completion.

elements.stimulus: With ena=1, issue cmd=WRITE with din=1; during the released SCL-high arbitration-check phase, externally hold SDA low to force arbitration loss before the WRITE command completes.
elements.expected_response: The command aborts on arbitration loss and cmd_ack does not pulse high at the aborted command's would-be completion edge or at any later cycle; the output remains low until a separately completed command.
elements.check_method: Inject the filtered SDA-low arbitration-loss condition, use the reference model to mark the command aborted rather than completed, and assert cmd_ack remains low throughout the abort and subsequent idle cycles.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT with the bus released high, then hold SCL high and drive SDA from high to low long enough for synchronization and filtering to produce a filtered START condition; keep the bus active afterward.
elements.expected_response: When the filtered START condition is detected, `busy` becomes high on the corresponding registered update and remains high throughout the resulting busy-bus interval. This is the high side of `busy` being high when the I2C bus is busy.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model for synchronization, filter majority, and filtered START detection; compare the predicted registered `busy` value with the DUT after each posedge, requiring `busy==1` after `sta_condition` and while the bus remains active.

elements.stimulus: First create a filtered START condition with SCL high and SDA transitioning high to low so the bus becomes busy. Then, while SCL remains high, drive SDA from low to high long enough for synchronization and filtering to produce a filtered STOP condition, and keep the bus released afterward.
elements.expected_response: After the filtered STOP condition is detected, `busy` becomes low on the corresponding registered update and remains low while the bus is not busy. This is the low side of `busy` being low when the I2C bus is not busy.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model for the filtered START and STOP transitions and registered status timing; compare the DUT `busy` output after each posedge, requiring it to be high before the STOP and `busy==0` after `sto_condition`.

elements.stimulus: After reset, hold filtered SCL high by driving scl_i high and drive sda_i high long enough for synchronization and filtering to settle. Drive sda_i low while keeping scl_i high and hold the levels until sta_condition is asserted. Then keep SCL high and SDA low for multiple enabled clocks before generating a STOP.
elements.expected_response: The holding side of the requirement is satisfied: after sta_condition is detected, busy becomes 1 on the corresponding registered update and remains 1 throughout the interval until the STOP condition is detected.
elements.check_method: At each clock after sta_condition detection and before sto_condition detection, compare busy against 1 using a reference model of the synchronizer/filter latency; assert that no sampled busy value is 0 during this interval.

elements.stimulus: With SCL high and SDA initially high, drive SDA low and hold it until sta_condition is detected. After busy has become 1, keep SCL high and drive SDA high, holding the transition until sto_condition is detected.
elements.expected_response: The contrasting clearing side of the requirement is satisfied: busy is cleared on the registered update corresponding to sto_condition and does not remain set after the detected STOP.
elements.check_method: Use the filtered START/STOP reference model to identify sta_condition and sto_condition; verify busy is 1 before the STOP detection, then equals 0 on the first settled sampled cycle at or after sto_condition and remains 0 while no subsequent START is detected.

elements.stimulus: After reset with ena=1, issue a WRITE command with din=1 and clk_cnt=0 while the external bus is high. During the WRITE released-SDA high phase when SDA arbitration checking is enabled, externally hold SDA low and keep filtered SDA low through the sampling point.
elements.expected_response: The al output asserts to 1 when the released-high WRITE bit observes filtered SDA low, indicating the arbitration-loss case in observed_via. It remains asserted after the command aborts and both output enables are released; no command-complete pulse is generated for the aborted command.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after nonblocking assignments settle, compare al against a reference arbitration model: require a low-to-high transition at or immediately after detection of the filtered arbitration-loss condition, then require al to remain high until reset. Also check that no cmd_ack pulse occurs for the aborted command.

elements.stimulus: After reset with ena=1, issue a WRITE command with din=0 and clk_cnt=0 while the external bus is high, then allow the WRITE sequence to complete without an unexpected STOP. Keep SDA low during the driven-low WRITE phase and do not introduce any released-SDA arbitration mismatch.
elements.expected_response: The al output remains low throughout the active command and after normal completion, representing the otherwise side of observed_via: al remains low when arbitration has not been lost. The command completes with its normal cmd_ack pulse.
elements.check_method: Sample al after every settled posedge and compare it with the reference model's no-loss expectation; require al=0 for the full command, including the completion cycle. Separately verify the expected single cmd_ack pulse to distinguish normal completion from an arbitration-loss abort.

elements.stimulus: Reset the controller, issue START with ena=1, then issue WRITE with din=1. During the WRITE released-SDA high phase when sda_chk=1 and filtered SCL is high, externally hold SDA low so filtered SDA ssda=0.
elements.expected_response: At the clock edge detecting sda_chk=1, sda_oen=1, and ssda=0, al asserts. The command aborts without cmd_ack, the controller returns to idle, and both scl_oen and sda_oen are released. al remains asserted on subsequent clocks until reset. This is the holding side of the observed al behavior.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model and assertions sampling after each posedge: assert al rises on the qualifying filtered arbitration condition, cmd_ack stays low for the aborted command, both output enables are 1 after abort, and al remains 1 on later clocks before reset.

elements.stimulus: Reset the controller, issue START with ena=1, then issue WRITE with din=0 or READ with ena=1. While the non-STOP command is active, arrange a stable filtered STOP condition by allowing filtered SDA to rise while filtered SCL is high, without issuing a STOP command.
elements.expected_response: When active_command=1 and sto_condition=1 for the unrequested STOP, al asserts, the active command is aborted, the FSM returns to idle, both SCL and SDA are released, and no cmd_ack is generated for the aborted command. al remains asserted until reset. This is the holding side of the observed al behavior for the unexpected-STOP cause.
elements.check_method: Drive the bus through the synchronizer and filter model to produce sto_condition, then compare post-edge al, idle, cmd_ack, scl_oen, and sda_oen against the reference model; assert that al is sticky after the detection edge.

elements.stimulus: Reset the controller, issue START with ena=1, then issue WRITE with din=1. During the WRITE released-SDA high phase, keep the external SDA high so filtered SDA ssda=1; maintain SCL normally and do not create a filtered STOP condition while the command is active.
