elements.expected_response: The released-SDA arbitration check completes without asserting al, because filtered SDA is not low. No unexpected STOP is detected, so al does not newly assert and retains its prior sticky value of 0 while the command proceeds normally toward completion.
elements.check_method: Use assertions at each active WRITE high phase that sda_chk=1 and sda_oen=1 with ssda=1 do not cause an al rising edge; independently check that no sto_condition occurs and compare the command progression and final al value with the reference model.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset low and release it, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, keep the filtered bus idle high, issue cmd=READ (1000) while idle, and allow the READ sequence to release SDA and SCL. Drive the external SDA line low and hold it stable through the filtered SCL rising edge used as the READ sample event.
elements.expected_response: At the registered update following that filtered SCL rising edge, dout equals the received data bit 0. This is the 'dout equals the received data bit' side of the observed behavior.
elements.check_method: Use the reference model for synchronizers, filtering, and READ sequencing to identify filtered_scl_rise; sample dout after the corresponding posedge and compare it with the SDA value presented at that filtered rising edge.

elements.stimulus: Reset and configure the DUT as in TP-0000, issue cmd=READ with ena=1, drive external SDA low through the READ sample window, and keep it low until the filtered SCL rising edge. Immediately after the registered update caused by that edge, change the external SDA line high while the READ phase continues.
elements.expected_response: dout remains 0, the bit captured at the filtered SCL rising edge, and does not change merely because SDA becomes 1 afterward. Relative to the subsequently changed received-line value, dout differs; this is the contrasting 'dout differs from the received data' side and confirms that sampling is tied to the filtered SCL rising edge rather than a later SDA change.
elements.check_method: Record the filtered SDA value at filtered_scl_rise, then change the external SDA value after that event and verify with a cycle-accurate scoreboard that dout retains the sampled value and is not updated by the post-edge change.

elements.stimulus: After reset, issue a READ command with ena=1 and clk_cnt set to a value that permits normal filtering. During the READ sequence, release SDA externally high, then allow filtered SCL to transition from low to high while scl_i is high. Ensure dout contains or is distinguishable from 1 before the filtered SCL rising edge, and hold filtered SDA at 0 at the rising-edge event.
elements.expected_response: At the filtered_scl_rise event, dout is updated to 0, the current filtered SDA value, and remains 0 until the next filtered SCL rising edge. This is the shows side of the observed_via behavior; it must not exhibit the otherwise side of retaining the prior value.
elements.check_method: Use the reference model for synchronization, filtering, majority history, and filtered_scl_rise detection. On the posedge that processes filtered_scl_rise, sample dout after nonblocking updates settle and compare it with the modeled filtered SDA value of 0; verify no update is attributed to a later rising edge.

elements.stimulus: Issue a READ command with ena=1 and a normal prescaler. During the READ sequence, have the external device release or drive SDA so that the filtered SDA value is stably 1 before and at the next filtered SCL rising edge, while scl_i is high and the controller has released SCL. Arrange for dout to be 0 before that edge.
elements.expected_response: At the filtered_scl_rise event, dout is updated to 1, the current filtered SDA value, and remains 1 until the next filtered SCL rising edge. This is the shows side of the observed_via behavior; the contrasting otherwise side would be dout not updating from its prior 0 value and must not occur.
elements.check_method: Predict filtered_scl_rise and filtered SDA with the reference synchronizer/filter model. Sample dout after the triggering posedge and compare it to modeled filtered SDA=1; specifically check that dout changes from its pre-edge 0 to 1 before the following filtered SCL rising edge.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset low, release it, then issue a START command with ena high and a released-high bus so the command sequence drives scl_oen low during its SCL-low phase and later changes the SCL output-enable state.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of shows: scl_o remains exactly 1'b0 at every clocked observation, including while scl_oen is 0 and while scl_oen is 1; only scl_oen changes the actual open-drain SCL ownership.
elements.check_method: At every posedge after reset release and throughout the complete START sequence, compare sampled scl_o against 1'b0 and assert that no sampled value is high or differs from the previous value; separately correlate the observations with scl_oen transitions.

elements.stimulus: After establishing a transaction with START, issue a STOP command with ena high and a released-high bus, causing the FSM to drive SCL low and then release it by toggling scl_oen from 0 to 1.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting otherwise side of shows: although a nonconforming implementation could make scl_o high or change when scl_oen is released, the DUT shall keep scl_o constantly at 1'b0 throughout the STOP sequence; the SCL line itself may rise when scl_oen becomes 1.
elements.check_method: Monitor scl_o and scl_oen on every posedge through the STOP low phase, release phase, and command acknowledgment. Fail if scl_o is ever 1 or changes, and independently verify that the external wired-AND SCL line responds to scl_oen rather than to scl_o.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, set ena=1 and clk_cnt to a value that permits progress, keep the external SCL and SDA lines released high, issue cmd=START, and advance through the START sequence until the controller pulls SCL low after generating the START condition.
elements.expected_response: During the START sequence's SCL-low phase, scl_oen is 0, which is the asserted side of the observed behavior: the active-low open-drain SCL control drives SCL low. The modeled bus SCL line shall therefore be low.
elements.check_method: At every settled posedge after command progression, compare scl_oen against the reference FSM phase and resolve the modeled open-drain SCL line as low when scl_oen=0; require scl_oen=0 and modeled SCL=0 in the SCL-low phase.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, set ena=1 and clk_cnt to a value that permits progress, keep the external SCL and SDA lines released high, issue cmd=START, and sample the initial START-sequence phase before SDA is pulled low while SCL is held released high.
elements.expected_response: During the initial released-SCL phase, scl_oen is 1, which is the contrasting side of the observed behavior: the SCL control is not asserted and SCL is released rather than driven low. With no external low driver, the modeled bus SCL line shall remain high.
elements.check_method: At settled posedges, compare scl_oen with the reference START phase and resolve the modeled open-drain SCL line; require scl_oen=1 and modeled SCL=1 during the initial released-SCL phase.

elements.stimulus: Set nReset low and then high, set rst=0 and ena=1, drive clk_cnt=0, keep scl_i and sda_i high, and issue a valid START command. During the START sequence, wait for the phase in which the controller releases SCL before pulling SDA low.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: scl_oen is 1, so the DUT releases SCL and the external pull-up drives the observed SCL line high. Throughout the sequence, sda_o remains constantly 0; SDA ownership is controlled only by sda_oen.
elements.check_method: At every settled posedge after reset and throughout the START sequence, assert sda_o===1'b0. When the START release phase is reached, assert scl_oen===1'b1 and, with no external SCL pull-down, assert the resolved SCL line is high. Record coverage of the scl_oen=1 release case.

elements.stimulus: Continue the same enabled START command sequence with clk_cnt=0 and the bus otherwise released, advancing through the phase after the START condition when the controller pulls SCL low.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: scl_oen is 0, so the DUT drives SCL low. Despite this SCL drive state, sda_o remains constantly 0, and the SDA line remains controlled by sda_oen rather than by sda_o.
elements.check_method: At the settled posedge for the SCL-low phase, assert scl_oen===1'b0 and, regardless of external SCL input, assert the resolved SCL line is low. At the same and all surrounding cycles, assert sda_o===1'b0 and verify SDA resolution follows sda_oen. Record coverage of the scl_oen=0 contrasting case.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, set ena=1 and clk_cnt to a value that permits clk_en progression, issue a WRITE command with din=0 while the external SDA and SCL lines are released high, and run through the WRITE data-bit phase.
elements.expected_response: During the WRITE data-bit drive phase, sda_oen is 0 at the interface sampling edge: this is the asserted-low side of the requirement and selects the open-drain operation that drives SDA low. With sda_o=0 and no external override, the observed SDA bus line is low.
elements.check_method: At every settled posedge during the WRITE data-bit phase, compare sda_oen against 0 and independently resolve the open-drain bus model; require sda_oen==0 and SDA line==0.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, set ena=1 and clk_cnt to a value that permits clk_en progression, issue a WRITE command with din=1 while the external SDA and SCL lines are released high, and run through the WRITE data-bit phase.
elements.expected_response: During the WRITE data-bit phase, sda_oen is not 0 and is instead 1: this is the contrasting side of the requirement, so the low-drive operation is not selected. The DUT releases SDA, allowing the externally released bus line to remain high.
elements.check_method: At every settled posedge during the WRITE data-bit phase, compare sda_oen against 1 and resolve the open-drain bus model; require sda_oen!=0 and, with no external low drive, SDA line==1.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, keep scl_i and sda_i high, issue the supported WRITE command with din=1, and run through the WRITE data-high phase until the registered sda_oen output is observable.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding case in observed_via.shows: sda_oen reads 1 during the WRITE high-data phase, releasing SDA so the external pull-up can drive the SDA line high.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge during the WRITE high-data phase, compare sda_oen against 1 and verify the open-drain bus model resolves SDA high when no external participant drives it low.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, keep scl_i and sda_i high, issue the supported WRITE command with din=0, and run through the WRITE data-low phase until the registered sda_oen output is observable.
elements.expected_response: This is the contrasting otherwise case in observed_via.shows: sda_oen reads 0 during the WRITE low-data phase, driving SDA low rather than releasing it to the external pull-up.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge during the WRITE low-data phase, compare sda_oen against 0 and verify the open-drain bus model resolves SDA low even though the external pull-up is present.

elements.stimulus: Provide the specification artifact containing the implementation-details section.
elements.expected_response: The artifact contains the exact heading "Implementation details:" followed by a numbered-list item beginning with "1.".
elements.check_method: Use a text parser or regular-expression check to locate the exact heading and verify that the next numbered-list marker is "1.".

elements.stimulus: After reset, exercise idle, START, WRITE with din=0 and din=1, READ, and STOP commands with ena high; allow each sequence to run to completion on a released external bus.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of shows: scl_o and sda_o remain 0 throughout reset, idle, and every command phase, regardless of scl_oen or sda_oen. The module therefore never directly drives either bus line high.
elements.check_method: Sample scl_o and sda_o after every posedge clk and assert they are continuously 0 for the complete stimulus interval; separately cross-check that only scl_oen and sda_oen change bus ownership.

elements.stimulus: Run the same command and reset activity while applying a checker-side fault injection that forces or models scl_o or sda_o to 1 for at least one clock, then release the injection and resume normal operation.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting side of shows: a high scl_o or sda_o is observable evidence that the module directly drives the corresponding line high and is a requirement violation; the DUT's actual outputs must not produce this condition during the run.
elements.check_method: Use an assertion and fault-injection scoreboard: flag any DUT-originated scl_o or sda_o value of 1, and confirm the injected high is classified as a failure signature rather than accepted behavior. After release, require both outputs to return/remain at 0.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low asynchronously, release it, then apply synchronous rst on a rising edge. Keep ena high while the module remains idle, and sample scl_o and sda_o after reset release and on multiple subsequent clock edges.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of shows: scl_o and sda_o are present and remain continuously 1'b0 at every observation point during reset recovery and idle operation.
elements.check_method: At each sampled clock edge and immediately after asynchronous reset assertion, compare scl_o === 1'b0 and sda_o === 1'b0; fail on any transition or unknown value.

elements.stimulus: With ena high, execute START, WRITE with din=0, WRITE with din=1, READ, and STOP commands while varying external scl_i and sda_i and allowing scl_oen and sda_oen to change through their command phases.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case of shows: although command sequences and the active-low output enables drive and release the I2C lines, scl_o and sda_o remain constantly 1'b0 rather than reflecting output-enable state or command phase. Any value other than 1'b0 is a failure of the required behavior.
elements.check_method: Monitor scl_o and sda_o on every clock throughout all command phases, including reset, START/STOP transitions, WRITE high phases, READ windows, and completion; assert each is exactly 1'b0 independently of scl_oen, sda_oen, scl_i, and sda_i.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, issue a valid START command, and sample the START phase in which SDA is driven low while SCL remains released. Model the external pull-up with no external low drive.
elements.expected_response: For the holding case, sda_oen is 0 and the resolved SDA line is pulled low; scl_oen is 1 and the resolved SCL line remains released high.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge sample, compare the resolved bus lines against the open-drain reference model: line=0 when its output enable is 0, otherwise line=1 with no external pull-down. Bin sda_oen=0 with SDA low and scl_oen=1 with SCL high.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, issue a valid START command, and sample the subsequent START phase after the controller pulls SCL low. Model the external pull-up with no external low drive.
elements.expected_response: For the holding case, scl_oen is 0 and the resolved SCL line is pulled low. The SDA output-enable reflects the current START phase and its resolved line follows the same active-low mapping.
elements.check_method: At the settled posedge for the SCL-low phase, assert scl_oen==0 and resolved SCL==0; independently compare the resolved SDA line with sda_oen using the same open-drain reference model.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, issue a valid START command, and sample the initial START phase before SDA is pulled low, when both bus lines are released. Model the external pull-up with no external low drive.
elements.expected_response: For the contrasting case, scl_oen is 1 and the resolved SCL line is released high; sda_oen is 1 and the resolved SDA line is released high.
elements.check_method: Compare both output enables and resolved lines at the settled posedge against the release model: each enable must equal 1 and, absent an external pull-down, each corresponding line must resolve high.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, issue a valid STOP command after establishing a transaction, and sample the STOP phase after SCL is released and SDA is released while SCL is high. Model the external pull-up with no external low drive.
elements.expected_response: For the contrasting case, scl_oen is 1 and the resolved SCL line is released high; when the STOP phase releases SDA, sda_oen is 1 and the resolved SDA line is released high.
elements.check_method: At the settled STOP-phase posedges, verify scl_oen==1 and resolved SCL==1, then verify sda_oen==1 and resolved SDA==1, using a bus-resolution monitor that treats enable-high as release to the pull-up.

elements.stimulus: Assert and release nReset, keep ena high, provide a released-high external bus, then issue a START command (cmd=0001) and wait for the START sequence's initial release phase.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: during the phase where the corresponding output enables are high, scl_oen=1 and sda_oen=1; the open-drain bus model resolves both released SCL and SDA lines high through the external pull-up resistors.
elements.check_method: At each registered output update, sample scl_oen and sda_oen and compare the resolved bus levels against an open-drain reference model with external pull-ups. Confirm the released-line observation is scl_oen=1/sda_oen=1 and SCL=SDA=1.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep ena high and issue a START command (cmd=0001) with the external bus released; wait until the START sequence reaches its phase that pulls SDA low while SCL remains high.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: sda_oen=0, so SDA is actively pulled low and is not raised by the external pull-up; scl_oen remains 1, so SCL is released and resolves high through its external pull-up.
elements.check_method: Sample sda_oen, scl_oen, and the resolved bus lines after the registered output update. Compare against the open-drain model and explicitly verify the non-holding side of the observation: sda_oen=0 implies SDA=0, while scl_oen=1 implies SCL=1.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1 and clk_cnt=16'h0003. Assert rst=1 for a rising edge of clk, with nReset=1, then deassert rst while holding all other inputs stable.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: on the reset clock, cnt is loaded from clk_cnt and clk_en is asserted. After reset is released, the reference divider starts from 3 and produces the next timing tick only after the modeled counter expiration.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after registered updates settle, compare the observed clk_en probe with a reference model that loads 3 during reset and records the reset-cycle tick.

elements.stimulus: With nReset=1, rst=0, clk_cnt=16'h0003, and ena=1, allow the counter to run until cnt_zero is observed, then continue for several enabled clocks.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: when cnt reaches zero, cnt is reloaded from 3 and clk_en is asserted on that clock. The resulting sequence repeats with the reference-model period; no decrement-only behavior occurs on the expiration clock.
elements.check_method: Use cnt_zero and the prior reference-model counter value to identify expiration cycles, then compare clk_en and subsequent tick spacing against a cycle-accurate divider model.

elements.stimulus: With nReset=1, rst=0, clk_cnt=16'h0005, first run with ena=1 for two clocks, then drive ena=0 and hold it low for four rising edges.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: on every clock while ena=0, cnt is loaded from clk_cnt and clk_en is asserted. The counter does not enter a decrementing sequence while the core is disabled.
elements.check_method: Compare clk_en on each ena-low clock with a reference model that reloads 5 on every disabled cycle; verify a tick on every such cycle.

elements.stimulus: With ena=1, rst=0, nReset=1, and clk_cnt=16'h0004, release SCL through scl_oen, establish filtered SCL high, then drive the external scl_i low and hold it long enough for synchronization so that scl_sync asserts.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: on the clock where multi-master synchronization is detected, cnt is reloaded from 4 and clk_en is asserted; subsequent decrement timing restarts from the reload value.
elements.check_method: Correlate the scl_sync probe with clk_en and compare the following tick schedule against a reference model that reloads 4 on the synchronization event.

elements.stimulus: With nReset=1, rst=0, ena=1, clk_cnt=16'h0003, and no reset, disable, cnt_zero, or scl_sync event active, start from a loaded counter and apply three consecutive enabled clocks.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: because none of the reload conditions holds, cnt decrements on each clock and clk_en is not asserted during those decrement cycles. A tick occurs only when the modeled counter reaches zero on the following expiration cycle.
elements.check_method: Drive the reference divider from the known reload value, assert that the no-trigger cycles decrement without clk_en, and compare the first subsequent expiration tick with the model.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=1, issue a supported START command, and when the controller releases SCL (scl_oen rises to 1), drive the external SCL input low and keep it low for multiple enabled clocks while leaving reset inactive.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding case of the observation: while SCL remains externally held low after scl_oen rises, slave_wait remains active, clk_en remains low on every clock, the timing counter retains its pre-wait value, and the command output-enable phase does not advance. No command-complete pulse is generated during the wait.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after scl_oen rises, compare clk_en against 0 and compare scl_oen/sda_oen with the reference FSM state; use the reference divider model or cnt_zero probe to verify the counter value is unchanged across the wait. Confirm that phase outputs and cmd_ack remain unchanged/low until external SCL is released high.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=1, issue a supported START command, and when the controller releases SCL (scl_oen rises to 1), keep the external SCL input high so the released line is not clock-stretched; continue clocking until the next timing phase is reached.
elements.expected_response: This is the contrasting non-holding case of the observation: because released SCL is high, slave_wait is not asserted, the timing counter progresses and expires, clk_en asserts at the expected enabled tick, and the command output enables advance to the next START phase rather than holding. The command eventually produces its normal one-clock cmd_ack.
elements.check_method: Monitor scl_oen/sda_oen and the clk_en probe after SCL release; compare the observed phase transition and tick timing with the reference divider/FSM model. Check that at least one clk_en tick occurs and the output-enable state advances before command completion, with exactly one cmd_ack pulse.

elements.stimulus: Apply no functional stimulus; review REQ-0052@1 as a scaffolding list-item marker stating no requirement.
elements.expected_response: No DUT behavior, output value, timing, or state transition is required by REQ-0052@1.
elements.check_method: Requirements review confirms the item contains no behavioral obligation and therefore has no DUT assertion beyond recording its no-requirement status.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0. Issue a supported READ command (cmd=4'b1000). Hold the external SCL line low with scl_i=0, allowing synchronization and filtering to settle low. When the READ sequence releases SCL by making scl_oen=1 while filtered SCL sscl=0, continue holding scl_i=0 for several enabled clocks.
elements.expected_response: Requirement-holds side: slave_wait asserts after SCL is released while filtered SCL remains low, stays asserted while sscl remains 0, and the timing counter and command FSM do not advance through the SCL-high phase. slave_wait may clear only after filtered SCL becomes high or SCL is driven low again.
elements.check_method: At every posedge after the scl_oen rising event, compare the slave_wait probe against the reference model condition (scl_oen==1 && sscl==0); verify it is asserted during the hold and that clk_en/FSM phase progression is suppressed until sscl rises or scl_oen falls.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0. Issue a supported READ command (cmd=4'b1000). Keep the external SCL line high with scl_i=1 long enough for the synchronized and filtered SCL value sscl to be high before the READ sequence releases SCL by making scl_oen=1; continue holding scl_i=1.
elements.expected_response: Requirement-does-not-hold side: when scl_oen is released high while filtered SCL is high, slave_wait remains deasserted, and the READ sequence is permitted to progress through the SCL-high phase without a slave-wait stall.
elements.check_method: At the scl_oen rising event and on subsequent enabled clocks, compare slave_wait with the reference model condition (scl_oen==1 && sscl==0); verify the condition is false, slave_wait stays 0, and normal FSM/timing progression occurs.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0. Complete a START command with the bus initially released and high, then issue WRITE with din=0. When the WRITE sequence releases SCL (scl_oen becomes 1), drive the external SCL line low and hold scl_i low long enough for the filtered value sscl to remain 0.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: scl_oen remains 1 while sscl is 0, indicating that another participant is holding SCL low. cmd_ack remains low and the WRITE completion pulse is postponed for the entire released-SCL wait; after scl_i is released and sscl becomes 1, the command proceeds and produces its one-clock cmd_ack pulse.
elements.check_method: Capture a cycle-accurate trace of scl_oen, sscl, slave_wait, clk_en, and cmd_ack. Assert that no WRITE cmd_ack occurs in any cycle with scl_oen=1 and sscl=0, and that cmd_ack occurs only after the filtered SCL-high condition ends the wait, as predicted by a divider/filter/FSM reference model.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0. Complete a START command with the bus initially released and high, then issue WRITE with din=0. During the WRITE released-SCL phase, keep the external SCL line high by driving scl_i high so that filtered sscl reaches 1 without clock stretching.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting ordinary case: when the master releases SCL and sscl is high, the released-SCL phase completes normally and cmd_ack pulses for exactly one clock without the postponement required by the holding case.
elements.check_method: Compare the trace of scl_oen, sscl, slave_wait, clk_en, and cmd_ack with the no-stretch reference model. Verify that cmd_ack follows the released-SCL phase, is exactly one clock wide, and occurs earlier than in the otherwise identical held-low scenario.

elements.stimulus: With the DUT reset and ena=1, issue a supported WRITE command with din=0 and a nonzero clk_cnt while the external bus is initially high. During the command's released-SCL phase, hold scl_i low long enough for filtered SCL to become low and keep it low for multiple expected timing-enable intervals, then release scl_i high.
elements.expected_response: While scl_oen=1 and filtered SCL remains low, slave_wait stays active, the timing counter does not progress, the bit-level command does not advance, and cmd_ack remains low; this is the holding-SCL side of the specified behavior. After scl_i is released and filtered SCL becomes high, timing resumes, the command completes, and cmd_ack asserts for exactly one clock.
elements.check_method: At every posedge after registered outputs settle, monitor scl_oen, filtered SCL/slave_wait probes, and cmd_ack. Compare the held interval against a divider reference model to ensure no counter or FSM phase progress and no cmd_ack pulse; after filtered SCL rises, verify forward progress and exactly one completion pulse.

elements.stimulus: With the DUT reset and ena=1, issue the same supported WRITE command with din=0 and the same clk_cnt, but keep the external bus released high whenever the DUT sets scl_oen=1 so filtered SCL reaches high without clock stretching.
elements.expected_response: This is the contrasting non-holding case: slave_wait does not remain active, the timing counter continues to expire and generate clk_en ticks, the bit-level command advances through its released-high phase, and cmd_ack asserts for exactly one clock when the command completes rather than being postponed by a held-low SCL.
elements.check_method: Use the divider and FSM reference model to predict enabled phase progression. Sample cmd_ack, scl_oen, filtered SCL, and slave_wait after each posedge; verify no sustained slave_wait, expected phase advancement, bounded completion relative to the model, and one one-clock cmd_ack pulse.

elements.stimulus: Do not apply a DUT stimulus; review the numbered list item 4 marker represented by REQ-0056@1.
elements.expected_response: No hardware output, state transition, timing behavior, or interface obligation is required by REQ-0056@1.
elements.check_method: Requirements-audit review confirming that the item has no observable behavior and that no DUT comparison is generated beyond documenting it as non-executable.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, issue a valid READ command with scl_i and sda_i high, and wait until the READ sequence releases SCL (scl_oen=1) and filtered SCL is high. While scl_oen remains high, drive scl_i low and hold it long enough for synchronization and filtering to produce a filtered SCL high-to-low transition.
elements.expected_response: For the falling-edge case described by REQ-0057, scl_sync asserts as a pulse when the filtered SCL falls while scl_oen is high.
elements.check_method: At every posedge clk, compare the scl_sync probe against a reference model of the two-stage SCL synchronizer, filter sampling, majority filtering, delayed filtered SCL, and released-SCL falling-edge detection; require a scl_sync assertion coincident with the modeled filtered falling edge.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, issue a valid READ command with scl_i and sda_i high, and wait until the READ sequence releases SCL (scl_oen=1) and filtered SCL is high. Keep scl_i high for the complete released-SCL observation window so no filtered SCL falling edge occurs.
elements.expected_response: For the no-falling-edge contrast, scl_sync remains deasserted while scl_oen is high; no synchronization pulse is generated.
elements.check_method: Monitor scl_sync on every posedge clk during the released-high window and compare it with the reference model; require scl_sync=0 for all cycles in which the modeled filtered SCL has not fallen while scl_oen is high.

elements.stimulus: With ena=1 and a valid released-high bus, issue a supported WRITE command, wait until the command reaches its released-SCL high phase with scl_oen=1, then have another bus participant hold SCL low long enough for the synchronized and filtered SCL value to make a falling transition.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: scl_oen remains 1 while the filtered SCL fall indicates another master forced SCL low, and the transition to the next SCL timing phase is postponed while the timing interval is reloaded.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after registered outputs settle, monitor scl_oen and compare its transition time against a reference divider/FSM model with SCL synchronization. Confirm scl_oen stays 1 through the externally forced filtered falling edge and does not advance at the nominal enabled timing tick.

elements.stimulus: With ena=1 and a valid released-high bus, issue the same supported WRITE command and wait until the command reaches its released-SCL high phase with scl_oen=1; keep external SCL high so no filtered SCL falling edge occurs.
elements.expected_response: Non-holding case: scl_oen advances to the next command phase at the nominal enabled timing after the released-SCL high interval; no postponement due to clock synchronization occurs.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after registered outputs settle, compare scl_oen transition timing with the reference divider/FSM model for an undisturbed high phase. Confirm the next-phase transition occurs at the nominal enabled timing rather than being delayed.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1 and a nonzero clk_cnt. With the bus released high, issue a supported WRITE command with din=0. During the active WRITE sequence, wait until scl_oen=1 and the filtered SCL is high, then have another master hold scl_i low long enough to produce a filtered SCL falling edge; keep the bus valid afterward so the command can complete.
elements.expected_response: The external falling edge while scl_oen=1 causes synchronization and restarts the low-period timing. The command's cmd_ack pulse is postponed by the restarted low-period timing interval and occurs later than the matched command without this external filtered SCL falling edge.
elements.check_method: Use a timing reference model for the divider and low-period reload. Confirm scl_sync asserts and the timing counter reloads, then compare command-acceptance-to-cmd_ack latency against the paired baseline trace; require exactly one cmd_ack pulse after the additional synchronization delay.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1 and the same clk_cnt and din as TP-0000. With the bus released high, issue the identical supported WRITE command and allow the active sequence to run, but do not introduce any external filtered SCL falling edge while scl_oen=1; keep SCL high whenever the module releases it.
elements.expected_response: The command completes at its normal timing, with cmd_ack occurring without the additional synchronization delay caused by a restarted low-period interval. This is the contrasting no-edge side of the requirement's observed behavior.
elements.check_method: Measure command-acceptance-to-cmd_ack latency and compare it with the divider/filter reference model and TP-0000. Confirm no scl_sync event occurs while scl_oen=1 and that cmd_ack is a single completion pulse at the normal modeled time.

elements.stimulus: In the testbench specification context, mark item 5 as considered, then apply nReset low and release it, set ena high, and drive cmd=0000 (NOP) while keeping the bus released and stable.
elements.expected_response: Because item 5 imposes no hardware requirement, the DUT exhibits only its ordinary reset and NOP behavior: it remains idle, cmd_ack=0, busy=0, al=0, scl_oen=1, sda_oen=1, and scl_o=0 and sda_o=0.
elements.check_method: After reset settles and on each subsequent posedge for the NOP observation window, compare the listed outputs and idle probe against the ordinary reset/NOP reference model; record that no additional item-5-specific transition occurs.

elements.stimulus: In the contrasting testbench specification context, omit item 5 or mark it not considered, then repeat the identical nReset, ena, cmd=0000 (NOP), and released stable-bus stimulus used in TP-0000.
elements.expected_response: The DUT produces the same ordinary reset and NOP behavior as in TP-0000—idle asserted, cmd_ack=0, busy=0, al=0, scl_oen=1, sda_oen=1, and constant-low scl_o and sda_o—with no item-5-related output difference.
elements.check_method: Run TP-0000 and this scenario with identical DUT inputs, compare all listed outputs and idle cycle-by-cycle, and require identical traces; any difference would incorrectly attribute hardware behavior to item 5.

elements.stimulus: After reset, drive scl_i=1 and sda_i=0 and hold both values stable across at least three rising edges of clk while ena=1.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of the synchronization behavior: cscl and csda capture the raw line values through the two-stage synchronizer, with the stable values appearing at the synchronized probes after the specified two clocked capture stages.
elements.check_method: At each posedge clk after registered updates settle, compare cscl and csda against a two-stage reference pipeline fed by scl_i and sda_i; require the expected two-cycle propagation and no unknown or incorrect value.

elements.stimulus: With ena=1, toggle scl_i and sda_i between rising edges of clk, then change them again immediately after the next rising edge and continue applying alternating values on successive clock intervals.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting non-combinational case: cscl and csda do not change immediately with the raw asynchronous inputs; they update only on rising edges of clk and reflect each raw value after propagation through the two-stage synchronization pipeline.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate two-stage reference model and sample cscl/csda both between edges and after edges. Assert that between-edge raw input changes do not alter the probes, and that post-edge probe values match the appropriately delayed sampled input sequence.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=8, drive stable raw scl_i=0 and sda_i=1, then wait through the two-stage synchronization and filter-counter interval until filter_cnt_expired asserts. Continue for multiple expiration events while keeping the synchronized input values stable.
elements.expected_response: On each filter_cnt_expired event while ena=1, newly synchronized SCL and SDA samples are shifted into the fSCL and fSDA histories; fscl and fsda therefore update according to the reference model's three-sample history shift. This is the holding side of shows: the histories shift when the filter-counter expiration window elapses.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model for the two-stage synchronizers, filter-counter interval, and history shift. At every filter_cnt_expired event, compare fscl and fsda against the model and verify that their history positions contain the newly synchronized samples.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set clk_cnt=8 and drive stable raw scl_i=0 and sda_i=1. Keep ena=0 for longer than the modeled filter sampling interval, including clocks on which the filter counter would otherwise expire; then set ena=1 and continue clocking until the first enabled filter-counter expiration.
elements.expected_response: While ena=0, synchronized input samples are not shifted into fSCL or fSDA, even when the disabled interval spans the nominal expiration time; fscl and fsda retain their prior histories. After ena returns high, the histories shift only when the filter counter actually expires on an enabled clock. This is the contrasting side of shows: the histories do not shift when filter progression is disabled or the expiration window has not been reached.
elements.check_method: Record fscl and fsda before each disabled clock and compare them after the clock, asserting no history change throughout ena=0. Then use the reference model to identify the first enabled filter_cnt_expired event and require the shift to occur only on that event.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low and release it, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, then drive scl_i=1 and sda_i=1 continuously for enough rising edges to pass the two-stage synchronizers and cause at least three filter sample updates, including a filter_cnt_expired event for the final history update.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of the majority behavior: after the final filter sample update, the three-sample fSCL and fSDA histories contain high samples and sscl=1 and ssda=1, equal to the majority value of each respective history.
elements.check_method: At each filter_cnt_expired event, compare the observed sscl and ssda against a reference model computing (f[2]&f[1]) | (f[2]&f[0]) | (f[1]&f[0]) from the corresponding post-update three-sample histories; specifically require both outputs to be 1 for the final all-high histories.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low and release it, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, then drive scl_i=0 and sda_i=0 continuously for enough rising edges to pass the two-stage synchronizers and cause at least three filter sample updates, including a filter_cnt_expired event for the final history update.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case of the majority behavior: after the final filter sample update, the three-sample fSCL and fSDA histories contain low samples and sscl=0 and ssda=0, equal to the majority value of each respective history rather than remaining at the reset-high value.
elements.check_method: At each filter_cnt_expired event, compare the observed sscl and ssda against a reference model computing (f[2]&f[1]) | (f[2]&f[0]) | (f[1]&f[0]) from the corresponding post-update three-sample histories; specifically require both outputs to be 0 for the final all-low histories.

elements.stimulus: Assert and release reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=16'h0000, and hold scl_i=1 and sda_i=1 long enough for the synchronized three-sample histories and filtered outputs to become 1. Then drive scl_i low for only one synchronized filter-sample opportunity and return it high, while keeping sda_i high.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of the requirement: sscl remains high throughout the one-sample SCL glitch and ssda remains high; no filtered SCL or SDA transition is produced by the short glitch.
elements.check_method: At every enabled clock, compare sscl and ssda against a reference model that includes two-stage input synchronization, filter sampling, three-sample history shifting, and majority-of-three calculation. Assert that the modeled and observed sscl values remain 1 during and after the one-history-entry low disturbance.

elements.stimulus: Assert and release reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=16'h0000, and hold scl_i=1 and sda_i=1 until the synchronized filter histories and filtered outputs are 1. Then drive scl_i low for two consecutive synchronized filter-sample opportunities and return it high, while keeping sda_i high.
elements.expected_response: Not-holding side of the requirement: because the SCL disturbance affects a majority of the three-sample history, sscl changes to low after the modeled synchronization and filter-sampling latency, then returns high only after high samples again form a majority. ssda remains high.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model for synchronization, sample updates, history contents, and majority filtering. Check that observed sscl changes exactly when the modeled history has at least two low entries and that observed ssda is unchanged.

elements.stimulus: Assert and release reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=16'h0000, and hold scl_i=1 and sda_i=1 long enough for the synchronized three-sample histories and filtered outputs to become 1. Then drive sda_i low for only one synchronized filter-sample opportunity and return it high, while keeping scl_i high.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of the requirement: ssda remains high throughout the one-sample SDA glitch and sscl remains high; no filtered SDA or SCL transition is produced by the short glitch.
elements.check_method: At every enabled clock, compare sscl and ssda against a reference model including synchronizer latency, filter sampling, three-sample history shifting, and majority-of-three calculation. Assert that the modeled and observed ssda values remain 1 during and after the one-history-entry low disturbance.

elements.stimulus: Assert and release reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=16'h0000, and hold scl_i=1 and sda_i=1 until the synchronized filter histories and filtered outputs are 1. Then drive sda_i low for two consecutive synchronized filter-sample opportunities and return it high, while keeping scl_i high.
elements.expected_response: Not-holding side of the requirement: because the SDA disturbance affects a majority of the three-sample history, ssda changes to low after the modeled synchronization and filter-sampling latency, then returns high only after high samples again form a majority. sscl remains high.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model for synchronization, sample updates, history contents, and majority filtering. Check that observed ssda changes exactly when the modeled history has at least two low entries and that observed sscl is unchanged.

elements.stimulus: Review implementation-detail item 6 and trace the DUT specification and implementation for any behavior, port response, state transition, timing rule, or internal obligation attributed solely to that item.
elements.expected_response: No required DUT behavior, output value, state transition, timing constraint, or interface obligation is attributed to item 6.
elements.check_method: Static specification-to-implementation review or lint check confirming item 6 produces no behavioral coverage obligation and has no corresponding behavioral assertions.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low and release it; keep ena=1 and clk_cnt=0. Hold scl_i=1 and sda_i=1 long enough for the synchronizers, filter histories, and delayed values to settle high. Then drive sda_i=0 while holding scl_i=1 for enough enabled clocks to produce a filtered SDA falling edge, and continue holding both inputs.
elements.expected_response: The filtered signals reach sscl=1, dsda=1, and ssda=0; sta_condition is asserted for the clock processing this filtered falling edge. This is the asserting side of the START-detection behavior.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model of the two-stage synchronization, three-sample filtering, delayed filtered SDA, and condition equation (~ssda & dsda & sscl). Compare the modeled sta_condition assertion with the sta_condition probe after each posedge.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low and release it; keep ena=1 and clk_cnt=0. Hold scl_i=0 and sda_i=1 long enough for the synchronized and filtered signals to settle. Then drive sda_i=0 while keeping scl_i=0 for enough enabled clocks to produce a filtered SDA falling edge, and continue holding both inputs.
elements.expected_response: Even when filtered SDA falls with dsda=1, sta_condition remains deasserted because filtered SCL is low (sscl=0). This is the non-asserting side of the START-detection behavior.
elements.check_method: Use the same reference filter and delayed-signal model to verify dsda=1 and ssda=0 while sscl=0, then compare the expected false value of (~ssda & dsda & sscl) against the sta_condition probe on every posedge.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set clk_cnt=0 and ena=1. Drive the bus so filtered SCL is stably high and filtered SDA is stably low, then drive SDA high and hold both SDA and SCL long enough for synchronization and the three-sample majority filter to update, creating a filtered SDA low-to-high transition while filtered SCL remains high.
elements.expected_response: The filtered STOP condition is detected: sto_condition asserts for the filtered SDA rising edge while filtered SCL is high. This is the positive side of the STOP-condition behavior.
elements.check_method: At each enabled clock after the filter update, compare the sto_condition probe against sSCL & sSDA & ~dSDA; require a one-event assertion when ssda rises while sscl is high, with sscl, ssda, and dsda sampled after registered updates settle.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set clk_cnt=0 and ena=1. Drive the bus so filtered SCL is stably low and filtered SDA is stably low, then drive SDA high and hold both SDA and SCL long enough for synchronization and the three-sample majority filter to update, creating a filtered SDA low-to-high transition while filtered SCL remains low.
elements.expected_response: sto_condition remains deasserted because the filtered SCL-high qualification is absent. This is the negative side of the STOP-condition behavior.
elements.check_method: At the filtered SDA rising-edge sample, assert that sscl=0 and sto_condition=0; additionally compare sto_condition against sSCL & sSDA & ~dSDA throughout the transition window.

elements.stimulus: No requirement-specific stimulus; execute the standard reset-and-idle smoke sequence with nReset asserted and released, rst inactive, ena high, and cmd=NOP.
elements.expected_response: No behavior is required by REQ-0068; the test records that this requirement imposes no additional observable constraint on the DUT.
elements.check_method: Vacuity review of the requirement-to-test mapping: confirm the scenario has no REQ-0068-specific output assertion and that no additional interface behavior is inferred from the text.

elements.stimulus: Release both reset inputs, keep the bus idle with scl_i=1 and sda_i=1 until the synchronized three-sample filter is stable, then drive sda_i=0 while holding scl_i=1 for enough enabled clocks to produce a filtered SDA falling edge; afterward keep scl_i=1 and sda_i=0 without generating a STOP.
elements.expected_response: Before the filtered START detection, busy remains low. When filtered SDA falls while filtered SCL is high, sta_condition asserts and busy becomes high on the corresponding registered update. busy remains high for the entire interval after that START while no filtered STOP occurs.
elements.check_method: Use the reference synchronizer/filter model to identify the filtered SDA falling edge and filtered SCL-high interval, then compare busy after each settled posedge: require busy=0 before the modeled START, busy=1 at the modeled START update, and busy=1 on every subsequent sampled clock until a STOP is intentionally driven.

elements.stimulus: First create a filtered START by holding scl_i=1 and transitioning sda_i from 1 to 0 for sufficient filter samples, then maintain the active bus condition. Next, while keeping scl_i=1, drive sda_i=1 for sufficient filter samples to create a filtered SDA rising edge and STOP; afterward keep both lines high.
elements.expected_response: busy is high after the filtered START and remains high before the filtered STOP. When filtered SDA rises while filtered SCL is high, sto_condition asserts and busy becomes low on the corresponding registered update; busy remains low after the filtered STOP.
elements.check_method: Model the synchronized and majority-filtered bus signals to locate the START and STOP edges, then compare the registered busy output after each settled posedge. Require busy=1 throughout the interval from START through the cycle before STOP, and require busy=0 at and after the STOP detection.

elements.stimulus: Apply no stimulus attributable to REQ-0070; leave the DUT inputs and environment under the governing module-level test scenarios.
elements.expected_response: No specific output, state transition, timing behavior, or other observable response is required or attributed to REQ-0070.
elements.check_method: Record the item as vacuously covered and verify that the testbench defines no assertion or scoreboard expectation for REQ-0070.

elements.stimulus: Assert and release reset with ena high, issue cmd=WRITE (0100) with din=1, allow the WRITE sequence to reach the stable high phase where sda_chk=1 and sda_oen=1, then externally hold SDA low long enough for the synchronized and filtered ssda value to become 0.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding case in observed_via.shows: while SDA arbitration checking expects released-high SDA and filtered SDA is low, al asserts high. The command is aborted and no cmd_ack is generated for the aborted command.
elements.check_method: After each clock edge, compare the DUT al output against a reference model that asserts al on the enabled WRITE arbitration-check phase when filtered SDA is 0; verify al transitions high after the filtered-low observation and remains high until reset, and verify no cmd_ack pulse occurs for the aborted command.

elements.stimulus: Assert and release reset with ena high, issue cmd=WRITE (0100) with din=1, allow the WRITE sequence to reach the stable high phase where sda_chk=1 and sda_oen=1, and leave the external SDA line released high so the synchronized and filtered ssda value remains 1 throughout arbitration checking.
elements.expected_response: This is the otherwise side in observed_via.shows: because filtered SDA is not low during the enabled arbitration check, no new assertion of al is caused by this check; al remains low and the WRITE sequence completes normally with its cmd_ack pulse.
elements.check_method: After each clock edge, compare al with a reference model that asserts it only for sda_chk=1 with filtered SDA=0; verify al stays low through the high phase and completion, and verify the normal one-clock cmd_ack pulse occurs.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT with nReset low, release reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, issue a READ command (cmd=1000) from idle, and wait until the READ sequence is active with filtered SCL high and SDA released. Externally drive SDA low long enough to produce filtered SDA low, then release SDA high while filtered SCL remains high so a filtered STOP condition is detected.
elements.expected_response: At the filtered STOP detection edge while the READ command is active, al newly asserts high. The command is aborted and the controller returns to idle with both output enables released; no command-complete pulse is generated for the aborted command.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model for command activity, synchronizer/filter latency, and filtered STOP detection. Sample al after the posedge that processes sto_condition and verify its 0-to-1 transition, then verify the active-command probe clears and both output enables are released.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT with nReset low, release reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, issue a STOP command (cmd=0010) from idle, and allow the STOP sequence to drive SDA low, release SCL high, and release SDA high while SCL is high, producing the filtered STOP condition during the requested STOP command.
elements.expected_response: At the filtered STOP detection edge while the STOP command is active, al does not newly assert high; it remains low. This is the contrasting side of the observed al behavior because the current command is STOP.
elements.check_method: Use the reference model to identify the filtered STOP detection edge and confirm the current command is STOP. Compare al before and after the settled posedge, requiring no 0-to-1 transition and no assertion of al.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep ena high and issue START with cmd=0001, wait for its completion, then issue WRITE with cmd=0100 and din=1. During the WRITE released-SDA high phase, while sda_chk is asserted and scl_oen is released, externally hold SDA low to force arbitration loss.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: al rises; the active command aborts, idle becomes asserted, and both scl_oen and sda_oen become high, releasing SCL and SDA. No command-complete pulse is generated for the aborted WRITE.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after registered outputs settle, monitor al, idle, scl_oen, sda_oen, and cmd_ack. Use a reference model to identify the arbitration-check phase and require al=1 followed by idle=1 with scl_oen=1 and sda_oen=1; require no cmd_ack after the injected loss.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep ena high and issue START with cmd=0001, wait for completion, then issue WRITE with cmd=0100 and din=0. Keep the external SDA and SCL lines high when released, and observe the initial WRITE data-drive low phase before any arbitration-loss condition is introduced.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting non-holding case: because no arbitration is lost, the FSM remains active rather than returning to idle, and during the WRITE data-drive low phase at least one output enable is low (sda_oen=0 for din=0, with SCL driven low as required by the phase). The enables therefore are not both high as the arbitration-loss recovery behavior requires.
elements.check_method: Use the write_sequence and active_command probes plus cycle-accurate sampling after posedges. Confirm no al assertion and no idle transition at this phase, and compare scl_oen/sda_oen against the reference model's active WRITE low phase, requiring that the ordinary active behavior differs from the recovery value scl_oen=sda_oen=1.

elements.stimulus: Review item 9 and the DUT interface/specification; apply arbitrary valid and invalid input sequences without treating any output behavior as required by item 9.
elements.expected_response: No hardware response, state transition, timing property, or interface value is required for compliance with item 9; the verification result for this requirement is recorded as not applicable to simulation.
elements.check_method: Perform a requirements-traceability and manual specification review confirming that item 9 declares no hardware behavior and that no simulation assertion or output comparison is associated with it.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue the READ command while the external bus is released. Drive the slave SDA line to a stable 0, allow filtering to produce filtered SCL low, then release/drive SCL high long enough for a filtered SCL low-to-high transition and filtered_scl_rise assertion.
elements.expected_response: On the registered sampling update associated with filtered_scl_rise, dout updates to 0, equal to the filtered SDA value at the filtered SCL rising edge. This is the holding case of observed_via.shows.
elements.check_method: Use the reference synchronizer/filter model to identify filtered_scl_rise and filtered SDA, then compare dout after the corresponding posedge clk against the modeled filtered SDA value; require exactly one matching update for the edge.

elements.stimulus: After reset, issue a READ command with ena=1, keep the filtered SCL signal low throughout the read sampling interval, and toggle the external SDA line from 0 to 1 while allowing synchronization and filtering to settle, but do not create a filtered SCL low-to-high transition.
elements.expected_response: dout does not capture the changed filtered SDA value while filtered_scl_rise is absent; dout retains its previously registered value. This is the contrasting non-holding case of observed_via.shows.
elements.check_method: Reference-model the synchronized and filtered SCL/SDA histories, assert that no filtered_scl_rise occurs during the SDA change, and compare dout across each posedge clk; require no dout update attributable to that SDA change.

elements.stimulus: With nReset deasserted, ena=1, and a released-high bus, issue cmd=READ (1000). During the READ data-sampling phase, have the external device hold filtered SDA low and provide a stable filtered SCL rising edge, then allow the command to complete.
elements.expected_response: At the registered update following the filtered SCL rising edge, dout presents the received data value 0 for collection by the byte controller; this is the holding side of the observed_via shows condition.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model for synchronization, filtering, and filtered_scl_rise; compare dout after the corresponding posedge with the modeled filtered SDA value and verify the value is captured before cmd_ack.

elements.stimulus: With nReset deasserted, ena=1, and a released-high bus, issue cmd=READ (1000). During the READ data-sampling phase, have the external device hold filtered SDA high and provide a stable filtered SCL rising edge, then allow the command to complete.
elements.expected_response: At the registered update following the filtered SCL rising edge, dout presents the received data value 1 for collection by the byte controller; this is the holding side of the observed_via shows condition.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model for synchronization, filtering, and filtered_scl_rise; compare dout after the corresponding posedge with the modeled filtered SDA value and verify the value is captured before cmd_ack.

elements.stimulus: With nReset deasserted, ena=1, and a released-high bus, issue cmd=READ (1000), then assert nReset asynchronously before any filtered SCL rising edge occurs in the READ data-sampling phase.
elements.expected_response: dout is reset and does not present a received READ data value for collection in the interrupted sampling window; this is the contrasting side of the observed_via shows condition.
elements.check_method: Monitor dout immediately after asynchronous reset assertion and after the next clock edge; compare against the reset reference model and confirm no filtered-sample capture or READ completion occurs before reset.

elements.stimulus: No DUT stimulus; record the presence of the numbered list marker "10." as a specification-scaffolding item.
elements.expected_response: No output, state transition, timing, or protocol behavior is required or constrained by this item.
elements.check_method: Manual or static testplan review confirming that the item has no behavioral assertion and imposes no DUT comparison.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, set ena=1 and a prescaler value that produces multiple enabled-clock cycles between clk_en ticks, keep scl_i and sda_i released high, issue a START command, and after the command is accepted hold cmd at NOP while the START sequence is active. Observe cycles in which the timing counter has not expired and clk_en=0.
elements.expected_response: HOLDING CASE: scl_oen holds its current command-phase value on every active-FSM cycle where clk_en=0; no next-phase scl_oen transition occurs solely because a clock edge occurred.
elements.check_method: At each posedge while active_command=1 and clk_en=0, use a temporal assertion or reference-model comparison that scl_oen at the settled output is equal to its preceding settled value.

elements.stimulus: Using the same reset, released-high bus, ena=1, prescaler, and accepted START sequence, continue driving cmd=NOP until the timing counter expires and clk_en=1 at a command timing-phase boundary where the next START phase changes scl_oen.
elements.expected_response: ADVANCING CASE: on the cycle in which clk_en=1, the command FSM advances to the next START phase and scl_oen changes to that phase's required value, subject to the registered one-clock output latency; the phase must not advance before this clk_en tick.
elements.check_method: Use the internal clk_en probe and a reference FSM model to identify the enabled boundary, then assert that the settled scl_oen transition occurs only on the corresponding enabled FSM update and matches the next START-phase value.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, leave the command FSM idle, set ena=1, provide a released-high bus, drive cmd=4'b0001 (START), and hold it until an idle=1 and clk_en=1 clock edge occurs.
elements.expected_response: On the enabled idle timing tick, the FSM enters the START command sequence; start_sequence becomes active and the START output phase begins.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after nonblocking assignments settle, assert that start_sequence is selected for cmd=0001 on the idle/clk_en tick and that stop_sequence, read_sequence, and write_sequence are not selected. Compare against a command-FSM reference model.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, leave the command FSM idle, set ena=1, arrange the bus for a STOP operation, drive cmd=4'b0010 (STOP), and hold it until an idle=1 and clk_en=1 clock edge occurs.
elements.expected_response: On the enabled idle timing tick, the FSM enters the STOP command sequence; stop_sequence becomes active. This is the holding side of the REQ-0079 observation.
elements.check_method: Sample the command-sequence probes after each posedge and compare the selected sequence with the reference model: stop_sequence must assert for cmd=0010 at the idle/clk_en tick, with the other sequence probes inactive.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, leave the command FSM idle, set ena=1, drive cmd=4'b1000 (READ), provide a released SDA/SCL bus, and hold the command until an idle=1 and clk_en=1 clock edge occurs.
elements.expected_response: On the enabled idle timing tick, the FSM enters the READ command sequence; read_sequence becomes active and SDA is released for the read bit phase.
elements.check_method: At the first idle/clk_en tick with cmd=1000, check that read_sequence is selected and the other command-sequence probes are not selected; compare the sampled trace with the reference model.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, leave the command FSM idle, set ena=1, drive cmd=4'b0100 (WRITE) with din=0, provide a released-high bus, and hold the command until an idle=1 and clk_en=1 clock edge occurs.
elements.expected_response: On the enabled idle timing tick, the FSM enters the WRITE command sequence; write_sequence becomes active and the write phase is selected.
elements.check_method: Sample the sequence probes after the idle/clk_en edge and assert that write_sequence, and only write_sequence, is selected for cmd=0100. Compare command selection and subsequent phase progression to the reference model.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, leave the command FSM idle, set ena=1, drive cmd=4'b0000 (NOP), then repeat with unsupported encodings 4'b0011, 4'b0101, 4'b0110, 4'b0111, 4'b1001, 4'b1010, 4'b1011, 4'b1100, 4'b1101, 4'b1110, and 4'b1111; hold each value through an idle=1 and clk_en=1 clock edge.
elements.expected_response: For each NOP or unsupported command, the FSM does not enter START, STOP, READ, or WRITE; it remains idle and produces no command-sequence selection. This is the contrasting non-holding side of the REQ-0079 observation.
elements.check_method: For every command value, sample idle and all four sequence probes after the enabled tick; assert idle remains active, all sequence probes remain inactive, and no supported sequence is selected. Compare each result with the reference model.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, set ena=1 and clk_cnt to a value producing enabled timing ticks, keep filtered SCL high, and issue cmd=START from idle. Allow the complete START sequence to run until cmd_ack.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: during START, scl_oen and sda_oen are both released initially, sda_oen becomes 0 while scl_oen remains 1 to create SDA-low while SCL-high, and scl_oen then becomes 0 with SDA still driven low. sda_chk remains 0 throughout the START sequence.
elements.check_method: At every posedge after registered outputs settle, use the start_sequence probe and a reference phase model to compare scl_oen, sda_oen, and sda_chk against the expected START phase values until cmd_ack. Check that the sequence reaches idle and produces one ack pulse.

elements.stimulus: Using a START command with a released-high bus, observe both the initial release phase and the subsequent SDA-low/SCL-high phase before allowing the sequence to complete.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: the initial START phase is the shows case for scl_oen=1 and sda_oen=1; in the following SDA-low/SCL-high phase, sda_oen=0 is the shows case and the prior sda_oen=1 value is the otherwise case for that phase. scl_oen remains 1 across these two phases, and sda_chk remains 0.
elements.check_method: Detect the start_sequence phase transition and assert the required one-clock-or-more change of sda_oen from 1 to 0 while scl_oen stays 1; compare each sampled value with the phase-specific reference model rather than only checking the final START outputs.

elements.stimulus: Reset, establish a busy transaction context with the bus released, set ena=1, and issue cmd=STOP from idle. Let the complete STOP sequence execute through cmd_ack.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: STOP first drives SDA low, then releases SCL while SDA remains low, and finally releases SDA while SCL is high. Thus the required phases include sda_oen=0 before the STOP release, scl_oen=1 during the high phase, and sda_oen=1 for the final STOP phase; sda_chk remains 0.
elements.check_method: Use stop_sequence and filtered SCL/SDA probes to align each registered output sample with the STOP reference phases, checking scl_oen, sda_oen, and sda_chk on every enabled FSM advance through the one-cycle cmd_ack.

elements.stimulus: Issue STOP while observing the phase that drives SDA low and the later phase that releases SDA after SCL is released high.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: the SDA-low phase is the shows case for sda_oen=0, while the final STOP phase is the shows case for sda_oen=1 and the otherwise case for retaining the earlier SDA drive. scl_oen is 1 in the final high phase, and sda_chk remains 0.
elements.check_method: Record the stop_sequence phase transitions and compare adjacent output-enable values against the reference model, requiring sda_oen to change from 0 to 1 only after SCL has been released/high; flag a constant or phase-swapped output as failure.

elements.stimulus: Reset, set ena=1, issue cmd=READ from idle, and drive the external SDA line first low and then high on separate filtered SCL rising-edge read windows. Allow the READ sequence to complete.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: READ releases SDA for the slave, releases SCL for the sampling window, then drives SCL low while SDA remains released. Therefore sda_oen=1 throughout, scl_oen=1 during the read high phase and 0 during the low phase, and sda_chk=0 throughout.
elements.check_method: Use read_sequence and filtered_scl_rise probes to identify the read high and low phases; compare registered scl_oen, sda_oen, and sda_chk with the reference model and verify dout captures each filtered SDA value.

elements.stimulus: Issue READ and observe the transition from the released-SCL sampling phase to the following SCL-low phase before cmd_ack.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: during the sampling phase, scl_oen=1 and sda_oen=1 are the shows case; after the filtered SCL rising-edge read window, scl_oen=0 while sda_oen remains 1 is the shows case and the otherwise case for continuing to release SCL. sda_chk remains 0 in both phases.
elements.check_method: Correlate filtered_scl_rise, read_sequence, and the registered output enables; require scl_oen to transition 1-to-0 at the modeled end of the read window while sda_oen stays 1, then compare the phase ordering through ack.

elements.stimulus: Reset, set ena=1, issue cmd=WRITE with din=1, provide a released-high external SDA during arbitration, and allow the complete WRITE sequence to finish.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: WRITE releases SCL for the high phase and releases SDA for din=1, then drives SCL low. During the stable released-high WRITE phase, sda_chk=1; outside that arbitration phase it is 0. The expected output-enable values are scl_oen=1 then 0, sda_oen=1 for din=1, with no arbitration loss.
elements.check_method: Use write_sequence and sda_chk probes to match every output sample to the din=1 WRITE reference phase, requiring sda_chk only during the stable high phase and verifying one cmd_ack with al remaining 0.

elements.stimulus: Issue WRITE with din=1 and observe both the SDA-data phase before SCL release and the stable released-high arbitration phase, then the following SCL-low phase.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: for din=1, sda_oen=1 is the shows case for releasing SDA, while scl_oen=1 and sda_chk=1 are the shows cases in the stable high phase. In the following low phase scl_oen=0 and sda_chk=0 are the shows cases; retaining the high-phase values is the otherwise case. The command completes without al.
elements.check_method: Sample write_sequence, scl_oen, sda_oen, and sda_chk after each posedge and compare phase transitions to the reference model, specifically requiring sda_chk to assert only after SCL is released and deassert when SCL is driven low.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep ena high and the filtered bus released high. Issue cmd=START (4'b0001) while idle, then allow the START sequence to advance through its terminal phase without reset, stretching, or arbitration interruption.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: when the START sequence completes, idle becomes asserted and cmd_ack rises for exactly one clock cycle, then returns low while the FSM remains idle.
elements.check_method: Use a clocked scoreboard/reference model to identify the terminal START phase and compare post-edge idle and cmd_ack. Assert cmd_ack is high on exactly one consecutive sampled clock, is low on the following clock, and that idle is asserted after completion.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep ena high and issue cmd=WRITE (4'b0100) with din=1 while idle. During the released-SDA high phase of the WRITE sequence, externally hold SDA low to force arbitration loss before the normal command terminal phase.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: because the command is aborted before normal completion, cmd_ack does not rise as a completion pulse; the command returns to idle with cmd_ack low rather than producing the one-clock completion pulse.
elements.check_method: Monitor the arbitration-loss/abort event and compare the subsequent clocked cmd_ack waveform against the reference model. Assert no cmd_ack high pulse occurs from the aborted command, including on the first idle clock after the abort.

elements.stimulus: Submit the REQ-0082 text and its source span ('11.') to the requirement-to-testplan traceability review.
elements.expected_response: The review identifies REQ-0082 as a numbered-list marker with no stated requirement and assigns no DUT stimulus or behavioral obligation.
elements.check_method: Static traceability check comparing the requirement text, normalized expectation, and generated testplan classification; pass only if no DUT behavior is attributed to REQ-0082.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, release reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, keep scl_i and sda_i externally released high, then issue cmd=4'b0001 (START) while the FSM is idle and continue clocking until cmd_ack is observed.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding case of the observed difference: the START sequence first has sda_oen=1 and scl_oen=1, then has sda_oen=0 while scl_oen=1 to create SDA low while SCL remains high, then has scl_oen=0, and produces cmd_ack=1 for exactly one clock after SCL is pulled low.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after registered outputs settle, use a temporal assertion or scoreboard to verify the ordered output-enable phases (1,1) -> (1,0) -> (0,0), with the middle phase requiring scl_oen=1 and sda_oen=0, and verify cmd_ack is a single-cycle pulse in the terminal phase.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, release reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, keep scl_i and sda_i externally released high, leave the FSM idle, and apply cmd=4'b0000 (NOP) for multiple enabled clocks without issuing a START command.
elements.expected_response: This is the non-holding case of the observed difference: the START-specific release-then-pull-low sequence does not occur; sda_oen and scl_oen remain at the released idle value 1, and cmd_ack remains 0.
elements.check_method: Monitor sda_oen, scl_oen, and cmd_ack over several enabled clocks and assert that no cycle contains sda_oen=0 or scl_oen=0 and that no cmd_ack pulse is generated.

elements.stimulus: Submit the scaffolding requirement REQ-0084, whose text states that list item 12 has no hardware obligation, to the requirement-to-testplan generation flow.
elements.expected_response: The verification plan classifies REQ-0084 as having no DUT behavior to exercise and produces no hardware stimulus or hardware-output expectation for it.
elements.check_method: Run a requirements-to-testplan audit and compare the generated entry against REQ-0084@1: confirm the requirement is covered by this non-hardware classification check and that no DUT transaction, signal assertion, or behavioral claim is generated.

elements.stimulus: Reset the core, leave the bus externally released with filtered SCL high, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, then issue cmd=4'b0010 (STOP) while idle. Keep rst=0 and nReset=1 and observe outputs after each posedge until cmd_ack is asserted.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: during the STOP sequence, sda_oen first becomes low while scl_oen is still low or before SCL release, then scl_oen becomes high to release SCL, and only afterward sda_oen becomes high while scl_oen is high to release SDA and complete the STOP condition. cmd_ack then pulses high for exactly one clock at the terminal phase and returns low.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-ordered assertion on registered outputs: record the first sda_oen=0 phase, require a subsequent scl_oen=1 phase, require sda_oen=1 only after that phase, and require exactly one cmd_ack=1 cycle after SDA release. Fail if SDA is released before SCL or if acknowledgement is missing or wider than one clock.

elements.stimulus: Reset the core, leave the bus externally released with filtered SCL high, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, keep the FSM idle, and issue cmd=4'b0000 (NOP) for one enabled timing tick. Observe sda_oen, scl_oen, and cmd_ack for several subsequent clocks without issuing a STOP command.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting non-holding case: sda_oen and scl_oen remain in the ordinary released idle state and do not exhibit the STOP ordering of SDA low followed by SCL release and then SDA release. cmd_ack remains low; no STOP sequence is entered.
elements.check_method: Compare the captured waveform against the STOP signature: require no sda_oen low-to-high transition qualified by a preceding STOP phase, no STOP sequencing transition on scl_oen, and no cmd_ack pulse during the observation window.

elements.stimulus: Hold ena=1, provide a released-high bus (scl_i=1 and sda_i=1), apply cmd=0010 (STOP) while the command FSM is idle, and run clk until the STOP sequence drives SDA low, releases SCL high, then releases SDA high.
elements.expected_response: When the accepted STOP sequence reaches its terminal phase with scl_oen=1 and sda_oen=1, cmd_ack asserts for exactly one clock cycle. This is the 'cmd_ack asserts for the STOP command' side of the observed behavior.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model to identify STOP acceptance and its terminal release phase; at the corresponding settled posedge compare cmd_ack against 1 for one cycle and 0 on the following cycle, while checking both output enables are high.

elements.stimulus: Hold ena=1, provide a released-high bus, apply cmd=0010 (STOP), and assert nReset=0 asynchronously before the STOP sequence reaches its terminal phase; release nReset and continue clocking without issuing another command.
elements.expected_response: The STOP sequence is aborted by reset, so no terminal completed STOP phase produces a cmd_ack pulse. This is the contrasting 'cmd_ack does not assert at that terminal STOP phase' side of the observed behavior.
elements.check_method: Monitor the STOP sequence and reset event with a cycle-accurate reference model; verify cmd_ack remains 0 throughout the aborted transaction and after reset until a new valid command is accepted.

elements.stimulus: Apply no DUT stimulus; review the generated verification mapping for REQ-0087.
elements.expected_response: No technical DUT behavior, output expectation, activation condition, or command sequence is required or attributed to REQ-0087.
