elements.check_method: Traceability review: confirm the requirement is represented only as a scaffolding/no-obligation item and has no asserted DUT signal comparison.

elements.stimulus: Hold nReset inactive, rst low, ena high, clk_cnt at 0, and the external SCL line released high. Issue cmd=1000 (READ), then maintain a valid released bus and wait until the READ data-bit phase is entered and before cmd_ack is asserted.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding side of shows: during the READ data-bit phase, sda_oen is high, releasing SDA so the slave can drive the data bit.
elements.check_method: At every settled posedge from READ sequence acceptance through the cycle before cmd_ack, sample sda_oen and assert it remains 1; fail if it is 0 at any point in the READ data-bit phase.

elements.stimulus: Hold nReset inactive, rst low, ena high, clk_cnt at 0, and the external SCL line released high. Issue cmd=0100 (WRITE) with din=0, then maintain a normal bus response until the WRITE data-bit phase is entered and before cmd_ack is asserted.
elements.expected_response: This is the contrasting otherwise side of shows: outside the READ data-bit phase, during the WRITE data-bit drive phase, sda_oen is low and SDA is driven instead of released.
elements.check_method: At the settled posedge that exposes the WRITE data-bit phase, sample sda_oen and compare against 0; also verify the phase is identified by write_sequence before cmd_ack.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=1, keep the bus released and filtered SCL high, issue cmd=READ (1000), and allow the READ sample window to complete normally.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of shows: during the READ sample window scl_oen becomes high and remains high for the sample interval; after the sample window completes, scl_oen becomes low on the subsequent registered FSM phase.
elements.check_method: At every posedge after registered outputs settle, record scl_oen and the READ-sequence probe. Assert that the interval from READ sample-window entry through completion contains no scl_oen=0, and that exactly one transition to scl_oen=0 follows the window.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=1, issue cmd=READ (1000), and externally hold SCL low after the DUT releases it by keeping the external SCL driver low; later release the external driver so filtered SCL rises and the READ sample window can complete.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting timing case: while the READ sample window is extended by the low SCL condition, scl_oen must remain high and must not transition low prematurely. Once the filtered sample window completes after SCL is released high, scl_oen then becomes low.
elements.check_method: Monitor scl_oen, filtered SCL, slave-wait indication, and the READ-sequence probe after each posedge. Assert scl_oen=1 for the entire interval in which the READ sequence is waiting for filtered SCL high, then detect a transition to scl_oen=0 only after the valid filtered sample window completes.

elements.stimulus: With ena high and the bus initially released, issue a READ command and allow the READ sequence to release SDA and SCL. Drive the external SDA line so the filtered SDA value is 1, then produce a stable filtered SCL low-to-high transition and hold the filtered SDA value at 1 through the filtered SCL rising edge.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: when filtered_scl_rise asserts, dout is updated on the following registered observation to the filtered SDA value 1.
elements.check_method: At each filtered_scl_rise probe assertion, sample dout after the posedge nonblocking updates and compare it with the reference model's filtered SDA value at that edge; require dout == 1 for this transaction.

elements.stimulus: During a READ sequence with SCL released, keep the external SCL low so filtered_scl_rise remains deasserted. After establishing dout at a known value from a prior filtered SCL rising edge, change the external SDA and allow filtered SDA to become the opposite value while filtered SCL remains low; do not generate another filtered SCL rising edge.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: because no filtered SCL rising edge occurs, dout is not updated to the changed filtered SDA value and retains its prior registered value.
elements.check_method: Monitor filtered_scl_rise and dout on every posedge; while filtered_scl_rise is 0, compare dout against its previous value and require no change attributable to the filtered SDA transition.

elements.stimulus: Deassert resets, set ena=1 and a valid clk_cnt, issue cmd=1000 (READ) while the external bus is released high, drive a stable SDA read value, and allow the READ sequence to reach a filtered SCL rising edge followed by its normal SCL-low completion phase without stretching, arbitration loss, or reset.
elements.expected_response: After the filtered SCL rising-edge sampling phase, the READ command completes by asserting cmd_ack high for exactly one clock cycle; this is the holding side of the requirement's observed_via shows statement.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model for synchronization, filtering, filtered_scl_rise, and variable command timing; compare the sampled completion event and cmd_ack waveform, requiring exactly one high cycle in the normal READ completion window and no additional pulse.

elements.stimulus: Deassert resets, set ena=1, issue cmd=1000 (READ), provide a stable SDA value, and allow the command to reach and capture the value at a filtered SCL rising edge. Before the normal READ completion acknowledgement is generated, assert rst=1 for a rising clock edge and keep reset asserted through the completion window.
elements.expected_response: The reset aborts the READ command, so cmd_ack does not pulse in the expected READ completion window; this is the non-holding side of the requirement's observed_via shows statement.
elements.check_method: Correlate the filtered SCL rising-edge sampling event with the reset edge using the reference model, then monitor cmd_ack through the post-sampling completion window and assert that it remains low rather than producing a one-clock completion pulse.

elements.stimulus: Provide the complete specification document to the verification artifact checker.
elements.expected_response: The specification contains a list item numbered 14.
elements.check_method: Parse the specification document and assert that a distinct list item with ordinal number 14 is present.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, provide a released-high bus, set cmd=WRITE (0100) and din=0, then clock until the WRITE sequence reaches its released SCL-high phase and completes its following SCL-low transition.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of shows: during the WRITE SCL-high data phase, sda_oen=0, scl_oen=1, and sda_chk=1; on the following low phase scl_oen becomes 0. The sequence continues normally without arbitration loss caused by SDA being low.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after registered outputs settle, use a protocol scoreboard keyed to the write_sequence phase to compare scl_oen, sda_oen, and sda_chk against the expected phase values, and verify al remains 0.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, provide a released-high bus, set cmd=WRITE (0100) and din=1, then clock until the WRITE sequence reaches its released SCL-high phase and completes its following SCL-low transition while the external SDA line remains high.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of shows: during the WRITE SCL-high data phase, sda_oen=1, scl_oen=1, and sda_chk=1; on the following low phase scl_oen becomes 0. With external SDA high, no arbitration loss occurs.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge, compare the observed registered output-enable and arbitration-check signals with the write_sequence reference model; assert sda_oen equals din, scl_oen is released then driven low, sda_chk is asserted only in the high phase, and al remains 0.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue a START command (cmd=START, 0001) on a released-high bus; keep din=1 and observe the command through its SDA-low and subsequent SCL-low phases.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting otherwise case of shows: because the active sequence is START rather than WRITE, sda_oen is controlled by the START protocol and is not selected from din as WRITE data, and sda_chk remains deasserted; no WRITE-specific data-drive/arbitration-check phase is present.
elements.check_method: Use the start_sequence phase reference model to sample scl_oen, sda_oen, and sda_chk after each settled posedge; verify no cycle is classified as write_sequence with sda_chk=1 and no sda_oen value is attributed to WRITE din encoding.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, choose a nonzero clk_cnt, hold the externally resolved SCL and SDA lines high, set din=0, and issue cmd=4'b0100 (WRITE) while idle. Continue supplying enabled clocks and allow the WRITE sequence to complete normally.
elements.expected_response: The WRITE sequence reaches its terminal phase and cmd_ack pulses high for exactly one clock when the WRITE command ends; it is low on the following clock and no arbitration loss occurs.
elements.check_method: A scoreboard tracks acceptance of the WRITE and its terminal low phase, then compares the registered cmd_ack output after each posedge against a one-cycle-high completion pulse. Assert that no additional cmd_ack pulse occurs for the same command.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, choose a nonzero clk_cnt, set din=1, and issue cmd=4'b0100 (WRITE). During the WRITE released-SDA high phase, externally hold SDA low to force arbitration loss before the command reaches its terminal phase.
elements.expected_response: This is the contrasting side of the observed behavior: cmd_ack does not pulse at the WRITE terminal phase because the WRITE is aborted by arbitration loss; al asserts and the command terminates without an acknowledgment.
elements.check_method: Monitor the arbitration-loss indication and command activity, then assert that no cmd_ack high cycle occurs from WRITE acceptance through and after the abort, while al becomes high and both output enables are released.

elements.stimulus: Elaborate the DUT and execute a normal clock/reset sequence without assigning any behavior or stimulus derived from the numbered-list marker "15.".
elements.expected_response: No output behavior is required or attributed to REQ-0095.
elements.check_method: Review the testbench trace and coverage mapping to confirm that this requirement has no associated output assertion beyond its explicit no-requirement expectation.

elements.stimulus: Initialize the DUT with nReset high, rst low, ena high, and clk_cnt nonzero. Drive a valid START command and bus conditions that allow the command FSM to leave idle; after a command phase is active and at a time between clk rising edges, assert nReset low without changing clk.
elements.expected_response: Immediately upon nReset assertion, the reset side of the observed behavior is present: scl_oen=1 and sda_oen=1, cmd_ack=0, al=0, busy=0, idle=1, filter_cnt is reset, fscl and fsda histories are initialized high, and sscl=1 and ssda=1. No command-complete pulse is produced by the reset.
elements.check_method: Use asynchronous event sampling immediately after the nReset transition, before the next clk rising edge, and compare all listed ports and licensed probes against the reset reference model; require the output enables and status signals to change without waiting for clk.

elements.stimulus: First perform normal activity with nReset high so that the DUT is not in its reset-initialized state. Assert rst high while nReset remains high, then provide one rising edge of clk while keeping rst high.
elements.expected_response: On the rising edge applying rst, the reset side of the observed behavior is present: the FSM is idle, scl_oen=1 and sda_oen=1, cmd_ack=0, al=0, busy=0, filter_cnt is reset, fscl and fsda histories are high, and sscl=1 and ssda=1. The reset values are not required before that rising edge solely because rst is high.
elements.check_method: Sample outputs and probes before rst's applying clock edge and immediately after that posedge; compare the post-edge values with the synchronous-reset reference model and verify that reset effects occur on the posedge rather than asynchronously.

elements.stimulus: Keep nReset high and rst low for multiple clk cycles. Issue a valid command with ena high and bus inputs that permit the FSM to advance, and continue clocking without asserting either reset input.
elements.expected_response: The contrasting, non-reset side of the observed behavior is present: the reset operation does not establish scl_oen=1, sda_oen=1, cmd_ack=0, al=0, busy=0, idle=1, reset filter_cnt, or force fscl, fsda, sscl, and ssda high. Instead, the DUT continues its ordinary command/FSM, timing, and filter behavior; any reset-initialized value is only required when nReset is asserted or rst is applied on a rising edge.
elements.check_method: Run the same stimulus against a reference model with both resets inactive, observe the registered outputs and probes on each settled posedge, and check that no reset transition is reported and that at least one non-reset operational state or value is reached.

elements.stimulus: Provide the complete specification document to the testplan checker.
elements.expected_response: The specification contains a section titled exactly "Processing Flow:".
elements.check_method: Run a case-sensitive structural text search or document parser against the specification and require one matching section heading named "Processing Flow:".

elements.stimulus: Set ena=0, cmd=NOP, and rst=0. Assert nReset=0 asynchronously between clk rising edges, then deassert nReset=1 without issuing a command. Separately repeat with nReset=1 and assert rst=1 for one clk rising edge.
elements.expected_response: HOLDING CASE of shows: during asynchronous nReset assertion, scl_oen becomes high without waiting for a clk edge; when rst is asserted, scl_oen is high on the asserting rising edge. This released value demonstrates reset and output-state initialization before normal processing.
elements.check_method: Use a post-NBA waveform check: assert scl_oen==1 immediately after asynchronous nReset assertion, and assert scl_oen==1 on the first rising edge with rst==1. Also check that no command activity or command acknowledgement occurs.

elements.stimulus: Deassert both resets, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, hold scl_i=1 and sda_i=1, and issue cmd=START from idle. Advance clocks until the START sequence enters its active low phase after pulling SDA low, then sample scl_oen while reset remains inactive.
elements.expected_response: CONTRASTING CASE of shows: during an active command low phase with neither reset asserted, scl_oen may be 0, rather than remaining at the reset-initialized released value of 1. The START sequence must otherwise continue toward SCL release/low-phase completion and command acknowledgement.
elements.check_method: Use the idle/start_sequence probes and post-NBA output sampling to identify the active START low phase; assert that scl_oen==0 in that phase and that rst==0 and nReset==1. Confirm the reset-case value was 1 before command processing and compare the two waveform intervals.

elements.stimulus: With nReset high, rst low, ena high, and clk_cnt set to 0, issue a START command and wait until the command sequence drives either scl_oen or sda_oen low. Assert nReset low between two rising edges of clk and hold it low through at least one rising edge.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: nReset assertion asynchronously returns the module to its known idle reset state without waiting for clk. cmd_ack, busy, and al become 0, and scl_oen and sda_oen become 1 (released); these reset values remain present while nReset is low.
elements.check_method: At the asynchronous nReset assertion event, sample all five observed ports before the next clk edge and compare against cmd_ack=0, busy=0, al=0, scl_oen=1, and sda_oen=1. Confirm the same values after the following posedge and record bins for asynchronous reset response and each cleared/released output.

elements.stimulus: With nReset high, rst low, ena high, and clk_cnt set to 0, issue a START command and wait until the command sequence is active and drives either scl_oen or sda_oen low. Assert rst high while nReset remains high, then apply one rising edge of clk and hold rst high for that edge.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: on the rising edge where rst is high, the module returns synchronously to its known idle reset state. After that edge, cmd_ack, busy, and al are 0 and scl_oen and sda_oen are 1 (released).
elements.check_method: Sample outputs immediately after the rst-asserting posedge, allowing nonblocking assignments to settle, and compare against cmd_ack=0, busy=0, al=0, scl_oen=1, and sda_oen=1. Verify that the reset values are not required before that posedge and record the synchronous-reset-on-edge bin.

elements.stimulus: With nReset high and rst low throughout, ena high, and clk_cnt set to 0, issue a START command and observe a command phase after it has begun driving at least one output-enable low. Continue clocking for one or more rising edges without asserting either reset input.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting non-holding case: because neither reset is asserted, the module is not forced to the reset idle port values during the active command. The command sequence continues according to ordinary timing, so at least the currently active drive phase remains observable (for example, an output enable remains low when that phase requires driving the line), rather than both scl_oen and sda_oen being forced high solely by the absence of reset.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model to identify an active START phase and compare post-posedge scl_oen/sda_oen and command progress with reset inactive. Confirm that the outputs are not spuriously changed to the reset tuple (cmd_ack,busy,al,scl_oen,sda_oen)=(0,0,0,1,1) solely between reset assertions; record the ordinary-active-command contrast bin.

elements.stimulus: Start with nReset=1, rst=0, ena=1, and a released-high bus. Drive a valid START or WRITE command and wait until the FSM is active; then assert nReset=0 between two rising edges and hold it active for at least one clock.
elements.expected_response: For the asynchronous reset case, after nReset assertion the command FSM is idle, cmd_ack=0, busy=0, al=0, scl_oen=1, and sda_oen=1. The idle probe is asserted, sda_chk is disabled, and sscl and ssda are high. Any in-progress command is abandoned and both bus lines are released.
elements.check_method: Sample outputs immediately after the asynchronous nReset transition and again after the next settled clock edge; use assertions against the reset-state vector {idle=1, cmd_ack=0, busy=0, al=0, scl_oen=1, sda_oen=1, sda_chk=0, sscl=1, ssda=1}. Confirm no command-complete pulse occurs while reset is active.

elements.stimulus: Keep nReset=1 and drive a valid command with ena=1 until the FSM is active or busy is asserted. Assert rst=1 before a rising edge and keep it high through that rising edge, then observe the DUT after that edge.
elements.expected_response: For the synchronous reset case, on the rst-active rising edge the command FSM returns to idle, cmd_ack=0, busy=0, al=0, scl_oen=1, and sda_oen=1. The idle probe is asserted, sda_chk is disabled, and sscl and ssda are high; the active command does not complete or generate cmd_ack.
elements.check_method: Drive rst relative to clk and sample after nonblocking assignments settle on the asserting posedge. Compare the observed reset-state vector {idle=1, cmd_ack=0, busy=0, al=0, scl_oen=1, sda_oen=1, sda_chk=0, sscl=1, ssda=1}; assert that cmd_ack remains low for the reset transition.

elements.stimulus: Deassert both resets, keep ena=1 and the bus released high, issue a valid START command, and allow the command FSM to advance through its sequence without asserting either reset.
elements.expected_response: Outside the reset assertion window, the DUT performs ordinary command behavior rather than remaining in the reset state: the START sequence changes sda_oen and later scl_oen as required, and exactly one cmd_ack pulse is produced when the sequence completes. Thus the non-reset side of the observed behavior is present: cmd_ack may be high for its completion pulse and the output enables may change from their reset values.
elements.check_method: Use a clocked reference model to identify the START phases and completion. Assert that at least one expected command-phase transition occurs on scl_oen or sda_oen and that cmd_ack is high for exactly one clock at completion, with no reset asserted; distinguish this from the reset-side expectations of cmd_ack=0 and both enables high.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low, release it, keep rst low and ena high, then hold scl_i=1 and sda_i=1 for at least five rising edges of clk. After synchronization has settled, hold both inputs unchanged for another ten rising edges.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of the observed behavior: cscl and csda acquire the corresponding high input values through their synchronization paths after reset and remain high while scl_i and sda_i remain high. No sampling activity is required to produce a difference during the final unchanged interval, so this case provides the post-reset baseline.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after reset deassertion, sample cscl and csda after nonblocking assignments settle and compare them with a reference model of the synchronization pipeline fed by scl_i and sda_i. Check that the settled values remain stable and equal to the modeled sampled values.

elements.stimulus: With nReset=1, rst=0, ena=1, and the synchronization paths settled from a prior scl_i=1, sda_i=1 condition, drive scl_i=0 and sda_i=1 for four rising edges of clk, then drive scl_i=1 and sda_i=0 for four rising edges, continuing to drive each value long enough for the synchronization latency to elapse.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting change side of the observed behavior: cscl and csda must follow the driven scl_i and sda_i transitions through the synchronization paths, with each new value appearing after the modeled capture latency. A design that does not continuously sample after reset would leave cscl/csda at their prior values; instead, the DUT must produce the corresponding low/high and then high/low synchronized updates.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model for the cSCL/cSDA synchronization paths. Compare cscl and csda on every settled posedge against the model, and explicitly check that each input transition is reflected at the expected synchronization stage and that no stale pre-transition value persists beyond the allowed latency.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep ena high and drive scl_i and sda_i to known values. Change both inputs to new, stable values sufficiently before a rising edge of clk, then apply additional distinct stable values before subsequent rising edges.
elements.expected_response: At each rising edge, the first synchronization stage captures the current raw scl_i and sda_i values, and the second stage captures the preceding first-stage values. Each sampled input value therefore appears at cSCL and cSDA after the expected two-stage synchronization latency, with no corruption or cross-channel mixing.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model of two serial capture stages. Sample scl_i and sda_i immediately before each posedge, compare the predicted first- and second-stage values with the cscl and csda probes after NBA settling, and record coverage for multiple 0-to-1 and 1-to-0 transitions on both inputs.

elements.stimulus: With the synchronizer initialized and no rising edge of clk occurring, change scl_i and sda_i several times between two consecutive rising edges; then hold final values through the next rising edge and continue clocking.
elements.expected_response: The contrasting non-capture behavior is observed between clock edges: cscl and csda do not change in response to asynchronous input changes alone. Only the values present at the next rising edge are captured into the synchronization pipeline, and those values propagate to the second stage after the defined two-stage latency.
elements.check_method: Monitor cscl and csda continuously between posedges and assert they remain unchanged despite raw input transitions. At the next and following posedges, compare the probes against a model that samples only on posedge clk and propagates the sampled values through two stages.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low, deassert it between clock edges, keep rst low, then drive scl_i=1 and sda_i=1. After several posedges, change scl_i=0 and sda_i=0 immediately after a posedge and hold both values across subsequent posedges while ena remains high.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: cSCL and cSDA do not change combinationally when the raw inputs change; after the modeled two-stage capture latency, each probe reflects its corresponding held raw input and remains stable while the inputs remain stable. The controller-visible captured values therefore follow the synchronized capture path rather than the raw asynchronous transition.
elements.check_method: At every posedge, compare cSCL and cSDA with a reference model of the two-stage capture registers, and assert that neither probe changes between posedges. Record bins for both captured 0 and captured 1 values and check the expected capture latency.

elements.stimulus: After reset initialization with scl_i=1 and sda_i=1, create a raw asynchronous pulse by changing scl_i and sda_i to 0 immediately after one posedge, hold them low for less than one clock period, and restore both to 1 before the next posedge. Repeat the pulse at offsets around the clock edge.
elements.expected_response: Non-holding case: cSCL and cSDA do not immediately follow the raw pulse and remain at their previously captured values when the pulse is absent at the sampling edge; no capture-stage output changes occur between clock edges. Only raw values presented to the synchronous capture path at the relevant clock edges may propagate after the modeled capture latency.
elements.check_method: Compare cSCL and cSDA cycle-by-cycle with the two-stage synchronizer reference model for each pulse phase, and assert that the probes remain unchanged throughout each between-edge pulse unless the model predicts a sampled value. Check bins for pulses before, at, and after a posedge.

elements.stimulus: After asserting and releasing reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=8. Drive scl_i=1 and sda_i=0 continuously for enough rising clk edges to pass both synchronization stages and at least three filter-sample expirations.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of shows: after the capture and filtering latency, cscl/csda contain the corresponding captured SCL/SDA values and the digital filtering stage produces sscl=1 and ssda=0. The filtered outputs remain at those values while the inputs stay stable.
elements.check_method: At each posedge clk after nonblocking assignments settle, compare the cscl/csda and sscl/ssda probes against a reference model of two-stage capture, filter sampling, and three-sample majority filtering; require sscl=1 and ssda=0 after the modeled filter latency.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=8, establish scl_i=1 and sda_i=1 until the captured and filtered outputs are stable high, then drive scl_i=0 and sda_i=0 only long enough to be captured by the synchronizers but shorter than the filter sampling interval required to establish a majority, and finally restore both inputs high.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case of shows: although cscl/csda may temporarily contain the captured low values, the digital filtering stage rejects the short transient; sscl and ssda remain high and do not show a corresponding filtered low pulse.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model for synchronization and filter sampling. Confirm that the transient appears, if applicable, in cscl/csda but never produces sscl=0 or ssda=0, and check that no filtered transition is observed during or after the injected pulse.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low, release it, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=8, keep scl_i and sda_i stable, then apply enabled rising clock edges while observing filter_cnt and filter_cnt_expired.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: the filter counter derives its sampling interval as clk_cnt >> 2 = 2. After reload, filter_cnt expires at the corresponding two-enabled-clock cadence and reloads according to that interval; it must not use 8 or an unrelated constant as the sampling interval.
elements.check_method: Reference-model the enabled-clock countdown and compare each observed filter_cnt value and filter_cnt_expired event against a model initialized with interval (8 >> 2)=2.

elements.stimulus: Without changing reset or ena, set clk_cnt=12 and continue applying enabled rising clock edges with scl_i and sda_i stable, observing filter_cnt and filter_cnt_expired after the new prescaler value is loaded.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: changing clk_cnt from 8 to 12 changes the derived filter sampling interval from 2 to clk_cnt >> 2 = 3. filter_cnt expiration and reload cadence must follow interval 3, demonstrating that the sampling interval is derived from the shifted clk_cnt value rather than remaining at the prior cadence.
elements.check_method: Compare the observed filter_cnt countdown and filter_cnt_expired spacing with a reference model using interval (12 >> 2)=3, and assert that the cadence differs from the preceding interval-2 observation.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset, deassert it, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=8, then drive stable SCL and SDA levels long enough for the two-stage synchronizers to capture them. Continue enabled clock cycles until the reference filter-counter model predicts filter_cnt_expired=1, and repeat with a changed synchronized SCL/SDA sample on a later expiration.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding case of shows: when filter_cnt_expired is asserted, the newly synchronized SCL and SDA samples are shifted into the fSCL and fSDA three-sample histories. The observed history contents change on each expiration according to the reference model, while samples are not shifted on unrelated enabled clocks.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after nonblocking assignments settle, compare the fscl and fsda probe history contents against a reference model that tracks the two-stage synchronization, the clk_cnt>>2 sampling interval, expiration events, and three-sample shifts. Require the modeled shift exactly on every filter_cnt_expired assertion.

elements.stimulus: After reset with ena=1 and clk_cnt=8, establish an initial synchronized SCL/SDA sample and wait for an expiration to establish the current fSCL and fSDA histories. Change the raw SCL and SDA inputs so the new values have reached the synchronizer, then observe enabled clocks strictly between the next filter-counter expiration events.
elements.expected_response: This is the non-holding case of shows: while filter_cnt_expired is deasserted, the newly synchronized samples are not shifted, so fscl and fsda retain their previous history contents. The histories change only when the subsequent filter-counter expiration is asserted.
elements.check_method: Use the reference filter-counter and synchronizer model to identify enabled clocks with filter_cnt_expired=0. Compare fscl and fsda before and after each such clock and require no change; then verify that the first subsequent expiration produces the predicted history shift.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0 so filtering samples on every enabled clock. Drive scl_i and sda_i through the synchronizer long enough to establish fSCL=110 and fSDA=001, then allow the next filter counter expiration with the synchronized samples unchanged.
elements.expected_response: At the filter update, sscl is 1 because the fSCL history has a two-to-one high majority, and ssda is 0 because the fSDA history has a two-to-one low majority. This is the high-SCL/low-SDA side of the filtered-output distinction.
elements.check_method: At each filter_cnt_expired event, sample the fSCL and fSDA histories and compare sscl and ssda against independent three-sample majority calculations; require sscl==1 and ssda==0 after the registered update.

elements.stimulus: Keep ena=1 and clk_cnt=0. Drive scl_i and sda_i through the synchronizer until the histories are the complementary patterns fSCL=001 and fSDA=110, then allow a filter counter expiration with those synchronized samples unchanged.
elements.expected_response: At the filter update, sscl is 0 because the fSCL history has a two-to-one low majority, and ssda is 1 because the fSDA history has a two-to-one high majority. This is the contrasting low-SCL/high-SDA side, proving the outputs change with the histories.
elements.check_method: At filter_cnt_expired, calculate the majority of each observed three-sample history independently and compare the post-update sscl and ssda values; require sscl==0 and ssda==1.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low and release it; set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0. Drive the external bus with scl_i=1 and sda_i=1 for enough enabled clocks to fill the synchronizer and three-sample filter histories. Then drive both lines stably low for enough filter sampling events to replace the histories, followed by stably high again.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: after synchronization and filter settling, sscl and ssda equal the corresponding stable external bus levels: both become 1, then both become 0, then both return to 1. The filtered signals remain at each value while the corresponding bus level is held stable and are available as the module's stable internal SCL and SDA versions.
elements.check_method: At every filter sample and after the documented synchronizer/filter settling latency, compare sscl and ssda against a reference model that shifts synchronized inputs into three-sample histories and computes their majority values. Assert that no filtered output changes during a stable-line interval.

elements.stimulus: After reset with ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, hold scl_i=1 and sda_i=1 long enough for sscl and ssda to settle high. Inject a raw low pulse on scl_i and independently on sda_i that is shorter than the synchronizer/filter settling interval, then restore each line high and hold it high.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting non-holding case: the short raw glitches must not appear as changes in the stable internal signals; sscl and ssda remain high throughout the injected pulses. No filtered-line transition is produced from either glitch.
elements.check_method: Compare the observed sscl and ssda waveforms with a reference synchronizer/filter model. Assert that each filtered signal remains high and that no filtered transition, START, STOP, or other downstream event is attributed to the short raw glitch.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low asynchronously, release it, set rst low, ena high, and clk_cnt to 0. Keep sda_i high and drive scl_i low continuously until the synchronized/filter reference model observes the filtered SCL transition from 1 to 0; then continue for one additional enabled clock.
elements.expected_response: On the enabled clock where sscl first becomes 0, dscl remains 1, equal to the prior filtered SCL value; on the following enabled clock dscl becomes 0. dsda remains equal to the unchanged filtered SDA value throughout. This is the holding side of the delayed-signal behavior.
elements.check_method: At every posedge after nonblocking assignments settle, compare dscl and dsda against a reference model containing the previous-cycle sscl and ssda values. Record bins for the first filtered SCL transition and verify the one-cycle delayed update exactly.

elements.stimulus: With reset released, ena high, and clk_cnt set to 0, hold scl_i high and drive sda_i low continuously until the synchronized/filter reference model observes the filtered SDA transition from 1 to 0; then continue for one additional enabled clock.
elements.expected_response: On the enabled clock where ssda first becomes 0, dsda remains 1, equal to the prior filtered SDA value; on the following enabled clock dsda becomes 0. dscl remains equal to the unchanged filtered SCL value. This is the holding side of the delayed-signal behavior.
elements.check_method: Compare dscl and dsda after each posedge with the previous-cycle filtered values produced by the synchronizer/filter reference model. Verify that the filtered SDA transition produces exactly one cycle of delayed disagreement before dsda follows ssda.

elements.stimulus: After both filtered lines have reached stable values, hold scl_i and sda_i unchanged for at least four enabled clocks with ena high and clk_cnt equal to 0; then apply no further bus transitions.
elements.expected_response: dscl equals sscl and dsda equals ssda on every sampled clock because there is no current filtered transition to expose the delay. This is the contrasting, non-difference side of shows; a direct-current copy and a delayed version have the same observable port values during a stable interval.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model that updates delayed values from the prior filtered samples, and assert dscl == sscl and dsda == ssda for all stable-interval clocks while separately checking that no filtered transition occurred.

elements.stimulus: Release reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, hold filtered-equivalent SCL and SDA high long enough for synchronization and filtering to settle, then drive sda_i low while keeping scl_i high and hold both levels long enough for the filtered histories to update.
elements.expected_response: When the current filtered SDA becomes low while delayed filtered SDA remains high and filtered SCL is high, sta_condition asserts for the detected START event; this is the holding side of the requirement's shows statement.
elements.check_method: At every enabled clock after filter updates, compare ssda against dsda and sscl, and check that sta_condition is asserted only on the filtered high-to-low SDA transition and is observable for the specified detection cycle.

elements.stimulus: Release reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, establish and hold filtered-equivalent SCL high and SDA high for enough enabled clocks to settle the synchronizer and filter, then continue holding scl_i high and sda_i high without any SDA transition.
elements.expected_response: Because current filtered SDA remains equal to delayed filtered SDA while filtered SCL is high, sta_condition remains deasserted and no START event is detected; this is the contrasting non-holding side of the requirement's shows statement.
elements.check_method: Monitor ssda, dsda, sscl, and sta_condition across multiple filter sample updates; assert that sta_condition is never asserted when ssda equals dsda and no filtered transition occurs.

elements.stimulus: Release reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, establish filtered-equivalent SCL high and SDA low, then drive sda_i high while keeping scl_i high and hold both levels long enough for synchronization and filtering to settle.
elements.expected_response: When the current filtered SDA becomes high while delayed filtered SDA remains low and filtered SCL is high, sto_condition asserts for the detected STOP event; this is the holding side of the requirement's shows statement.
elements.check_method: At each enabled clock after filter updates, compare ssda against dsda and sscl, and check that sto_condition is asserted only on the filtered low-to-high SDA transition with SCL high.

elements.stimulus: Release reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, establish and hold filtered-equivalent SCL high and SDA low for enough enabled clocks to settle the synchronizer and filter, then continue holding scl_i high and sda_i low without any SDA transition.
elements.expected_response: Because current filtered SDA remains equal to delayed filtered SDA while filtered SCL is high, sto_condition remains deasserted and no STOP event is detected; this is the contrasting non-holding side of the requirement's shows statement.
elements.check_method: Monitor ssda, dsda, sscl, and sto_condition across multiple filter sample updates; assert that sto_condition is never asserted when ssda equals dsda and no filtered transition occurs.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0. Drive scl_i=1 and sda_i=1 long enough for the two-stage synchronizer and three-sample filter to establish filtered SCL=1 and filtered SDA=1. Then change sda_i from 1 to 0 while keeping scl_i=1, and hold both levels for enough enabled clocks for the filtered transition to occur.
elements.expected_response: When filtered SDA transitions from high to low while filtered SCL remains high, sta_condition asserts for the START-detection event.
elements.check_method: Use the reference synchronizer/filter model to predict the cycle of the filtered SDA falling edge and verify that the sta_condition probe is asserted on that cycle, with filtered SCL equal to 1; require no assertion before the modeled filtered transition.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0. Drive scl_i=1 and establish filtered SDA=1. Keep sda_i continuously high for multiple filter sampling intervals, then optionally drive a low-to-high or stable-low-to-low SDA condition without producing a filtered high-to-low transition while scl_i remains high.
elements.expected_response: Because filtered SDA does not transition from high to low while filtered SCL is high, sta_condition remains deasserted; no START-detection event is produced.
elements.check_method: Compare sta_condition against the reference filtered-edge model on every enabled clock and assert it is never high in the absence of a modeled filtered SDA falling edge with filtered SCL high.

elements.stimulus: With ena high and the bus filter operating, first drive scl_i high and sda_i low long enough for the synchronized three-sample filter to produce sscl=1 and ssda=0. Then drive sda_i high while keeping scl_i high, and hold both levels long enough for the filtered SDA rising transition ssda=0 to ssda=1 to occur.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: when filtered SDA rises while filtered SCL is high, the STOP condition is detected and sto_condition asserts for the corresponding filtered transition.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model of the two-stage synchronizer, filter sampling, three-sample majority, and delayed filtered SDA. At the modeled ssda rising edge with sscl=1, compare the DUT sto_condition probe against an asserted STOP-detection event.

elements.stimulus: Drive and hold filtered-bus conditions that do not constitute a STOP: establish sscl=0 while changing sda_i from low to high, and separately hold sscl=1 with ssda remaining high or remaining low without a low-to-high transition. Keep each condition stable long enough for the filter to settle.
elements.expected_response: Not-holding case: because filtered SDA does not rise while filtered SCL is high, sto_condition remains deasserted and no STOP-detection event is reported.
elements.check_method: Predict sscl, ssda, and delayed ssda with the reference filter model; for every cycle without the predicate sscl=1 and ssda rising from 0 to 1, assert that the DUT sto_condition probe is low.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset so busy is low, release reset, hold filtered SCL high and filtered SDA high long enough to establish the idle filtered bus, then drive SDA low and hold it stable with SCL high long enough for synchronization and filtering to produce a filtered START condition.
elements.expected_response: At the registered response to the filtered START detection, busy becomes high and remains high while no filtered STOP condition occurs. This is the holding side of the requirement: busy is high after START.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model of the synchronizers, filter majority, and START detector to identify the filtered START event; compare busy sampled after the corresponding posedge against the model and assert it remains high on subsequent clocks absent STOP or reset.

elements.stimulus: First create a busy state by driving a filtered START as in TP-0000. Then, while filtered SCL is high, drive SDA high from low and hold it stable long enough for synchronization and filtering to produce a filtered STOP condition.
elements.expected_response: At the registered response to the filtered STOP detection, busy becomes low and remains low. This is the contrasting clearing side of the requirement: busy is low after STOP.
elements.check_method: Use the filtered-signal reference model to identify the STOP event and compare busy after the corresponding posedge with the expected low value; verify it stays low on later clocks unless a new filtered START is detected.

elements.stimulus: Create a filtered START so busy is high, then apply unrelated bus activity that cannot form START or STOP: toggle SCL while SDA remains stable, and drive SDA transitions only while filtered SCL is low. Hold each level long enough to pass the filter, but do not produce a filtered SDA transition while filtered SCL is high.
elements.expected_response: busy remains high throughout the unrelated activity. This is the non-holding side of the requirement's observation: busy does not change in response to unrelated activity.
elements.check_method: Reference-model the filtered SCL/SDA values and assert that neither sta_condition nor sto_condition occurs during the activity; compare busy after every settled clock against its pre-stimulus high value.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=4. Issue a valid START command, then issue a valid READ command. During the READ released-SCL interval, keep the external SCL line high, provide a stable SDA value, and do not generate any external SCL falling edge.
elements.expected_response: This is the contrasting normal case from the requirement observation: with filtered SCL high and no external SCL falling edge, the READ command progresses on the normal enabled timing and produces its one-clock cmd_ack without an additional stretch or resynchronization delay.
elements.check_method: Use a reference divider/FSM model to predict the normal completion tick. Compare the observed cmd_ack pulse and its cycle against the predicted tick, and verify no slave_wait or scl_sync event occurs during the released interval.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=4. Issue a valid START command followed by a valid READ command. When the READ sequence releases SCL, externally hold SCL low long enough for filtered SCL to remain low across the expected completion tick, then release SCL high and provide a stable SDA value.
elements.expected_response: This is the clock-stretching side of the requirement observation: cmd_ack is postponed while filtered SCL remains low, command progression does not complete on the otherwise expected timing tick, and the command completes with a one-clock cmd_ack only after filtered SCL becomes high.
elements.check_method: Compare cmd_ack against a reference model that holds the timing counter and FSM during slave_wait. Verify cmd_ack is absent at the normal completion tick, slave_wait is asserted while released SCL is filtered low, and cmd_ack occurs only after filtered SCL returns high and the remaining timing phase completes.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=4. Issue a valid START command followed by a valid READ command. During the READ released-SCL high interval, drive an external SCL falling edge while the DUT has SCL released, then keep the shared SCL low for the synchronized low period before allowing it high again.
elements.expected_response: This is the multi-master synchronization side of the requirement observation: cmd_ack is postponed relative to the normal no-fall case, command progression does not complete on the otherwise expected timing tick, and completion occurs only after the external SCL fall has been detected and synchronized low-period timing has completed.
elements.check_method: Compare the observed cmd_ack cycle with a reference model that detects scl_sync, reloads the timing counter, and restarts the low-period timing. Verify cmd_ack is not asserted at the normal completion tick and is asserted for exactly one clock after synchronized timing permits command completion.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1 and clk_cnt to a nonzero value. Issue a supported WRITE command with the bus initially high. During the command's released-SCL phase, drive the external SCL low while scl_oen=1 and hold scl_i low long enough for synchronization and filtering to make filtered SCL low; keep reset inactive.
elements.expected_response: This is the case where the requirement holds: while scl_oen=1 and filtered SCL remains low, slave_wait asserts. The timing counter remains paused and the command phase does not advance until filtered SCL becomes high or SCL is driven low by the controller.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge, use a reference model for the two-stage SCL synchronizer and three-sample majority filter to identify the interval with scl_oen=1 and filtered SCL=0. Assert that slave_wait is high throughout that interval, that cnt does not progress and clk_en is suppressed, and that the FSM does not advance. Record coverage for entry, persistence, and exit of slave_wait.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1 and clk_cnt to the same nonzero value. Issue a supported WRITE command with the bus initially high. During the command's released-SCL phase, leave the external SCL high so that scl_i remains high and the synchronized, filtered SCL remains high while scl_oen=1; keep reset inactive.
elements.expected_response: This is the contrasting case where the requirement does not hold: releasing SCL while filtered SCL is high does not assert slave_wait. The timing counter and command timing continue normally, subject to the configured prescaler, and the command proceeds to its next legal phase.
elements.check_method: Use the synchronizer/filter reference model to identify cycles with scl_oen=1 and filtered SCL=1, then compare the slave_wait probe on every settled posedge. Require slave_wait=0 and verify that cnt/clk_en and FSM phase progress according to the non-stretched timing model.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep ena high and the bus initially high, issue cmd=READ, and hold the external SCL participant low long enough for the synchronized and filtered sscl value to become 0 when the controller releases SCL (scl_oen becomes 1).
elements.expected_response: In the released-SCL phase, scl_oen is 1, sscl is 0, and slave_wait is asserted. This is the 'participant is holding SCL low' side of the observed behavior.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge after synchronization and filtering, compare the released-SCL condition (scl_oen==1 && sscl==0) with the slave_wait probe and require slave_wait==1; also require the condition to persist while the external SCL remains low.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep ena high and the bus initially high, issue cmd=READ, and allow the external participant to release SCL high so that, after synchronization and filtering, sscl becomes 1 when the controller releases SCL (scl_oen becomes 1).
elements.expected_response: In the released-SCL phase, scl_oen is 1, sscl is 1, and slave_wait is deasserted. This is the 'no participant is holding SCL low' side of the observed behavior.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge in the released-SCL phase, compare the condition (scl_oen==1 && sscl==1) with the slave_wait probe and require slave_wait==0; verify the READ sequence can proceed rather than remaining in slave-wait.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, set ena=1 and a nonzero clk_cnt, issue a supported command such as START, and model the bus with SCL initially high. After the command releases SCL (scl_oen becomes 1), externally hold SCL low long enough for filtered SCL to become low and for multiple timing-enable opportunities to occur; then release the external SCL drive so filtered SCL becomes high.
elements.expected_response: While slave_wait is active because scl_oen=1 and filtered SCL is low, scl_oen remains held at 1 and the command's next SCL timing transition is postponed for the entire interval. The bit-level command FSM and timing counter resume only after filtered SCL becomes high; this is the holding side of the observed_via shows clause.
elements.check_method: At every posedge clk during the filtered-SCL-low interval, compare scl_oen against its value at entry to slave_wait and assert that it does not change despite elapsed clk_en opportunities. After filtered SCL becomes high, verify that the next prescribed scl_oen transition and subsequent command progress occur.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, set ena=1 and the same nonzero clk_cnt, issue the same supported command and reach the corresponding phase in which the controller releases SCL (scl_oen becomes 1), but allow the external bus to keep SCL high so filtered SCL remains high and slave_wait is inactive.
elements.expected_response: With slave_wait inactive and filtered SCL high in the same command phase, scl_oen advances to the next prescribed timing value at the normal enabled timing point rather than remaining held at 1; this is the contrasting otherwise side of the observed_via shows clause.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model for clk_en and the command phase, then verify that scl_oen changes to the expected next value at the first eligible timing tick and that the FSM progresses, contrasting it with the held-low case.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and provide a released-high bus. Issue a READ command and wait until the READ high phase is reached with scl_oen=1. While the master continues to release SCL, externally pull scl_i low and hold it low for sufficient clk cycles to pass synchronization and filtering.
elements.expected_response: Holding case for the requirement: after the synchronized and filtered external SCL falling edge, scl_sync asserts, the timing counter reloads from clk_cnt, and local low-period timing restarts in synchronization with the shared bus clock rather than continuing its prior countdown.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model of the two-stage SCL capture, filtering, scl_sync edge detection, and counter reload. At the expected filtered falling-edge cycle, compare the scl_sync probe and verify the counter/reloaded low-period timing and subsequent clk_en schedule against the model.

elements.stimulus: Repeat the same reset, ena=1, READ-command, and released-SCL-high setup, but keep scl_i high throughout the released-SCL high phase; do not apply an external SCL falling edge.
elements.expected_response: Non-holding contrast for the requirement: scl_sync remains deasserted, no synchronization reload is performed due to an external SCL fall, and the local timing counter follows its ordinary enabled countdown and clk_en schedule.
elements.check_method: Compare the scl_sync probe and counter/clk_en trace with the no-fall reference-model trace over the complete high phase. Confirm that no scl_sync pulse or associated counter reload occurs, while ordinary command timing continues.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset low asynchronously, release it, keep rst low and ena high, set clk_cnt to 4, hold scl_i and sda_i high, and issue a START command. After command acceptance, continue supplying clocks and record each successive scl_oen phase transition through completion of the START sequence.
elements.expected_response: Holding case for REQ-0119: scl_oen remains in each command phase until a timing tick generated by cnt, with each phase transition occurring at the interval predicted by a reference counter loaded from clk_cnt=4 and decremented once per enabled clock. No phase transition occurs earlier than the predicted counter expiration, and the START sequence completes in the expected ordered phases.
elements.check_method: At every posedge after settled registered outputs, compare scl_oen transition cycles and phase ordering against a cycle-accurate reference model that reloads cnt from clk_cnt and decrements it on each enabled clock. Bin the measured intervals and assert equality with the model-predicted interval.

elements.stimulus: Run two otherwise identical enabled START-command trials with the bus held released-high: first with clk_cnt=1, then with clk_cnt=8. Apply reset before each trial, issue START, and record the cycles of all successive scl_oen phase transitions.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case for REQ-0119: the scl_oen phase-transition intervals must differ between the clk_cnt=1 and clk_cnt=8 trials as predicted by their respective cnt load-and-decrement schedules; the larger prescale must produce the correspondingly longer interval. A fixed interval independent of clk_cnt, a transition before cnt expires, an incorrect interval, or failure to advance is the non-holding side of the specified shows behavior and must fail the check.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model for each clk_cnt value, measure the interval between corresponding scl_oen transitions, and compare both measured interval sets and their difference against the model. Assert that phase ordering is preserved and that the measured timing is sensitive to the applied prescale.

elements.stimulus: After reset, hold ena high and the external SCL/SDA bus stable and released. Set clk_cnt to 4, issue a supported START command while the FSM is idle, and continue clocking until completion without arbitration loss or clock stretching.
elements.expected_response: The counter-driven timing progression is observed: cmd_ack remains low before the reference-model counter reload/decrement delays have elapsed, then asserts for exactly one clock when the START sequence completes. This is the requirement-holding side of the observed behavior.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model that loads cnt from clk_cnt and decrements it on each enabled clock; compare the predicted command-completion cycle and one-cycle cmd_ack pulse against the DUT after reset and command acceptance.

elements.stimulus: Run otherwise identical supported START commands with ena high, stable released bus inputs, and no stretching or arbitration loss, first with clk_cnt=1 and then with clk_cnt=8.
elements.expected_response: The cmd_ack latency changes according to the two reference-model counter reload/decrement progressions: the clk_cnt=8 run must not produce cmd_ack at the same or an earlier counter-equivalent cycle as the clk_cnt=1 run. The contrasting requirement-not-holding behavior is latency independent of clk_cnt or completion before the programmed counter delays, which shall be reported as a failure.
elements.check_method: Measure command-acceptance-to-cmd_ack latency in both runs and compare each result with the reference model. Verify that the measured latency difference and pulse timing track the change from clk_cnt=1 to clk_cnt=8, rather than being constant or prematurely asserted.

elements.stimulus: After reset, drive ena=1, set clk_cnt=1, keep the filtered bus released-high, and issue a valid START command while continuing to provide posedge clk cycles until the timing counter expires.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: when the timing counter reaches zero, the internal clk_en tick asserts for the expiration event and the command FSM advances or accepts the START command on that enabled timing event; subsequent START sequencing proceeds toward the SDA-low-while-SCL-high phase.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after registered updates settle, compare the observed clk_en probe and idle/start_sequence progression against a reference divider model loaded from clk_cnt=1. Require clk_en=1 on the modeled expiration cycle and require the FSM to advance only on that tick.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set clk_cnt=1, issue a valid START command, then hold ena=0 for multiple posedge clk cycles while the counter would otherwise expire; keep the filtered bus released-high, then reassert ena=1.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: while ena=0, no timing-enable tick is asserted at the would-be expiration events and the command FSM does not accept or advance the START command. After ena returns high, timing progression resumes and clk_en is asserted at the next modeled counter expiration.
elements.check_method: Monitor clk_en and the idle/start_sequence probe on every settled posedge. Compare against a reference model that disables counter progression while ena=0; require clk_en=0 and no FSM progress throughout the disabled interval, followed by a clk_en pulse and corresponding progress after re-enabling.

elements.stimulus: Set clk_cnt to a nonzero prescaler value, hold ena high, keep scl_i and sda_i high, issue cmd=START while the controller is idle, and use the divider reference model to identify an active START timing-phase boundary where the prescribed next phase changes scl_oen. Hold the inputs stable while clk_en remains 0 for at least one enabled clock.
elements.expected_response: This is the no-tick side of the requirement: while the active START sequence is ready for the next timing phase but clk_en=0, scl_oen holds its current phase value and does not change to the next phase value.
elements.check_method: At every posedge after registered outputs settle, correlate the internal clk_en probe with the reference FSM phase. Assert that scl_oen remains unchanged across all active phase-boundary cycles for which clk_en=0, and record a coverage bin for a held phase with no timing-enable tick.

elements.stimulus: Set clk_cnt to a nonzero prescaler value, hold ena high, keep scl_i and sda_i high, issue cmd=START while the controller is idle, and continue the START sequence until the reference divider expires at an active timing-phase boundary where the next phase prescribes a different scl_oen value. Allow the resulting clk_en tick to occur.
elements.expected_response: This is the tick side of the requirement: when clk_en=1 at the active START phase boundary, the FSM advances to the next timing phase and scl_oen changes to the value prescribed for that next phase, observable after the registered-output update.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate divider/FSM scoreboard to predict the next phase. On the posedge producing clk_en=1, compare the settled scl_oen value with the predicted next-phase value and assert that the change occurs only on that permitted tick; record a coverage bin for a phase transition enabled by clk_en.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset, set clk_cnt to a small nonzero value, keep the bus released and free of stretching or arbitration loss, assert ena and issue a valid WRITE command, then during the active WRITE timing phases deassert ena and hold it low for multiple clk_en periods.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding case of the observed behavior: while ena remains low, cmd_ack remains low and does not pulse; normal WRITE bit-level timing does not progress. The timing counter is reloaded on enabled-clock cycles rather than allowing the FSM to advance.
elements.check_method: After each posedge clk, compare cmd_ack and the command-progress timing against a reference divider/FSM model with ena=0; assert that no cmd_ack pulse occurs during the disabled interval and that reasserting ena allows the previously stalled command to resume and eventually complete.

elements.stimulus: Under the same reset, clk_cnt, released-bus, and no-error conditions, assert ena and issue a valid WRITE command, then keep ena high continuously through all WRITE timing phases.
elements.expected_response: This is the contrasting otherwise case of the observed behavior: with ena high, the timing counter expires normally, the WRITE phases progress to completion, and cmd_ack asserts for exactly one clock cycle.
elements.check_method: Use a reference divider/FSM model sampled after each posedge clk to verify clk_en-driven phase advancement and compare the DUT cmd_ack waveform; require one completion pulse and no indefinite stall.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=1, din=1, keep the externally resolved SCL and SDA lines high, and issue cmd=0100 (WRITE). Run until the WRITE sequence reaches its released-SCL stable-high phase.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: during the WRITE operation's arbitration-checking phase, write_sequence=1 and sda_chk=1. sda_chk is not asserted in the other WRITE phases, and the operation subsequently completes with cmd_ack=1 if arbitration is not lost.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-aligned waveform assertion that whenever write_sequence=1 and the WRITE FSM is in its stable released-SCL high phase, sda_chk is high; also check that sda_chk is low before and after that phase and that no arbitration loss occurs with SDA externally high.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=1, keep the externally resolved SCL and SDA lines high, and issue cmd=0001 (START), followed after its acknowledgement by cmd=0010 (STOP). Do not issue a WRITE command.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting non-holding case: sda_chk remains 0 throughout the START and STOP sequences, because arbitration checking is selected for WRITE operations only.
elements.check_method: Compare the cycle-by-cycle sda_chk waveform against the command-sequence probe: assert sda_chk is never high while start_sequence or stop_sequence is active, and record that no WRITE sequence occurs.

elements.stimulus: Release both bus lines high, set ena=1, drive cmd=WRITE (0100) and din=1, then run clk until the WRITE sequence reaches its stable high phase with write_sequence=1 and scl_oen=1; keep filtered SCL high and do not assert reset.
elements.expected_response: Shows the holding case: sda_chk is asserted during the stable high phase of the WRITE bit while SCL is released.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge, use the write_sequence and scl_oen probes to identify the stable high WRITE phase and compare the sampled sda_chk probe against 1; record a coverage bin for that phase.

elements.stimulus: Issue the same enabled WRITE command with din=1 and a released-high bus, advance through the stable high phase, then continue clocks until the WRITE sequence drives SCL low (write_sequence=1 and scl_oen=0), and also sample the pre-high or setup phase.
elements.expected_response: Shows the non-holding case: sda_chk is deasserted outside the stable high phase, including the setup phase and after SCL is driven low.
elements.check_method: Use the write_sequence and scl_oen probes to classify samples outside the stable high phase, then compare sda_chk against 0 at those samples and ensure no assertion persists into the SCL-low phase.

elements.stimulus: After reset with al cleared, set ena=1, issue a WRITE command cmd=0100 with din=1, and hold the external SDA line low long enough for synchronization and filtering to produce ssda=0. Allow the command to reach its released-high arbitration-check phase, where sda_oen=1.
elements.expected_response: At the released-high WRITE arbitration-check phase with sda_oen=1 and filtered SDA ssda=0, al is asserted; this is the asserted side of the requirement's observed_via shows condition. The command is aborted and no completion pulse is generated for the aborted command.
elements.check_method: Use a clocked reference model for command acceptance, synchronization, filtering, and phase timing. At the cycle after the phase processing, compare al against 1 and verify the arbitration-loss transition occurs while sda_oen=1 and ssda=0; also verify the active command terminates.

elements.stimulus: After reset with al cleared, set ena=1, issue a WRITE command cmd=0100 with din=1, and keep the external SDA line released high long enough for synchronization and filtering to produce ssda=1. Allow the command to reach its released-high arbitration-check phase, where sda_oen=1.
elements.expected_response: At the released-high WRITE arbitration-check phase with sda_oen=1 and filtered SDA ssda=1, al is not newly asserted by this condition; this is the non-asserted side of the requirement's observed_via shows condition. The WRITE sequence continues normally rather than aborting for arbitration loss.
elements.check_method: Use a clocked reference model to identify the released-high arbitration-check phase and compare al before and after that phase. Require no 0-to-1 transition on al while ssda=1, and verify the command remains active for its normal subsequent phase.

elements.stimulus: Assert and release reset with al cleared. Set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, issue cmd=READ (1000), and wait until the READ sequence has released SDA and SCL is high. Drive the external bus SDA low, then transition it high while SCL remains high long enough for synchronization and filtering to produce a filtered STOP condition.
elements.expected_response: At the filtered STOP detection edge while the READ command is active, al asserts, the active command is aborted, both scl_oen and sda_oen are released, and no cmd_ack is generated for the aborted READ. This is the holding case of observed_via.shows: al asserts for the unexpected STOP condition.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model for synchronization, filtering, and STOP detection. At the modeled filtered STOP edge, assert that al transitions from 0 to 1 and remains asserted, that the FSM returns to idle, both output enables are 1, and cmd_ack remains 0 for the aborted command.

elements.stimulus: Assert and release reset with al cleared. Set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, issue cmd=STOP (0010), and allow the STOP sequence to drive SDA low, release SCL high, and release SDA high while SCL remains high long enough for the resulting filtered STOP condition to be detected.
elements.expected_response: When the filtered STOP condition occurs while the current active command is STOP, al does not newly assert and remains 0; the STOP sequence completes and produces its normal one-clock cmd_ack. This is the contrasting case of observed_via.shows: al does not newly assert when the current command is STOP.
elements.check_method: Use the reference model to identify the filtered STOP detection edge and verify al is 0 before and after that edge, with no rising transition. Separately verify the expected STOP completion cmd_ack pulse occurs once.

elements.stimulus: Reset the controller, set ena=1 and din=1, issue a WRITE command, and during its stable high phase drive the external SDA line low while the controller has released SDA (sda_oen=1); keep the arbitration-loss condition present through the processing edge.
elements.expected_response: Arbitration loss is processed: the FSM returns to idle, scl_oen becomes high to release SCL, and sda_oen becomes high to release SDA. The command is aborted and no subsequent command phase advances before a new command is accepted. This is the holding side of the observed port behavior: both output enables are high in the arbitration-loss response window.
elements.check_method: At the arbitration-loss processing edge and on following clocks, compare idle, scl_oen, and sda_oen against a reference trace; require idle=1, scl_oen=1, and sda_oen=1, with no command-phase transition or command-complete pulse for the aborted command.

elements.stimulus: Reset the controller, set ena=1 and din=1, issue the same WRITE command with SCL released-high timing, but allow the external SDA line to remain high during the stable high phase so arbitration is not lost; continue supplying normal bus timing until the WRITE completes.
elements.expected_response: The controller does not take the arbitration-loss response: it does not return to idle prematurely and does not force both output enables high as an abort. Instead, the WRITE sequence advances through its remaining phases and completes normally, with its normal command acknowledgment. This is the contrasting side of the observed port behavior: scl_oen or sda_oen may subsequently be driven according to the active WRITE phases rather than remaining released due to arbitration loss.
elements.check_method: Compare the full cycle-by-cycle trace of idle, scl_oen, sda_oen, al, and cmd_ack with the normal WRITE reference model; require continued active-command progression, no arbitration-loss abort, and normal completion, distinguishing it from the forced idle/released outputs required in TP-0000.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue cmd=READ (1000) from idle. Allow the READ sequence to release SDA and SCL, drive the external bus so the filter histories converge to ssda=1, and then provide a filtered SCL rising edge during the READ sample window.
elements.expected_response: At the filtered SCL rising edge during read_sequence, dout is updated to 1, the current filtered SDA value ssda. This is the required holding side of the observed port behavior.
elements.check_method: Use the reference synchronizer/filter model to predict ssda and filtered_scl_rise; sample dout after the triggering posedge and compare it exactly with predicted ssda, with a one-clock registered-output allowance.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue cmd=READ (1000) from idle. During the released SDA read window, arrange for the raw synchronized SDA input to be 1 while the three-sample filter history yields ssda=0 at the next filtered SCL rising edge; hold the filtered SCL high long enough to produce that rising-edge event.
elements.expected_response: At the filtered SCL rising edge during read_sequence, dout is updated to 0, the filtered SDA value ssda, and must not be updated to the raw/unfiltered SDA value 1. The contrasting otherwise side of shows would be dout=1 from unfiltered sampling, which this test must detect and reject.
elements.check_method: Compute ssda and filtered_scl_rise from the reference filter model, then compare the registered dout after the event against ssda and independently assert dout is not the raw SDA value when raw SDA differs from ssda.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and drive scl_i low with sda_i stable low long enough for synchronization and filtering to settle. Then drive scl_i high and hold both inputs stable until the three-sample filter produces a filtered SCL rising edge while filtered SDA is low.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: at the registered sample corresponding to the filtered SCL rising edge, dout updates to 0, the filtered SDA value.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model for the two-stage synchronizers, filter sampling, majority filtering, and filtered SCL edge detection; compare dout after each posedge against the model and record a bin for a filtered SCL rise with filtered SDA=0.

elements.stimulus: First establish dout=0 using a filtered SCL rising edge with filtered SDA low. Keep ena=1 and hold scl_i high so filtered SCL remains high; change sda_i from low to high and hold it long enough for filtered SDA to become high, without driving scl_i low and high again.
elements.expected_response: Non-holding case: because no filtered SCL rising edge occurs after the SDA change, dout does not update due to this requirement and remains 0.
elements.check_method: Use the reference filter model to confirm filtered SDA changes while filtered SCL has no low-to-high transition; assert that dout retains its previous value on every subsequent posedge until the next filtered SCL rising edge, and record a no-rise hold bin.

elements.stimulus: With the bus released and ena high, issue cmd=READ and wait until the READ data-bit phase is active. Drive the filtered SDA value to 0 for one run and 1 for a second run, then provide a filtered SCL rising edge followed by the remaining READ low phase.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: on the registered update caused by the filtered SCL rising edge, dout becomes the sampled filtered SDA bit (0 or 1 respectively) and retains that value for the remainder of the READ data-bit phase until cmd_ack completes the READ command.
elements.check_method: At each filtered_scl_rise, sample dout after the posedge NBA update and compare it with the filtered SDA value presented at that edge. Continue sampling through the READ phase and require dout to remain equal to the captured bit until cmd_ack.

elements.stimulus: With the bus released and ena high, issue cmd=READ and enter the READ data-bit phase, but hold filtered SCL low before its rising edge. Set filtered SDA to the opposite value from the current dout and keep the READ operation active without producing a filtered SCL rising edge.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting non-holding case: before the filtered SCL rising edge captures SDA, dout does not carry the current filtered SDA value as the received READ bit; it remains at its previously registered value. After a subsequent filtered SCL rising edge, dout must change to the sampled SDA bit.
elements.check_method: Monitor dout while the READ phase is active and filtered_scl_rise is absent; require dout to remain unchanged despite the differing filtered SDA value. Then generate filtered_scl_rise and compare the post-edge dout value with filtered SDA.

elements.stimulus: Assert and release reset to initialize the command FSM in idle. Set ena=1, drive cmd=START (0001), choose clk_cnt=3, and hold the valid command while clk_en remains low for the prescaler interval.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of shows: before the first permitted clk_en tick, the command FSM remains in idle and does not begin the START sequence.
elements.check_method: At every posedge before the reference-model clk_en tick, compare the idle probe with the expected value 1 and verify that no START-sequence output transition or cmd_ack occurs.

elements.stimulus: After reset initialization in idle, set ena=1 and drive cmd=START (0001) continuously through the first reference-model clk_en assertion, using clk_cnt=3 and a released-high bus.
elements.expected_response: Non-holding case of shows: when clk_en is asserted for the valid command, the FSM leaves idle and enters the START sequence, observable as start_sequence becoming active and the corresponding SDA/SCL output-enable phase beginning.
elements.check_method: Use the divider reference model to identify the clk_en posedge; verify idle changes from 1 to 0 and start_sequence becomes active on the permitted advancement, with no such transition accepted before that tick.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low, release it, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, keep the filtered bus released/high, then drive cmd=4'b0001 (START) while idle and hold it through the next enabled clk_en tick.
elements.expected_response: The START value is decoded as START: scl_oen remains released during the initial START phase and then follows the START command timing, including the subsequent SCL drive-low phase, rather than remaining in the idle/released condition.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after nonblocking assignments settle, compare scl_oen against a reference command-FSM model and confirm the observed release-to-drive-low START sequence begins at the clk_en decode tick.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low, release it, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, establish an idle released-high bus, then drive cmd=4'b0010 (STOP) while idle and hold it through the next enabled clk_en tick.
