elements.expected_response: The STOP value is decoded as STOP: scl_oen follows the STOP sequence by releasing SCL after the initial phase, instead of remaining in the idle/released condition without a command-specific sequence.
elements.check_method: Sample scl_oen after every posedge and compare its phase transitions with the reference STOP sequence, keyed to the clk_en tick at which cmd is decoded.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low, release it, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, keep SCL externally high and the bus otherwise released, then drive cmd=4'b1000 (READ) while idle and hold it through the next enabled clk_en tick.
elements.expected_response: The READ value is decoded as READ: scl_oen enters the READ timing sequence and releases SCL for the read window, followed by the command's subsequent SCL drive-low phase, rather than staying in the idle condition.
elements.check_method: Use a reference FSM to compare the sampled scl_oen sequence from the decode clk_en tick through the read high window and following low phase.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low, release it, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, keep the bus released/high, then drive cmd=4'b0100 (WRITE) while idle and hold it through the next enabled clk_en tick.
elements.expected_response: The WRITE value is decoded as WRITE: scl_oen follows the WRITE timing sequence, releasing SCL for the write high phase and subsequently driving SCL low, rather than remaining in the idle/released condition.
elements.check_method: Compare scl_oen on each settled clock against a reference WRITE sequence beginning at the clk_en tick that accepts cmd; allow the command's variable completion time but require the expected release-to-low phase ordering.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low, release it, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, establish idle with both lines released, then apply cmd=4'b0000 (NOP) and separately cmd=4'b0011 (unsupported) for at least one enabled clk_en tick each while idle.
elements.expected_response: The NOP and unsupported values select no command sequence: scl_oen remains in the idle/released condition and does not produce START, STOP, READ, or WRITE command-specific signaling. This is the contrasting non-holding side of the requirement's observed_via shows statement.
elements.check_method: For each command value, compare scl_oen over the observation window with the idle reference waveform and assert that no command-specific scl_oen transition occurs at or after the clk_en tick.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, keep ena=1, set clk_cnt=1, hold scl_i=1 and sda_i=1, wait until idle=1 and clk_en=1, then present cmd=4'b0001 (START) for the accepting clock.
elements.expected_response: On the enabled idle decode, the recognized START command enters the START command sequence: start_sequence becomes 1 and idle becomes 0. This is the recognized-command side of the requirement.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after NBA settling, sample idle, start_sequence, stop_sequence, read_sequence, and write_sequence; require start_sequence=1 with idle=0 after the accepting clk_en tick and require the other sequence probes to remain 0.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, keep ena=1, set clk_cnt=1, establish a released-high bus with scl_i=1 and sda_i=1, wait until idle=1 and clk_en=1, then present cmd=4'b0010 (STOP) for the accepting clock.
elements.expected_response: On the enabled idle decode, the recognized STOP command enters the STOP command sequence: stop_sequence becomes 1 and idle becomes 0. This is the recognized-command side of the requirement.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after NBA settling, sample idle, start_sequence, stop_sequence, read_sequence, and write_sequence; require stop_sequence=1 with idle=0 after the accepting clk_en tick and require the other sequence probes to remain 0.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, keep ena=1, set clk_cnt=1, hold scl_i=1 and drive the external SDA line high, wait until idle=1 and clk_en=1, then present cmd=4'b1000 (READ) for the accepting clock.
elements.expected_response: On the enabled idle decode, the recognized READ command enters the READ command sequence: read_sequence becomes 1 and idle becomes 0. This is the recognized-command side of the requirement.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after NBA settling, sample idle, start_sequence, stop_sequence, read_sequence, and write_sequence; require read_sequence=1 with idle=0 after the accepting clk_en tick and require the other sequence probes to remain 0.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, keep ena=1, set clk_cnt=1, hold scl_i=1 and sda_i=1, wait until idle=1 and clk_en=1, set din=1, then present cmd=4'b0100 (WRITE) for the accepting clock.
elements.expected_response: On the enabled idle decode, the recognized WRITE command enters the WRITE command sequence: write_sequence becomes 1 and idle becomes 0. This is the recognized-command side of the requirement.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after NBA settling, sample idle, start_sequence, stop_sequence, read_sequence, and write_sequence; require write_sequence=1 with idle=0 after the accepting clk_en tick and require the other sequence probes to remain 0.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, keep ena=1, set clk_cnt=1, hold scl_i=1 and sda_i=1, wait until idle=1, and on successive enabled decode opportunities present cmd=4'b0000 (NOP) and every unsupported encoding {4'b0011, 4'b0101, 4'b0110, 4'b0111, 4'b1001, 4'b1010, 4'b1011, 4'b1100, 4'b1101, 4'b1110, 4'b1111} for one accepting clock each, returning cmd to NOP between values.
elements.expected_response: For NOP and for every unsupported command value, the FSM remains in idle: idle stays 1 and start_sequence, stop_sequence, read_sequence, and write_sequence stay 0. This is the non-recognized-command side of the requirement.
elements.check_method: At each enabled decode tick and after NBA settling, compare all five FSM probes; require idle=1 and all four command-sequence probes=0 for every tested encoding, with no transition into any sequence.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset, release nReset and rst, set ena=1, clk_cnt=1, hold scl_i=1 and sda_i=1, issue cmd=4'b0001 (START) for an enabled command-acceptance tick, then hold cmd=4'b0000 while allowing the sequence to complete.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of the observed behavior: during the START sequence, scl_oen and sda_oen are initially 1, then sda_oen becomes 0 while scl_oen remains 1, and subsequently scl_oen becomes 0. The FSM returns to idle and cmd_ack is high for exactly one clock cycle at completion, then low.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after registered outputs settle, use a temporal scoreboard to require the ordered output phases (scl_oen,sda_oen)=(1,1), then (1,0), then (0,0), followed by idle=1 and a single-cycle cmd_ack pulse; assert no additional cmd_ack pulse occurs without another accepted command.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset, release nReset and rst, set ena=1, clk_cnt=1, hold scl_i=1 and sda_i=1, issue cmd=4'b0000 (NOP) for multiple enabled ticks, and do not issue a START command.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting side of the observed behavior: the controller remains idle with scl_oen=1 and sda_oen=1; it does not produce the START release-then-SDA-low transition, does not pull SCL low for a START sequence, and does not assert cmd_ack.
elements.check_method: After reset and over the complete observation window, compare the registered outputs against a no-command reference model: require idle=1, require scl_oen=1 and sda_oen=1 on every sampled clock, and assert cmd_ack remains 0 and no START phase ordering occurs.

elements.stimulus: Reset the core, set ena=1, provide a released-high bus, issue cmd=0010 (STOP), and sample sda_oen and scl_oen after every posedge until the STOP sequence releases SCL.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of shows: during the initial STOP-sequence phase, sda_oen is 0 before scl_oen transitions to 1. The STOP sequence then releases SCL by transitioning scl_oen to 1 only after SDA has been driven low.
elements.check_method: Use a temporal assertion that records the first cycle with sda_oen==0 and requires that cycle to precede the first subsequent cycle with scl_oen==1; fail if scl_oen becomes 1 without a prior sda_oen==0 observation.

elements.stimulus: Run the enabled cmd=0010 STOP sequence from reset while monitoring the initial STOP phase; include a negative-ordering monitor that flags any transition of scl_oen to 1 before sda_oen has been 0.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting otherwise side of shows: the forbidden behavior, in which scl_oen transitions to 1 before sda_oen has been 0, must never be observed. Any such ordering is a requirement violation and fails the test.
elements.check_method: Track the ordering of output transitions with a scoreboard or assertion; create a forbidden-ordering coverage bin for scl_oen==1 preceding sda_oen==0 and require that bin to remain empty while the STOP sequence is active.

elements.stimulus: With ena high and the filtered bus initially high, drive cmd=0010 (STOP) while idle. Run clocks until the STOP sequence releases SCL (scl_oen becomes 1), then continue observing until before cmd_ack asserts.
elements.expected_response: During the interval after scl_oen becomes 1 and before cmd_ack, sda_oen is 1, releasing SDA high while SCL is high; this is the required side of the observed_via shows distinction and generates a valid STOP condition.
elements.check_method: Use a clocked waveform assertion that, for each STOP transaction, detects the first registered cycle with scl_oen==1 and requires sda_oen==1 on that cycle and through the high-SCL phase until cmd_ack. Also verify the external open-drain bus resolves SDA high.

elements.stimulus: With ena high and the filtered bus initially high, drive cmd=0010 (STOP) while idle and observe the initial STOP phase immediately after command acceptance, before scl_oen becomes 1.
elements.expected_response: Before SCL is released high, sda_oen remains 0, keeping SDA driven low; this is the contrasting otherwise side of the observed_via shows distinction, and SDA is not released prematurely.
elements.check_method: Use a clocked waveform assertion that, after STOP acceptance and while scl_oen==0 before its first transition to 1, requires sda_oen==0. Check the ordering of sda_oen release relative to scl_oen release.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset=0 and release it, keep rst=0 and ena=1, present cmd=STOP (4'b0010), and keep the externally observed SCL and SDA lines released high. Allow the STOP sequence to advance through driving SDA low, releasing SCL high, and releasing SDA high while SCL is high; continue clocking until command completion.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of the observed port behavior: after the completed STOP condition, scl_oen and sda_oen are high, the FSM probe idle is asserted, and cmd_ack is high for exactly one clock cycle and low on the following clock.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model to identify completion of the STOP release phase, then compare the registered idle and cmd_ack outputs on each subsequent posedge; assert one and only one cmd_ack=1 cycle immediately after completion.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset=0 and release it, keep rst=0 and ena=1, issue cmd=STOP (4'b0010), and allow the sequence to begin. Before the STOP sequence reaches the phase that releases SDA high while SCL is high, assert nReset=0 asynchronously, then release nReset and provide clocks without issuing another command.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting otherwise case of the observed port behavior: because the STOP condition was not completed, cmd_ack does not pulse high for one clock for that aborted STOP command, and the FSM is reset to idle with both output enables released high.
elements.check_method: Monitor the STOP phase probe and verify it never reaches completed STOP before reset; after reset release, compare cmd_ack over the next several clocks against a one-cycle-pulse detector and require no acknowledgement attributable to the aborted command, while checking idle and released output enables.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and provide a released-high bus. Issue cmd=READ (1000) while idle, then keep the external SCL high and allow the command sequence to reach its data-bit/sample window before cmd_ack.
elements.expected_response: During the active READ data-bit/sample window, the READ sequence is active and sda_oen=1. This is the holding side of the observation: SDA is released so the external slave can drive the data bit.
elements.check_method: Use a temporal assertion keyed to the observed READ sequence or read_sequence probe: after READ acceptance and before cmd_ack, whenever the data-bit/sample window is active, sample sda_oen after each posedge and require it to equal 1.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and provide a released-high bus. Issue cmd=WRITE (0100) with din=0 while idle, and allow the command to reach its data-bit high-phase window before cmd_ack.
elements.expected_response: During the WRITE data-bit phase, sda_oen is not 1; it is 0 to drive SDA low for din=0. This is the contrasting side of the observation: the port does not exhibit the READ behavior of releasing SDA because the READ command sequence is not active.
elements.check_method: Use a temporal assertion keyed to the WRITE sequence or write_sequence probe: during the WRITE din=0 data-bit phase before cmd_ack, sample sda_oen after each posedge and require it to equal 0, contrasting it with the READ-window requirement.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, set ena=1 and cmd=READ (1000) while idle, provide a released-high bus, and wait until the READ sequence reaches its read window without ending that window.
elements.expected_response: Positive side of shows: during the active READ read window, scl_oen remains 1, releasing SCL high while the external slave may drive SDA.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge during the read-window interval, use the read_sequence probe and compare registered scl_oen against 1; record a coverage hit for the sustained-high phase.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, set ena=1 and cmd=READ (1000) while idle, provide a released-high bus, wait for the READ sequence to enter its read window, then allow the read-window timing phase to complete and continue through the following low phase.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting end-of-window side of shows: scl_oen is 1 throughout the read window, then transitions to 0 at its end to drive SCL low; it must not remain 1 after the read window.
elements.check_method: Use read_sequence and clk_en/filtered_scl_rise probes to identify the read-window end, then compare the registered scl_oen trace: sustained 1 before the boundary and exactly 0 after the boundary, with the transition ordered after the high phase.

elements.stimulus: With ena high, issue a READ command and model the external bus so SDA is stably low before the filtered SCL rising edge, then allow SCL to transition high long enough for the synchronizer and three-sample filter to produce filtered_scl_rise.
elements.expected_response: On the registered cycle processing filtered_scl_rise, dout captures the actual filtered SDA value of 0; this is the 'dout captures the actual filtered SDA value' side of the requirement.
elements.check_method: Use the reference synchronizer/filter model and filtered_scl_rise probe to identify the qualifying edge, then compare dout after the posedge with the modeled filtered SDA value on that edge.

elements.stimulus: With ena high during a READ sequence, hold filtered SCL low so no filtered SCL rising edge occurs, change the external SDA input from 0 to 1, and keep SCL low or apply only a raw SDA change that does not produce filtered_scl_rise.
elements.expected_response: dout does not update to the filtered SDA value as a consequence of the SDA change; it remains at its prior value until a filtered SCL rising edge occurs. This is the 'dout does not update to the filtered SDA value as a consequence of that filtered SCL rising edge' contrasting side.
elements.check_method: Use the reference filter model to confirm that filtered_scl_rise is absent, and compare dout before and after the SDA change at settled posedges; require no dout update attributable to the change.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue cmd=4'b1000 for READ with the bus released. Allow the READ sequence to release SDA and SCL; drive a stable SDA value, allow filtered SCL to rise, then allow the terminal READ low phase to complete. Wait until the sequence reaches its completion phase.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of the observed cmd_ack behavior: after the filtered SCL rising-edge READ capture and terminal low phase, the FSM is observable in idle and cmd_ack asserts for exactly one clock cycle, then deasserts.
elements.check_method: At each posedge clk after registered outputs settle, use the idle probe and sample cmd_ack. Assert that the completion transition is followed by idle=1 and cmd_ack=1 for one cycle only, with cmd_ack=0 on the adjacent cycles; compare the observed sequence against a READ reference model.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue cmd=4'b1000 for READ with the bus released. During the READ sequence, keep filtered SCL low after the controller releases SCL, preventing the filtered SCL rising edge and terminal READ low phase from completing; observe for multiple enabled timing ticks without completing the READ bit.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting otherwise case of the observed cmd_ack behavior: because the READ bit cycle has not completed, cmd_ack does not pulse high and the FSM does not return to idle prematurely; it remains in the active READ sequence while the filtered SCL remains low.
elements.check_method: Use the idle probe and sample cmd_ack after every posedge clk with registered outputs settled. Assert idle=0 and cmd_ack=0 throughout the induced slave-wait interval, and ensure no one-clock acknowledgement occurs until a later stimulus permits the filtered SCL rising edge and terminal phase to complete.

elements.stimulus: Keep nReset deasserted, rst low, al clear, and ena high. Issue a WRITE command cmd=0100 with din=0 on an otherwise released-high I2C bus, then allow the command to enter its data phase and complete.
elements.expected_response: During the WRITE data phase, sda_oen is 0, which is the din=0 side of the specified behavior and drives SDA low; the output remains phase-correct through the released-SCL high phase and the command eventually asserts cmd_ack.
elements.check_method: At each clock after registered outputs settle, use the WRITE sequence probe or phase reference model to identify the data phase and compare sda_oen against din; require sda_oen==0 whenever din==0 and confirm the single completion pulse.

elements.stimulus: Keep nReset deasserted, rst low, al clear, and ena high. Issue a WRITE command cmd=0100 with din=1 on an otherwise released-high I2C bus, then allow the command to enter its data phase and complete.
elements.expected_response: During the WRITE data phase, sda_oen is 1, which is the din=1 side of the specified behavior and releases SDA high; the output remains phase-correct through the released-SCL high phase and the command eventually asserts cmd_ack.
elements.check_method: At each clock after registered outputs settle, use the WRITE sequence probe or phase reference model to identify the data phase and compare sda_oen against din; require sda_oen==1 whenever din==1 and confirm the single completion pulse.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, provide a released-high bus, set din=0, and issue cmd=WRITE (0100). Allow the WRITE sequence to reach its SDA setup and released-SCL high phase without arbitration loss or reset.
elements.expected_response: During the WRITE data-bit phase, including SDA setup and the released-SCL high phase before cmd_ack, sda_oen is 0. This is the din=0 side of the required behavior: SDA is driven low.
elements.check_method: At every settled posedge while write_sequence is active and before cmd_ack, compare sda_oen against the reference model expectation 0; require the value to remain 0 through the data-bit high phase and verify cmd_ack terminates the sequence.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, provide a released-high bus, set din=1, and issue cmd=WRITE (0100). Allow the WRITE sequence to reach its SDA setup and released-SCL high phase without arbitration loss or reset.
elements.expected_response: During the WRITE data-bit phase, including SDA setup and the released-SCL high phase before cmd_ack, sda_oen is 1. This is the contrasting din=1 side of the required behavior: SDA is released high, opposite to the din=0 case.
elements.check_method: At every settled posedge while write_sequence is active and before cmd_ack, compare sda_oen against the reference model expectation 1; require the value to remain 1 through the data-bit high phase and verify cmd_ack terminates the sequence.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep ena=1, clk_cnt=0, and the filtered bus released high. From idle, issue cmd=4 (WRITE) with din=1 and hold the external SDA and SCL lines high so arbitration succeeds. Run clocks until the WRITE command completes.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of observed_via.shows: during the WRITE stable-high phase, sda_chk is asserted and scl_oen=1, then scl_oen becomes 0 for the following SCL-low phase; the FSM returns to idle and cmd_ack is high for exactly one clock.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after registered outputs settle, use a scoreboard to find the WRITE sequence and assert the ordered transitions sda_chk=1 with scl_oen=1, then scl_oen=0, followed by idle=1 and a single-cycle cmd_ack pulse. Assert cmd_ack is low on the adjacent clocks.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep ena=1, clk_cnt=0, and the filtered SCL line high. From idle, issue cmd=4 (WRITE) with din=1. When the WRITE phase releases SCL and enables arbitration checking, externally hold SDA low to force arbitration loss, then run clocks through the abort.
elements.expected_response: Non-holding side of observed_via.shows: the required WRITE completion progression is not present; after arbitration loss the active command aborts, the FSM returns to idle, both output enables are released, and cmd_ack remains low rather than producing the normal completion pulse.
elements.check_method: Monitor the filtered arbitration condition and registered outputs after each posedge. Confirm al asserts, no cmd_ack pulse occurs from the aborted WRITE, idle becomes 1, and scl_oen and sda_oen are released; classify the absence of the normal scl_oen=1-then-0 completion sequence and acknowledgement as the contrasting observed behavior.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, hold the external SCL and SDA lines released high, and issue START (cmd=0001) from idle. Wait for the START sequence to reach its phase that pulls SDA low and then pulls SCL low.
elements.expected_response: This is the actively-pulled-low side of the requirement: scl_o and sda_o remain constant 0, scl_oen=0 whenever SCL is driven low, and sda_oen=0 whenever SDA is driven low.
elements.check_method: At every settled posedge from command acceptance through cmd_ack, assert scl_o==0 and sda_o==0; correlate each output-enable value with the START sequence phase and assert enable 0 for every driven-low line.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, hold the external SCL and SDA lines released high, and issue START (cmd=0001) from idle. Observe the initial START phase before SDA is pulled low, when both bus lines are released.
elements.expected_response: This is the released-line side of the requirement: scl_o and sda_o remain constant 0, while scl_oen=1 and sda_oen=1 select released SCL and SDA lines.
elements.check_method: Sample outputs after each posedge and assert scl_o==0 and sda_o==0; during the START release phase assert scl_oen==1 and sda_oen==1 and verify the external lines remain high when not externally driven low.

elements.stimulus: First issue START with ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, then after its completion issue STOP (cmd=0010) while busy. Hold the external bus released high and observe the STOP phase that begins with SDA driven low.
elements.expected_response: This is the actively-pulled-low side of the requirement: scl_o and sda_o stay constant 0, sda_oen=0 while STOP drives SDA low, and scl_oen reflects 0 whenever the STOP sequence drives SCL low.
elements.check_method: Use a waveform assertion over the active STOP sequence: scl_o==0 and sda_o==0 on every settled posedge, with sda_oen==0 during the SDA-low phase and scl_oen==0 in any SCL-low phase.

elements.stimulus: First issue START with ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, then issue STOP (cmd=0010). During STOP, observe the phase after SCL is released high and the final phase after SDA is released high.
elements.expected_response: This is the released-line side of the requirement: scl_o and sda_o remain constant 0; scl_oen=1 when STOP releases SCL high and sda_oen=1 when STOP releases SDA high.
elements.check_method: After each posedge, compare output enables with the STOP phase reference model and assert the corresponding enable is 1 for every released line while both constant drive outputs remain 0.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, issue READ (cmd=1000) from idle with the external slave returning a valid bit. Wait through the read window until the controller pulls SCL low after the filtered SCL rising edge.
elements.expected_response: This is the actively-pulled-low side of the requirement: scl_o and sda_o remain constant 0, scl_oen=0 during the post-read SCL-low phase, and sda_oen=0 whenever the READ sequence actively pulls SDA low.
elements.check_method: Trace read_sequence through cmd_ack, assert scl_o==0 and sda_o==0 at every settled posedge, and check each output-enable against the reference phase: 0 for every actively driven-low line.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, issue READ (cmd=1000) from idle, and have the external slave hold SDA at either 0 or 1 during the read sample window while SCL is released high.
elements.expected_response: This is the released-line side of the requirement: during the read window scl_o and sda_o remain constant 0, scl_oen=1 releases SCL, and sda_oen=1 releases SDA for the slave to drive.
elements.check_method: At the read-window posedges, assert both output drives are 0 and both output enables are 1; independently verify the sampled bus value is determined by the external SDA level rather than a DUT-driven high value.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, issue WRITE (cmd=0100) with din=0, and hold the external bus released high. Observe the WRITE data phase and the subsequent SCL-low phase.
elements.expected_response: This is the actively-pulled-low side of the requirement: scl_o and sda_o remain constant 0; sda_oen=0 for the din=0 data phase, and scl_oen=0 when the WRITE sequence pulls SCL low.
elements.check_method: Sample after every posedge in write_sequence and assert constant-low drive outputs; compare scl_oen and sda_oen to the phase model and require enable 0 for each line that is actively pulled low.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, issue WRITE (cmd=0100) with din=1, and hold the external bus released high. Observe the data high phase while SDA is released and SCL is released for arbitration.
elements.expected_response: This is the released-line side of the requirement: scl_o and sda_o remain constant 0, sda_oen=1 for din=1, and scl_oen=1 during the released SCL high phase.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge in the WRITE released-high phase, assert scl_o==0 and sda_o==0 and require scl_oen==1 and sda_oen==1; verify the external SDA line can determine the arbitration sample.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, keep the externally resolved SCL and SDA lines high, issue cmd=START, and run until the START sequence reaches the phase that pulls SDA low while SCL remains released.
elements.expected_response: At the START pull-down phase, scl_o=0 and sda_o=0, scl_oen=1 indicates SCL is released, and sda_oen=0 indicates SDA is actively pulled low. This is the active-low selection side of the requirement.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge, assert scl_o==0 and sda_o==0. During the identified START phase, compare scl_oen and sda_oen against the reference open-drain model and require scl_oen==1 and sda_oen==0.

elements.stimulus: Complete a transaction so busy is set, then issue cmd=STOP with ena=1 and clk_cnt=0 while the external bus is released high; run until the STOP sequence has released SDA after releasing SCL.
elements.expected_response: In the final STOP phase, scl_o=0 and sda_o=0, scl_oen=1 and sda_oen=1 indicate that both SCL and SDA are released. This is the release side contrasting with the active-low pull-down case.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge, assert scl_o==0 and sda_o==0. During the final STOP release phase, compare both output enables with the open-drain line model and require scl_oen==1 and sda_oen==1; flag any enable value that does not select the stated release behavior.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, keep the externally resolved SCL and SDA lines high, issue cmd=START, and run until the START sequence reaches the phase that pulls SCL low.
elements.expected_response: Holding case for SCL: scl_oen becomes 0 during the START sequence's SCL-low phase, and the resolved SCL line is low. scl_o remains 0 as the constant open-drain drive value.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge, compare the registered scl_oen and constant scl_o against the reference command-sequence model; when the modeled SCL-low phase is active, require scl_oen==0 and resolved_scl==0.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, keep the externally resolved SCL line high, issue cmd=READ, and run through the read high-phase window while the external device releases SDA high.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case for SCL: during the READ high-phase window, scl_oen remains 1, so the DUT does not drive SCL low; the resolved SCL line is high. scl_o remains 0 because it is constant, independent of the released state.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge in the modeled READ high phase, require scl_oen==1 and resolved_scl==1, while also checking scl_o==0; flag any low output-enable assertion in this phase.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, keep the externally resolved bus high, issue cmd=STOP, and run until the STOP sequence reaches its initial phase that drives SDA low.
elements.expected_response: Holding case for SDA: sda_oen becomes 0 during the STOP sequence's SDA-low phase, and the resolved SDA line is low. sda_o remains 0 as the constant open-drain drive value.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge, compare the registered sda_oen and constant sda_o against the reference STOP sequence; when the modeled SDA-low phase is active, require sda_oen==0 and resolved_sda==0.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, keep the externally resolved bus high, issue cmd=READ, and run through the read data-bit window with the external device releasing SDA high.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case for SDA: during the READ data-bit window, sda_oen remains 1, so the DUT does not drive SDA low; the resolved SDA line is high. sda_o remains 0 because it is constant, independent of the released state.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge in the modeled READ data-bit window, require sda_oen==1 and resolved_sda==1, while also checking sda_o==0; flag any low output-enable assertion in this phase.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low asynchronously, then deassert it with ena high and an external bus model that drives neither SCL nor SDA low. Before accepting a command, sample the reset-initialized scl_oen and sda_oen values and the resulting bus lines.
elements.expected_response: For the holding case where scl_oen=1 and sda_oen=1, the corresponding SCL and SDA lines are released and rise high through the external pull-up resistor.
elements.check_method: After reset settles, assert that scl_oen==1 and sda_oen==1 and that the wired open-drain bus model resolves SCL==1 and SDA==1 when the external participant is released.

elements.stimulus: With nReset deasserted, ena high, clk_cnt=0, and the external bus released high, issue a START command and advance through its phases; then continue until the controller drives SCL low. Observe each registered output-enable phase and resolve the bus with no external low drive.
elements.expected_response: For the contrasting case where scl_oen=0 or sda_oen=0, the corresponding line is actively pulled low rather than released: SDA is low during the START condition and SCL is low after the START high phase.
elements.check_method: At each settled clock edge, compare scl_oen and sda_oen against the wired open-drain bus model: assert SDA==0 whenever sda_oen==0, SCL==0 whenever scl_oen==0, and verify that these low results are not attributed to the external pull-up.

elements.stimulus: Assert reset, release it, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=1, hold scl_i and sda_i high, issue cmd=4'b0001 (START), and continue clocking until the START sequence reaches its terminal phase.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of REQ-0150: at completion, cmd_ack rises on one registered clk cycle, remains high for exactly that one cycle, and is low on the following cycle.
elements.check_method: At every posedge after command acceptance, compare cmd_ack against a reference START-sequence model; assert one high sample at terminal completion and low samples on the immediately preceding and following cycles.

elements.stimulus: Assert reset, release it, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=1, establish a busy bus with scl_i and sda_i high, issue cmd=4'b0010 (STOP), and continue clocking until the STOP sequence reaches its terminal phase.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of REQ-0150: at completion, cmd_ack rises for exactly one clk cycle and is deasserted on the next clk cycle.
elements.check_method: Use a STOP timing reference model to identify terminal completion, then sample the registered cmd_ack after each posedge and verify a single-cycle pulse with no adjacent high cycle.

elements.stimulus: Assert reset, release it, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=1, hold the external bus released high, issue cmd=4'b1000 (READ), drive the returned SDA bit and SCL high for the read window, then allow the READ sequence to reach its terminal phase.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of REQ-0150: after the READ low phase completes, cmd_ack is asserted on exactly one clk cycle and returns low on the next cycle.
elements.check_method: Predict READ terminal completion from filtered SCL timing and command state, then compare the observed registered cmd_ack waveform against one and only one high cycle at that completion.

elements.stimulus: Assert reset, release it, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=1, hold the bus released high, set din=1, issue cmd=4'b0100 (WRITE), allow the released SCL high phase to complete without arbitration loss, and continue until the WRITE sequence reaches its terminal phase.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of REQ-0150: at the end of the WRITE sequence, cmd_ack is high for exactly one clk cycle, with no second consecutive high cycle.
elements.check_method: Track the WRITE sequence and terminal phase with a reference model; assert that cmd_ack has one rising assertion at completion, one-cycle width, and is low before and after the pulse.

elements.stimulus: For each of START, STOP, READ, and WRITE, issue the supported command with ena=1 and drive a normal bus response; monitor cmd_ack continuously from command acceptance through several clocks after the sequence completes.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case of REQ-0150: cmd_ack is absent before the terminal phase and absent after the one completion cycle; it must not remain high for multiple clocks or appear at a nonterminal phase. Any absence at terminal completion or any pulse of duration other than one clk cycle is a failure.
elements.check_method: Use a command-sequence reference model to classify pre-terminal, terminal, and post-terminal cycles, then assert cmd_ack=0 in all pre- and post-terminal cycles and exactly one high sample in the terminal completion cycle for each command.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep ena high and provide a released-high bus. Issue cmd=START and maintain normal SCL/SDA conditions until the START sequence reaches its terminal phase; then issue a second supported command only after observing the completion indication.
elements.expected_response: For the holding case in REQ-0151, cmd_ack is asserted high for exactly one clock on the completion edge of the accepted START operation, then returns low. The subsequent command is accepted only after that pulse.
elements.check_method: At every posedge after registered outputs settle, compare cmd_ack against a reference FSM that identifies the START terminal phase. Assert exactly one high cycle, no adjacent high cycle, and verify the next command is not required to overlap the pulse.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep ena high and issue cmd=START on a released-high bus. When the controller releases SCL for the high phase, externally hold SCL low to cause clock stretching and maintain it low for multiple enabled timing ticks, so the START operation remains incomplete.
elements.expected_response: For the non-holding case in REQ-0151, cmd_ack does not pulse while the bit-level operation is incomplete and the controller remains waiting for SCL to become high. No completion indication is emitted until the stretch is released and the operation actually reaches its terminal phase.
elements.check_method: Monitor cmd_ack on every settled posedge while filtered SCL remains low and the command has not reached its terminal phase; require cmd_ack=0 throughout the wait interval, then separately confirm any later pulse occurs only after completion.
